docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯದೇವೇಹ ತದಮುತ್ರ ಯದಮುತ್ರ ತದನ್ವಿಹ । ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯುಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಯ ಇಹ ನಾನೇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ ॥ ೧೦ ॥   Whatever is here, that indeed is there; and whatever is there, that indeed is here. He who sees even the slightest plurality here goes from death to death.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯತ್ ಏವ ಇಹ

Whatever indeed is here

  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಇಹ → here

ತತ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ

That is there

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there

ಯತ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ

Whatever is there

  • ಯತ್ → whatever
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there

ತತ್ ಅನು ಇಹ

That again is here

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅನು → likewise, correspondingly
  • ಇಹ → here

ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಸಃ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ

He goes from death to death

  • ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ → from death
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ → death
  • ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ → attains

ಯಃ ಇಹ ನಾನಾ ಇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ

Who sees plurality as though real here

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಇಹ → here
  • ನಾನಾ → multiplicity, diversity
  • ಇವ → as though
  • ಪಶ್ಯತಿ → sees

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಯದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ ತತ್ತದುಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾದಬ್ರಹ್ಮವದವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ ಸಂಸಾರ್ಯನ್ಯತ್ಪರಸ್ಮಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ ಇತಿ ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ಕಸ್ಯಚಿದಾಶಂಕೇತೀದಮಾಹ — ಯದೇವೇಹ ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣೋಪಾಧಿಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವದವಭಾಸಮಾನಮವಿವೇಕಿನಾಮ್ , ತದೇವ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಸ್ಥಮ್ ಅಮುತ್ರ ನಿತ್ಯವಿಜ್ಞಾನಘನಸ್ವಭಾವಂ ಸರ್ವಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವರ್ಜಿತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ । ಯಚ್ಚ ಅಮುತ್ರ ಅಮುಷ್ಮಿನ್ನಾತ್ಮನಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಮ್ , ತದನು ಇಹ ತದೇವ ಇಹ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣನಾಮರೂಪೋಪಾಧಿಮ್ ಅನು ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ ನಾನ್ಯತ್ । ತತ್ರೈವಂ ಸತಿ ಉಪಾಧಿಸ್ವಭಾವಭೇದದೃಷ್ಟಿಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಮೋಹಿತಃ ಸನ್ ಯ ಇಹ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ್ಯನಾನಾಭೂತೇ ಪರಸ್ಮಾದನ್ಯೋಽಹಂ ಮತ್ತೋಽನ್ಯತ್ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೇತಿ ನಾನೇವ ಭಿನ್ನಮಿವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ ಉಪಲಭತೇ, ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯೋರ್ಮರಣಾತ್ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಮರಣಂ ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ ಜನನಮರಣಭಾವಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯತೇ । ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತಥಾ ನ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ । ವಿಜ್ಞಾನೈಕರಸಂ ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣಾಕಾಶವತ್ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೈವಾಹಮಸ್ಮೀತಿ ಪಶ್ಯೇದಿತಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಾರ್ಥಃ ॥   Lest anyone entertain the doubt that the Self appearing in all beings—from Brahmā down to the smallest stationary object—is something different from the Supreme Brahman because it appears conditioned and subject to saṃsāra, the Upaniṣad declares this mantra.  That which appears here to the undiscriminating as associated with causes, effects, and limiting adjuncts, and therefore as possessing the characteristics of worldly existence, is itself the very Brahman that exists in its own nature, there (in reality), as pure consciousness, eternal, homogeneous knowledge, and free from all attributes of saṃsāra.  And that which exists there in the Self is precisely what appears here through the adjuncts of body, senses, names, and forms. It is not something different.  When this is so, a person deluded by ignorance, characterized by perceiving differences arising from limiting adjuncts, imagines:  "I am different from Brahman; Brahman is something other than me."  Seeing plurality as though it were real, he repeatedly attains death—that is, repeated birth and death.  Therefore one should not see in that manner.  Rather, one should realize:  "I am Brahman alone—of the nature of pure consciousness, continuous, and all-pervading like space."  This is the meaning of the passage.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿ ಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ

That which exists in all beings from Brahmā down to the immobile

  • ಯತ್ → that which
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾದಿ → beginning with Brahmā
  • ಸ್ಥಾವರಾಂತೇಷು → ending with stationary beings
  • ವರ್ತಮಾನಂ → existing

ತತ್ ತತ್ ಉಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾತ್

Because of various limiting adjuncts

  • ತತ್ ತತ್ → various
  • ಉಪಾಧಿತ್ವಾತ್ → due to conditioning adjuncts

ಅಬ್ರಹ್ಮವತ್ ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ

Appearing as though non-Brahman

  • ಅಬ್ರಹ್ಮವತ್ → as though not Brahman
  • ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ → appearing

ಸಂಸಾರಿ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ

Something different from the Supreme Brahman and subject to saṃsāra

  • ಸಂಸಾರಿ → worldly, transmigrating
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → different
  • ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ → from Supreme Brahman

ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ ಕಸ್ಯಚಿತ್ ಆಶಂಕಾ

Lest anyone have such a doubt

  • ಮಾ ಭೂತ್ → let there not be
  • ಕಸ್ಯಚಿತ್ → for anyone
  • ಆಶಂಕಾ → doubt

ಯತ್ ಏವ ಇಹ

That which is here

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಏವ → indeed
  • ಇಹ → here

ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣೋಪಾಧಿ ಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ

Associated with cause-and-effect adjuncts

  • ಕಾರ್ಯ → effect
  • ಕಾರಣ → cause
  • ಉಪಾಧಿ → limiting adjunct
  • ಸಮನ್ವಿತಂ → associated with

ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವತ್ ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ

Appearing as though possessed of worldly attributes

  • ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವತ್ → as if having saṃsāric qualities
  • ಅವಭಾಸಮಾನಂ → appearing

ಅವಿವೇಕಿನಾಂ

To the undiscriminating

  • ಅವಿವೇಕಿನಾಂ → of those lacking discrimination

ತತ್ ಏವ ಅಮುತ್ರ

That very same is there

  • ತತ್ ಏವ → that very same
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there (in reality)

ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಸ್ಥಂ

Established in its own nature

  • ಸ್ವ → own
  • ಆತ್ಮಸ್ಥಂ → abiding in itself

ನಿತ್ಯ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಘನ ಸ್ವಭಾವಂ

Of the nature of eternal homogeneous consciousness

  • ನಿತ್ಯ → eternal
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ → consciousness
  • ಘನ → solid mass, homogeneous
  • ಸ್ವಭಾವಂ → nature

ಸರ್ವಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮವರ್ಜಿತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

Brahman free from all worldly attributes

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ಸಂಸಾರಧರ್ಮ → attributes of saṃsāra
  • ವರ್ಜಿತಂ → devoid of
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman

ಯತ್ ಚ ಅಮುತ್ರ ಅಮುಷ್ಮಿನ್ ಆತ್ಮನಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಂ

That which exists there in the Self

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಚ → and
  • ಅಮುತ್ರ → there
  • ಆತ್ಮನಿ → in the Self
  • ಸ್ಥಿತಂ → established

ತತ್ ಅನು ಇಹ

That very same is here

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅನು → likewise
  • ಇಹ → here

ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣನಾಮರೂಪೋಪಾಧಿಂ ಅನು ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ

Appearing through the adjuncts of body, senses, names, and forms

  • ಕಾರ್ಯ → body, effect
  • ಕರಣ → senses
  • ನಾಮ → name
  • ರೂಪ → form
  • ಉಪಾಧಿಂ → limiting adjunct
  • ಅನು → through
  • ವಿಭಾವ್ಯಮಾನಂ → appearing

ನ ಅನ್ಯತ್

Not different

  • ನ → not
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → other

ಉಪಾಧಿ ಸ್ವಭಾವ ಭೇದ ದೃಷ್ಟಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ

Through ignorance characterized by seeing differences due to adjuncts

  • ಉಪಾಧಿ → adjunct
  • ಸ್ವಭಾವ → nature
  • ಭೇದ → difference
  • ದೃಷ್ಟಿ → perception
  • ಲಕ್ಷಣಯಾ → characterized by
  • ಅವಿದ್ಯಯಾ → by ignorance

ಮೋಹಿತಃ ಸನ್

Being deluded

  • ಮೋಹಿತಃ → deluded
  • ಸನ್ → being

ಅನ್ಯಃ ಅಹಂ

"I am different"

  • ಅನ್ಯಃ → different
  • ಅಹಂ → I

ಮತ್ತಃ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

"Brahman is different from me"

  • ಮತ್ತಃ → from me
  • ಅನ್ಯತ್ → different
  • ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Supreme Brahman

ನಾನಾ ಇವ ಭಿನ್ನಂ ಇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ

Sees plurality as though real

  • ನಾನಾ → many
  • ಇವ → as though
  • ಭಿನ್ನಂ → separate
  • ಪಶ್ಯತಿ → sees

ಸ ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ

He goes from death to death

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಮೃತ್ಯೋಃ → from death
  • ಮೃತ್ಯುಂ → death
  • ಆಪ್ನೋತಿ → attains

ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ ಜನನಮರಣಭಾವಂ

Repeated birth and death

  • ಪುನಃ ಪುನಃ → again and again
  • ಜನನ → birth
  • ಮರಣ → death
  • ಭಾವಂ → condition

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತಥಾ ನ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್

Therefore one should not see thus

  • ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ → therefore
  • ತಥಾ → in that manner
  • ನ → not
  • ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ → should see

ವಿಜ್ಞಾನೈಕರಸಂ

Of the nature of pure undivided consciousness

  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾನ → consciousness
  • ಏಕರಸಂ → homogeneous

ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣ

Without interruption

  • ನೈರಂತರ್ಯೇಣ → continuously

ಆಕಾಶವತ್ ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ

All-pervading like space

  • ಆಕಾಶವತ್ → like space
  • ಪರಿಪೂರ್ಣಂ → completely full, all-pervading

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಏವ ಅಹಂ ಅಸ್ಮಿ

"I am Brahman alone"

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಏವ → alone
  • ಅಹಂ → I
  • ಅಸ್ಮಿ → am

ಇತಿ ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್

Thus should one realize

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಪಶ್ಯೇತ್ → should see, realize

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ ವೇದ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಜೀವಮಂತಿಕಾತ್ । ಈಶಾನಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ನ ತತೋ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೫ ॥   He who knows this Self as the enjoyer of the fruits of actions, as the living principle dwelling near (in the body), and as the Lord of the past and the future, does not seek to protect himself from anything thereafter. Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯಃ ಇಮಂ ವೇದ

Who knows this

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಇಮಂ → this
  • ವೇದ → knows

ಮಧ್ವದಂ

The enjoyer of the fruits of actions

  • ಮಧು → sweetness, pleasant result
  • ಅದಂ → eater, enjoyer
  • ಮಧ್ವದಂ → enjoyer of the fruits (of karma)

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ

As the Self

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self

ಜೀವಂ ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್

As the living principle dwelling near

  • ಜೀವಂ → the living being, life-principle
  • ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ → near, dwelling within the body

ಈಶಾನಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ

The Lord of the past and the future

  • ಈಶಾನಂ → ruler, lord
  • ಭೂತಸ್ಯ → of the past
  • ಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ → of the future

ನ ತತಃ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ

Thereafter he does not seek protection

  • ನ → not
  • ತತಃ → thereafter
  • ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ → seeks to protect himself, shrinks away in fear

ಏತತ್ ವೈ ತತ್

Verily, this is That

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ → That (Brahman taught earlier)

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ ಕರ್ಮಫಲಭುಜಂ ಜೀವಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೇದ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ ಅಂತಿಕೇ ಸಮೀಪೇ ಈಶಾನಮ್ ಈಶಿತಾರಂ ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ, ತತಃ ತದ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾದೂರ್ಧ್ವಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ನ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ ನ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛತಿ, ಅಭಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ । ಯಾವದ್ಧಿ ಭಯಮಧ್ಯಸ್ಥೋಽನಿತ್ಯಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಮನ್ಯತೇ ತಾವದ್ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಾನಮ್ । ಯದಾ ತು ನಿತ್ಯಮದ್ವೈತಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ, ತದಾ ಕಃ ಕಿಂ ಕುತೋ ವಾ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಮಿಚ್ಛೇತ್ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತದಿತಿ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ॥   Further, whoever knows this Self as the enjoyer of the fruits of actions, as the living principle, as the sustainer of the aggregate of prāṇas and senses, as dwelling nearby in the body, and as the ruler of the past, present, and future — after gaining this knowledge, such a person no longer seeks to protect himself, for he has attained fearlessness.  So long as a person remains subject to fear and regards the Self as impermanent, he seeks to protect himself. But when he realizes the Self as eternal and non-dual, then who would protect whom, from what, and for what reason?  “Verily, this is That” — as explained before.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಕಿಂಚ

Further

  • ಕಿಂಚ → moreover, further

ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ ಇಮಂ ಮಧ್ವದಂ

Whoever knows this enjoyer of the fruits of action

  • ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ → whoever
  • ಇಮಂ → this
  • ಮಧ್ವದಂ → enjoyer of the fruits of karma

ಕರ್ಮಫಲಭುಜಂ ಜೀವಂ

The jīva who experiences the fruits of actions

  • ಕರ್ಮ → action
  • ಫಲ → fruit, result
  • ಭುಜಂ → enjoyer
  • ಜೀವಂ → living being

ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಂ

The sustainer of the aggregate of prāṇas and senses

  • ಪ್ರಾಣಾದಿ → prāṇa and the rest
  • ಕಲಾಪಸ್ಯ → aggregate, collection
  • ಧಾರಯಿತಾರಂ → supporter, sustainer

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೇದ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ

Knows and realizes as the Self

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ವೇದ → knows
  • ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ → realizes

ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ ಅಂತಿಕೇ ಸಮೀಪೇ

As dwelling nearby, within the body

  • ಅಂತಿಕಾತ್ → near
  • ಅಂತಿಕೇ → in proximity
  • ಸಮೀಪೇ → nearby

ಈಶಾನಂ ಈಶಿತಾರಂ

As the ruler and controller

  • ಈಶಾನಂ → ruler
  • ಈಶಿತಾರಂ → controller

ಭೂತಭವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ

Of the three divisions of time

  • ಭೂತ → past
  • ಭವ್ಯ → future
  • ಕಾಲತ್ರಯಸ್ಯ → of the threefold time (past, present, future)

ತತಃ ತದ್ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ

After realizing That

  • ತತಃ → thereafter
  • ತತ್-ವಿಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ → from the knowledge of That
  • ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ → afterwards

ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ನ ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ

He does not seek to protect himself

  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → himself
  • ನ → not
  • ವಿಜುಗುಪ್ಸತೇ → seeks to protect, guard

ನ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ ಇಚ್ಛತಿ

Nor does he desire preservation

  • ನ → not
  • ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ → to protect, preserve
  • ಇಚ್ಛತಿ → desires

ಅಭಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್

Because he has attained fearlessness

  • ಅಭಯ → fearlessness
  • ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ → because of having attained

ಯಾವತ್ ಹಿ ಭಯಮಧ್ಯಸ್ಥಃ

So long as one remains in fear

  • ಯಾವತ್ → so long as
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಭಯ-ಮಧ್ಯಸ್ಥಃ → situated amidst fear

ಅನಿತ್ಯಂ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಮನ್ಯತೇ

He considers the Self to be impermanent

  • ಅನಿತ್ಯಂ → impermanent
  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ಮನ್ಯತೇ → thinks

ತಾವತ್ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ ಇಚ್ಛತಿ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ

So long he seeks to protect himself

  • ತಾವತ್ → so long
  • ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ → to protect
  • ಇಚ್ಛತಿ → desires
  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → himself

ಯದಾ ತು ನಿತ್ಯಂ ಅದ್ವೈತಂ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ

But when he realizes the Self as eternal and non-dual

  • ಯದಾ → when
  • ತು → however
  • ನಿತ್ಯಂ → eternal
  • ಅದ್ವೈತಂ → non-dual
  • ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ → the Self
  • ವಿಜಾನಾತಿ → realizes

ತದಾ ಕಃ ಕಿಂ ಕುತೋ ವಾ ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ ಇಚ್ಛೇತ್

Then who would protect what, and from whom?

  • ತದಾ → then
  • ಕಃ → who
  • ಕಿಂ → what
  • ಕುತಃ → from whom, from what
  • ವಾ → indeed
  • ಗೋಪಾಯಿತುಂ → to protect
  • ಇಚ್ಛೇತ್ → would desire

ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್

Verily, this is That

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ → That (Brahman)

ಇತಿ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್

As explained before

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ → as before

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸೋ ಜಾತಮದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಮಜಾಯತ । ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಯೋ ಭೂತೇಭಿರ್ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೬ ॥   He who sees That which was born from tapas in the beginning, which came into being before the waters, and which, having entered the cave of the heart, abides there together with the elements—he indeed realizes That. Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯಃ

Who

  • ಯಃ → who

ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸಃ ಜಾತಂ

Born from tapas in the beginning

  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → in the beginning
  • ತಪಸಃ → from tapas
  • ಜಾತಂ → born, arisen

ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ಅಜಾಯತ

Born before the waters

  • ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ → before/from the waters
  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → before
  • ಅಜಾಯತ → was born

ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ

Having entered the cave (of the heart), abiding there

  • ಗುಹಾಂ → the cave, the heart
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ → having entered
  • ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ → abiding, remaining

ಯಃ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ

Who sees (That) in association with the elements

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ → with the elements, among created beings
  • ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ → sees clearly, realizes

ಏತತ್ ವೈ ತತ್

Verily, this is That

  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ → That (Brahman)

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಯಃ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಗಾತ್ಮೇಶ್ವರಭಾವೇನ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟಃ, ಸ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮೇತ್ಯೇತದ್ದರ್ಶಯತಿ — ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿನ್ಮುಮುಕ್ಷುಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ತಪಸಃ ಜ್ಞಾನಾದಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ ಇತ್ಯೇತತ್ ; ಜಾತಮ್ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಂ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಮ್ । ಕಿಮಪೇಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಪೂರ್ವಮಿತಿ, ಆಹ — ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಮ್ ಅಪ್ಸಹಿತೇಭ್ಯಃ ಪಂಚಭೂತೇಭ್ಯಃ, ನ ಕೇವಲಾಭ್ಯೋಽದ್ಭ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ । ಅಜಾಯತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಃ ಯಸ್ತಂ ಪ್ರಥಮಜಂ ದೇವಾದಿಶರೀರಾಣ್ಯುತ್ಪಾದ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿಗುಹಾಂ ಹೃದಯಾಕಾಶಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನುಪಲಭಮಾನಂ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಭೂತೈಃ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣಲಕ್ಷಣೈಃ ಸಹ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ ಯೋ ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ ಯಃ ಪಶ್ಯತೀತ್ಯೇತತ್ ; ಯ ಏವಂ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ, ಸ ಏತದೇವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ — ಯತ್ತತ್ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ॥   The Self that was previously described as the inner ruler (Pratyagātman and Īśvara) is now shown to be the Self of all.  Whoever is a seeker of liberation and realizes Hiraṇyagarbha, the first-born, who arose from Brahman characterized by tapas, knowledge, and the like, and who was born before the waters—that is, before the five elements beginning with water—such a person truly sees.  Having first produced the bodies of the gods and other beings, that Hiraṇyagarbha entered the heart-space, the cave of all living beings, and remains there, experiencing sound and other sense objects, together with the body, senses, and mind.  Whoever sees Him in this manner truly sees. Such a person sees none other than the Brahman that is the subject under discussion in this section.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯಃ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಗಾತ್ಮ ಈಶ್ವರಭಾವೇನ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟಃ

The Self previously taught as the inner ruler

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಪ್ರತ್ಯಗಾತ್ಮ → the inner Self
  • ಈಶ್ವರ-ಭಾವೇನ → in the form of the Lord
  • ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟಃ → indicated, taught

ಸಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಇತಿ ಏತತ್ ದರ್ಶಯತಿ

He is the Self of all—this is what is shown

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ → the Self of all
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ದರ್ಶಯತಿ → shows

ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ ಮುಮುಕ್ಷುಃ

Any seeker of liberation

  • ಯಃ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ → whoever
  • ಮುಮುಕ್ಷುಃ → seeker of liberation

ಪೂರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ

The first-born

  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → first
  • ಪ್ರಥಮಂ → foremost

ತಪಸಃ ಜ್ಞಾನಾದಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ

From Brahman characterized by knowledge and tapas

  • ತಪಸಃ → from tapas
  • ಜ್ಞಾನಾದಿ-ಲಕ್ಷಣಾತ್ → characterized by knowledge and the like
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ → from Brahman

ಜಾತಂ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಂ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಂ

The arisen Hiraṇyagarbha

  • ಜಾತಂ → born
  • ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಂ → arisen
  • ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಂ → Hiraṇyagarbha

ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ ಪೂರ್ವಂ

Before the waters

  • ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ → before the waters
  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → prior to

ಅಪ್ಸಹಿತೇಭ್ಯಃ ಪಂಚಭೂತೇಭ್ಯಃ

Before the five elements beginning with water

  • ಅಪ್-ಸಹಿತೇಭ್ಯಃ → together with water
  • ಪಂಚಭೂತೇಭ್ಯಃ → the five elements

ನ ಕೇವಲಾಭ್ಯಃ ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ

Not merely before water alone

  • ನ → not
  • ಕೇವಲ → merely
  • ಅದ್ಭ್ಯಃ → before water

ಪ್ರಥಮಜಂ

The first-born

  • ಪ್ರಥಮ → first
  • ಜಂ → born

ದೇವಾದಿ ಶರೀರಾಣಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದ್ಯ

Having created the bodies of gods and others

  • ದೇವಾದಿ → gods and others
  • ಶರೀರಾಣಿ → bodies
  • ಉತ್ಪಾದ್ಯ → having produced

ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿ ಗುಹಾಂ ಹೃದಯಾಕಾಶಂ

The heart-space, the cave of all beings

  • ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿ → all living beings
  • ಗುಹಾಂ → cave
  • ಹೃದಯಾಕಾಶಂ → the space of the heart

ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ

Having entered, abiding there

  • ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ → having entered
  • ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ → remaining

ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನ್ ಉಪಲಭಮಾನಂ

Experiencing sound and other objects

  • ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನ್ → sound and other sense objects
  • ಉಪಲಭಮಾನಂ → experiencing, perceiving

ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಕಾರ್ಯಕರಣಲಕ್ಷಣೈಃ ಸಹ

Together with body, senses, and mind

  • ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ → with the elements
  • ಕಾರ್ಯ-ಕರಣ-ಲಕ್ಷಣೈಃ → characterized as body and instruments (senses)
  • ಸಹ → together with

ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ

Abiding

  • ತಿಷ್ಠಂತಂ → remaining

ಯಃ ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ

Who sees clearly

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ವ್ಯಪಶ್ಯತ → sees distinctly, realizes

ಯಃ ಏವಂ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ

Who sees in this manner

  • ಯಃ → who
  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ಪಶ್ಯತಿ → sees

ಸಃ ಏತತ್ ಏವ ಪಶ್ಯತಿ

He alone truly sees This

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಏವ → alone
  • ಪಶ್ಯತಿ → sees

ಯತ್ ತತ್ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

Namely the Brahman under discussion

  • ಯತ್ ತತ್ → that which
  • ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ → presently being discussed
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಸಂಭವತಿ ಅದಿತಿರ್ದೇವತಾಮಯೀ । ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿರ್ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೭ ॥   That Aditi, who is constituted of all the deities, who manifests along with Prāṇa, who enters and abides in the cave of the heart, and who appears through the elements—he who realizes Her thus, realizes That. Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಯಾ

Who

  • ಯಾ → who, which

ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಸಂಭವತಿ

Comes forth together with Prāṇa

  • ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ → along with Prāṇa
  • ಸಂಭವತಿ → arises, manifests

ಅದಿತಿಃ ದೇವತಾಮಯೀ

Aditi, consisting of all the deities

  • ಅದಿತಿಃ → Aditi
  • ದೇವತಾ-ಮಯೀ → constituted of the deities

ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ

Having entered the cave (of the heart), abiding there

  • ಗುಹಾಂ → the cave, the heart (Jiva tadatmya)
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ → having entered
  • ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ → abiding

ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ

Who manifested through the elements

  • ಯಾ → who
  • ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ → through the elements
  • ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ → manifested, became differentiated

ಏತತ್ ವೈ ತತ್

Verily, this is That

  • ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ → That (Brahman)

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಾ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾಮಯೀ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭರೂಪೇಣ ಪರಸ್ಮಾದ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ ಸಂಭವತಿ ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನಾಮದನಾತ್ ಅದಿತಿಃ ತಾಂ ಪೂರ್ವವದ್ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಮ್ ಅದಿತಿಮ್ । ತಾಮೇವ ವಿಶಿನಷ್ಟಿ — ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಭೂತೈಃ ಸಮನ್ವಿತಾ ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನೇತ್ಯೇತತ್ ॥   Further, that Aditi, who is of the nature of all the deities and constituted by all the deities, manifests from the Supreme Brahman in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha associated with Prāṇa. She is called Aditi because she consumes (or receives) sound and the other sense objects.  That very Aditi, having entered the cave of the heart as explained before, abides there.  The mantra further specifies her nature: she is the one who manifested together with the elements; that is, she came into existence associated with the elements.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಕಿಂಚ

Further

  • ಕಿಂಚ → moreover, further

ಯಾ ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾಮಯೀ

Who is constituted of all the deities

  • ಯಾ → who
  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ದೇವತಾ → deities
  • ಮಯೀ → consisting of, constituted of

ಸರ್ವದೇವತಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ

Whose nature is all the deities

  • ಸರ್ವ → all
  • ದೇವತಾ → deities
  • ಆತ್ಮಿಕಾ → having the nature of

ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭರೂಪೇಣ

In the form of Hiraṇyagarbha associated with Prāṇa

  • ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ → with Prāṇa
  • ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭ → Hiraṇyagarbha
  • ರೂಪೇಣ → in the form of

ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ ಸಂಭವತಿ

Arises from the Supreme Brahman

  • ಪರಸ್ಮಾತ್ → from the Supreme
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ → Brahman
  • ಸಂಭವತಿ → manifests, arises

ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನಾಂ ಅದನಾತ್ ಅದಿತಿಃ

She is called Aditi because she consumes sound and other objects

  • ಶಬ್ದಾದೀನಾಂ → sound and other sense objects
  • ಅದನಾತ್ → because of consuming
  • ಅದಿತಿಃ → Aditi

ತಾಂ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ಗುಹಾಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ ಅದಿತಿಂ

That Aditi who, as explained before, enters the cave and abides there

  • ತಾಂ → that
  • ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ → as before
  • ಗುಹಾಂ → the cave of the heart
  • ಪ್ರವಿಶ್ಯ → having entered
  • ತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀಂ → abiding
  • ಅದಿತಿಂ → Aditi

ತಾಮೇವ ವಿಶಿನಷ್ಟಿ

The mantra further specifies her

  • ತಾಂ ಏವ → that very one
  • ವಿಶಿನಷ್ಟಿ → distinguishes, explains further

ಯಾ ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ ಭೂತೈಃ ಸಮನ್ವಿತಾ

Who is associated with the elements

  • ಯಾ → who
  • ಭೂತೇಭಿಃ → with the elements
  • ಭೂತೈಃ → by the elements
  • ಸಮನ್ವಿತಾ → associated, accompanied

ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಾ

Manifested, came into existence

  • ವ್ಯಜಾಯತ → manifested
  • ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಾ → arose, came into being

ಇತಿ ಏತತ್

This is the meaning

  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಏತತ್ → this

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಅರಣ್ಯೋರ್ನಿರ್ಹಿತೋ ಜಾತವೇದಾ ಗರ್ಭ ಇವ ಸುಭೃತೋ ಗರ್ಭಿಣೀಭಿಃ । ದಿವೇ ದಿವ ಈಡ್ಯೋ ಜಾಗೃವದ್ಭಿರ್ಹವಿಷ್ಮದ್ಭಿರ್ಮನುಷ್ಯೇಭಿರಗ್ನಿಃ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೮ ॥   Agni, the all-knowing fire, lies hidden in the two araṇi sticks, carefully preserved like an embryo by pregnant women. Day after day, he is worshipped by vigilant men who offer oblations. Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ ಪದಾರ್ಥ
docs.text:
ಅರಣ್ಯೋಃ ನಿರ್ಹಿತಃ ಜಾತವೇದಾಃ

The all-knowing Fire hidden in the two araṇis

  • ಅರಣ್ಯೋಃ → in the two araṇi sticks
  • ನಿರ್ಹಿತಃ → hidden, placed within
  • ಜಾತವೇದಾಃ → Agni, the knower of all beings

ಗರ್ಭಃ ಇವ ಸುಭೃತಃ

Well protected like an embryo

  • ಗರ್ಭಃ → embryo, fetus
  • ಇವ → like
  • ಸುಭೃತಃ → carefully protected, well preserved

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯಃ ಅಧಿಯಜ್ಞಮ್ ಉತ್ತರಾಧರಾರಣ್ಯೋರ್ನಿಹಿತಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಃ ಜಾತವೇದಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಪುನಃ ಸರ್ವಹವಿಷಾಂ ಭೋಕ್ತಾ ಅಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಂ ಚ ಯೋಗಿಭಿಃ, ಗರ್ಭ ಇವ ಗರ್ಭಿಣೀಭಿಃ ಅಂತರ್ವತ್ನೀಭಿರಗರ್ಹಿತಾನ್ನಭೋಜನಾದಿನಾ ಯಥಾ ಗರ್ಭಃ ಸುಭೃತಃ ಸುಷ್ಠು ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಭೃತೋ ಲೋಕೇ, ಇತ್ಥಮೇವ ಋತ್ವಿಗ್ಭಿರ್ಯೋಗಿಭಿಶ್ಚ ಸುಭೃತ ಇತ್ಯೇತತ್ । ಕಿಂಚ, ದಿವೇ ದಿವೇ ಅಹನ್ಯಹನಿ ಈಡ್ಯಃ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯೋ ವಂದ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಕರ್ಮಿಭಿರ್ಯೋಗಿಭಿಶ್ಚಾಧ್ವರೇ ಹೃದಯೇ ಚ ಜಾಗೃವದ್ಭಿಃ ಜಾಗರಣಶೀಲೈಃ ಅಪ್ರಮತ್ತೈರಿತ್ಯೇತತ್ । ಹವಿಷ್ಮದ್ಭಿಃ ಆಜ್ಯಾದಿಮದ್ಭಿಃ ಧ್ಯಾನಭಾವನಾವದ್ಭಿಶ್ಚ ಮನುಷ್ಯೇಭಿಃ ಮನುಷ್ಯೈಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ; ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ತದೇವ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ॥   Further, that Agni, known as Jātavedas, who in the sacrificial context is hidden and established in the upper and lower araṇi sticks, and who is the enjoyer of all sacrificial offerings, is also realized inwardly by yogins.  Just as an embryo is carefully nourished and protected by pregnant women through proper food and conduct, so too this Agni is carefully sustained by priests through ritual and by yogins through contemplation.  Moreover, day after day he is worthy of praise and worship by ritualists in the sacrifice and by yogins in the heart. He is worshipped by vigilant and attentive persons who are free from negligence.  He is served by people possessing offerings such as ghee and other sacrificial materials, and also by those endowed with meditation and contemplation.  Verily, this Agni is that very Brahman which is the subject under discussion.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text: ಯತಶ್ಚೋದೇತಿ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ಅಸ್ತಂ ಯತ್ರ ಚ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ । ತಂ ದೇವಾಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ಅರ್ಪಿತಾಸ್ತದು ನಾತ್ಯೇತಿ ಕಶ್ಚನ । ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥ ೯ ॥   From whom the Sun rises, and into whom it sets; upon whom all the deities depend; whom none can ever transcend—verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text: ಕಿಂಚ, ಯತಶ್ಚ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ ಉದೇತಿ ಉತ್ತಿಷ್ಠತಿ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ, ಅಸ್ತಂ ನಿಮ್ಲೋಚನಂ ತಿರೋಧಾನಂ ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನೇವ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣೇ ಅಹನ್ಯಹನಿ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ, ತಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ದೇವಾಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ಅಗ್ನ್ಯಾದಯಃ ಅಧಿದೈವಂ ವಾಗಾದಯಶ್ಚಾಧ್ಯಾತ್ಮಂ ಸರ್ವೇ ವಿಶ್ವೇ ಅರಾ ಇವ ರಥನಾಭೌ ಅರ್ಪಿತಾಃ ಸಂಪ್ರವೇಶಿತಾಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಕಾಲೇ । ಸೋಽಪಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮೈವ । ತತ್ ಏತತ್ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ, ತದು ನಾತ್ಯೇತಿ ನಾತೀತ್ಯ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತಾಂ ತದನ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಗಚ್ಛತಿ, ಕಶ್ಚನ ಕಶ್ಚಿದಪಿ ಏತದ್ವೈ ತತ್ ॥   Further, from that Prāṇa the Sun rises and becomes manifest; and into that very Prāṇa it sets and disappears day after day.  Upon that Prāṇa, which is the Self, all the deities such as Agni in the cosmic sphere, and speech and the other faculties in the individual sphere, are established. They are fixed in it just as the spokes of a wheel are fixed in the hub.  That Prāṇa is itself Brahman.  This Brahman is the Self of all. No one can go beyond It. No one can transcend Its nature and become something other than It, for there exists nothing apart from It.  Verily, this is That.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ 3.2.1
docs.text:
ಸ ವೇದೈತತ್ಪರಮಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಧಾಮ ಯತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ನಿಹಿತಂ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಮ್ । ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹ್ಯಕಾಮಾಸ್ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಮೇತದತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ ॥ ೧ ॥ He knows that supreme Brahman, the luminous abode in which the entire universe rests and shines. Those wise ones who, free from desires, meditate upon that Purusha, transcend this seed of birth (saṁsāra).

ಸಃ ವೇದ ಏತತ್ ಪರಮಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಧಾಮ

He knows this supreme Brahman, the abode.

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ವೇದ → knows
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಪರಮಂ → supreme
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಧಾಮ → abode, luminous reality

ಯತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ನಿಹಿತಂ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಂ

Where the whole universe rests and shines in purity.

  • ಯತ್ರ → wherein
  • ವಿಶ್ವಂ → universe
  • ನಿಹಿತಂ → lodged, established
  • ಭಾತಿ → shines
  • ಶುಭ್ರಂ → pure, luminous

ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹಿ ಅಕಾಮಾಃ

  • ಉಪಾಸತೇ → meditate upon
  • ಪುರುಷಂ → Purusha, Supreme Being
  • ಯೇ → who
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಅಕಾಮಾಃ → free from desires

ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಮ್ ಏತತ್ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ

Those wise ones transcend this seed/source of birth.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಶುಕ್ರಮ್ → seed, source of generation
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ → transcend
  • ಧೀರಾಃ → wise ones

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸ ವೇದ ಜಾನಾತಿ ಏತತ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರಮಂ ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಧಾಮ ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಮಾಶ್ರಯಮಾಸ್ಪದಮ್, ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ ಧಾಮ್ನಿ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸಮಸ್ತಂ ಜಗತ್ ನಿಹಿತಮ್ ಅರ್ಪಿತಮ್, ಯಚ್ಚ ಸ್ವೇನ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಂ ಶುದ್ಧಮ್, ತಮಪ್ಯೇವಂವಿಧಮಾತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹಿ ಅಕಾಮಾಃ ವಿಭೂತಿತೃಷ್ಣಾವರ್ಜಿತಾ ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ ಸಂತಃ ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಪರಮಿವ ದೇವಮ್, ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಂ ನೃಬೀಜಂ ಯದೇತತ್ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಮ್ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ ಬುದ್ಧಿಮಂತಃ, ನ ಪುನರ್ಯೋನಿಂ ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ । ‘ನ ಪುನಃ ಕ್ವ ರತಿಂ ಕರೋತಿ’ ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ । ಅತಸ್ತಂ ಪೂಜಯೇದಿತ್ಯಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ ॥ Because he knows this Brahman characterized as previously described—the supreme Reality, the support and abode of all desires, in which the entire universe is established and offered, and which shines by its own light as pure—that knower of the Self, being of such nature, is meditated upon by seekers of liberation who are free from craving for powers and enjoyments, as though He were the Supreme Lord Himself. Those wise ones transcend this seed of human birth, namely the well-known cause of embodiment. They do not again enter the womb. As the scripture says: > "He does not again delight in birth." Therefore, the intention is that such a knower should indeed be worshipped.

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸಃ ವೇದ ಜಾನಾತಿ ಏತತ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ

Because he knows this Brahman characterized as previously described.

  • ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ → because
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ವೇದ → knows
  • ಜಾನಾತಿ → understands
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣಂ → having the characteristics already described
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman

ಪರಮಂ ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ ಧಾಮ ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಂ ಆಶ್ರಯಂ ಆಸ್ಪದಂ

The supreme abode and support of all desires.

  • ಪರಮಂ → supreme
  • ಪ್ರಕೃಷ್ಟಂ → highest
  • ಧಾಮ → abode
  • ಸರ್ವಕಾಮಾನಾಂ → of all desires
  • ಆಶ್ರಯಂ → support
  • ಆಸ್ಪದಂ → resting place

ಯತ್ರ ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ ಧಾಮ್ನಿ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸಮಸ್ತಂ ಜಗತ್ ನಿಹಿತಂ ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ

In which Brahman the entire universe is established and offered.

  • ಯತ್ರ → wherein
  • ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ → in which
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಿ → in Brahman
  • ಧಾಮ್ನಿ → in the luminous abode
  • ವಿಶ್ವಂ → universe
  • ಸಮಸ್ತಂ → entire
  • ಜಗತ್ → world
  • ನಿಹಿತಂ → placed
  • ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ → offered/resting

ಯತ್ ಚ ಸ್ವೇನ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ ಭಾತಿ ಶುಭ್ರಂ ಶುದ್ಧಂ

And which shines by its own light as pure.

  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಚ → and
  • ಸ್ವೇನ → by its own
  • ಜ್ಯೋತಿಷಾ → light
  • ಭಾತಿ → shines
  • ಶುಭ್ರಂ → luminous/pure
  • ಶುದ್ಧಂ → pure

ತಂ ಅಪಿ ಏವಂವಿಧಂ ಆತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ ಪುರುಷಂ ಯೇ ಹಿ ಅಕಾಮಾಃ ವಿಭೂತಿತೃಷ್ಣಾ ವರ್ಜಿತಾಃ ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ ಸಂತಃ ಉಪಾಸತೇ

That knower of the Self is meditated upon by desireless seekers of liberation free from craving for powers.

  • ತಂ → that
  • ಅಪಿ → indeed
  • ಏವಂವಿಧಂ → of such nature
  • ಆತ್ಮಜ್ಞಂ → knower of Self
  • ಪುರುಷಂ → person
  • ಯೇ → who
  • ಹಿ → indeed
  • ಅಕಾಮಾಃ → desireless
  • ವಿಭೂತಿ → powers/glories
  • ತೃಷ್ಣಾ → craving
  • ವರ್ಜಿತಾಃ → free from
  • ಮುಮುಕ್ಷವಃ → seekers of liberation
  • ಸಂತಃ → being
  • ಉಪಾಸತೇ → meditate upon/worship

ಪರಂ ಇವ ದೇವಂ

As though He were the Supreme Lord.

  • ಪರಂ → supreme
  • ಇವ → as though
  • ದೇವಂ → divine Lord

ತೇ ಶುಕ್ರಂ ನೃಬೀಜಂ ಯತ್ ಏತತ್ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಂ ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ ಧೀರಾಃ

Those wise ones transcend the seed of human birth, the cause of embodiment.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಶುಕ್ರಂ → seed
  • ನೃಬೀಜಂ → human seed
  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ಏತತ್ → this
  • ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ → well-known
  • ಶರೀರೋಪಾದಾನಕಾರಣಂ → cause of bodily embodiment
  • ಅತಿವರ್ತಂತಿ → transcend
  • ಅತಿಗಚ್ಛಂತಿ → go beyond
  • ಧೀರಾಃ → wise ones

ನ ಪುನಃ ಯೋನಿಂ ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ

They do not again enter the womb.

  • ನ → not
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಯೋನಿಂ → womb/birth
  • ಪ್ರಸರ್ಪಂತಿ → enter/proceed into

ನ ಪುನಃ ಕ್ವ ರತಿಂ ಕರೋತಿ ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ

As scripture says: “He does not again delight in birth.”

  • ನ → not
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಕ್ವ → anywhere
  • ರತಿಂ → attachment/delight/like
  • ಕರೋತಿ → makes
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಶ್ರುತೇಃ → from scripture

ಅತಃ ತಂ ಪೂಜಯೇತ್ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ

Therefore the intention is that such a knower should be worshipped.

  • ಅತಃ → therefore
  • ತಂ → him
  • ಪೂಜಯೇತ್ → should worship
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ → intention

docs.title: ಅವತಾರಿಕಾಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ ವಿಸ್ತರಾನುವಾದೀದಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಮಾರಭ್ಯತೇ । ಋಷಿಪ್ರಶ್ನಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನಾಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾಸ್ತುತಯೇ । ಏವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಸಂವಾಸಾದಿತಪೋಯುಕ್ತೈರ್ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ, ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈರಾಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ ಚ, ನ ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿದಿತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ ಸ್ತೌತಿ । ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿಸಾಧನಸೂಚನಾಚ್ಚ ತತ್ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ ಸ್ಯಾತ್ — This Brāhmaṇa section is now commenced as a detailed exposition of the meaning that was briefly stated in the mantra. The narrative in the form of the sages asking questions and receiving answers is intended for the glorification of this knowledge (Brahma-vidyā). The purpose is to praise the knowledge by showing that it is fit to be received only by those who have undergone austerities such as living in brahmacarya for a year, residing with the teacher, and observing other disciplines. Likewise, it is to be taught only by teachers who, like Pippalāda, are comparable to omniscient persons; it is not something that may be taught by just anyone. Thus the Upaniṣad extols the greatness of this knowledge. Furthermore, by indicating disciplines such as brahmacarya and the like, the text also establishes that these are duties to be undertaken by seekers of knowledge.

ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸ್ಯ ವಿಸ್ತರಾನುವಾದೀ ಇದಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಮಾರಭ್ಯತೇ

This Brāhmaṇa portion is begun as a detailed explanation of the meaning expressed in the mantra.

  • ಮಂತ್ರೋಕ್ತಸ್ಯ → stated in the mantra
  • ಅರ್ಥಸ್ಯ → of the meaning
  • ವಿಸ್ತರ → detailed
  • ಅನುವಾದೀ → explanatory restatement
  • ಇದಂ → this
  • ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಂ → Brāhmaṇa section
  • ಆರಭ್ಯತೇ → is commenced

(Mundaka is mantra and Prasna is brahmana )

ಋಷಿಪ್ರಶ್ನಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನಾಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ ತು ವಿದ್ಯಾಸ್ತುತಯೇ

The narrative consisting of the sages' questions and answers is for the praise of the knowledge.

  • ಋಷಿ → sage
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ → question
  • ಪ್ರತಿವಾಚನ → answer
  • ಆಖ್ಯಾಯಿಕಾ → narrative account
  • ತು → indeed
  • ವಿದ್ಯಾ → knowledge
  • ಸ್ತುತಯೇ → for praise

ಏವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಸಂವಾಸಾದಿತಪೋಯುಕ್ತೈರ್ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ

Thus this knowledge is to be received by those endowed with austerities such as living for a year in brahmacarya and residing with the teacher.

  • ಏವಂ → thus
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರ → one year
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯ → celibate discipline
  • ಸಂವಾಸ → residence with the teacher (gurukula)
  • ಆದಿ → and other
  • ತಪಃ → austerities
  • ಯುಕ್ತೈಃ → endowed with
  • ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ → fit to be received

ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈರಾಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ ಚ

And it is to be taught by teachers who, like Pippalāda, are comparable to omniscient persons.

  • ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದವತ್ → like Pippalāda
  • ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಕಲ್ಪೈಃ → comparable to omniscient beings (kalpa = like)
  • ಆಚಾರ್ಯೈಃ → by teachers
  • ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಾ → should be taught
  • ಚ → and

ನ ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿದಿತಿ ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ ಸ್ತೌತಿ

By implying that it should not be taught by just anyone, the text praises the knowledge.

  • ನ → not
  • ಯೇನ ಕೇನಚಿತ್ → by any random person
  • ಇತಿ → thus
  • ವಿದ್ಯಾಂ → the knowledge
  • ಸ್ತೌತಿ → praises

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿಸಾಧನಸೂಚನಾಚ್ಚ ತತ್ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ ಸ್ಯಾತ್

And by indicating disciplines such as brahmacarya, it establishes that these are to be practiced.

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಾದಿ → brahmacarya and similar disciplines
  • ಸಾಧನ → means/spiritual disciplines
  • ಸೂಚನಾತ್ → by indicating
  • ಚ → and
  • ತತ್ → those
  • ಕರ್ತವ್ಯತಾ → obligatoriness, duty
  • ಸ್ಯಾತ್ → is established

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text:
ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ ಶೈಬ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಚ ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಶ್ಚಾಶ್ವಲಾಯನೋ ಭಾರ್ಗವೋ ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಸ್ತೇ ಹೈತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಾನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾ ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತೀತಿ ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯೋ ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಮುಪಸನ್ನಾಃ ॥ ೧ ॥ Sukeśa, the son of Bharadvāja; Satyakāma, the son of Śibi; Gārgya of the lineage of Sūryāyaṇa; Kauśalya, the son of Aśvala; Bhārgava of Vidarbha; and Kabandhi, the son of Kātyāyana—these seekers were devoted to Brahman, established in Brahman, and desirous of knowing the Supreme Brahman. Thinking, “Surely this revered teacher will explain all this to us,” they approached the venerable Pippalāda, carrying sacrificial fuel in their hands.

ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ

And Sukeśa, the son of Bharadvāja.

  • ಸುಕೇಶಃ → Sukeśa
  • ಚ → and
  • ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ → descendant/son of Bharadvāja

ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ ಚ ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ

And Satyakāma, the descendant of Śibi.

  • ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ → descendant of Śibi
  • ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ → Satyakāma

ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಚ ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ

And Gārgya of the Sūryāyaṇa lineage.

  • ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ → belonging to Sūryāyaṇa lineage
  • ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ → Gārgya

ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ ಚ ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ

And Kauśalya, son of Aśvala.

  • ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ → Kauśalya
  • ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ → descendant of Aśvala

ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ

Bhārgava of Vidarbha.

  • ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ → descendant of Bhṛgu
  • ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ → from Vidarbha

ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ

Kabandhi, son of Kātyāyana.

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhi
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Kātyāyana

ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ

These indeed were devoted to Brahman.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಏತೇ → these
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ → having Brahman as their supreme goal

ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ

Established in Brahman.

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → steadfast in contemplation of Brahman

In this context, Śaṅkara generally takes this as being devoted to scriptural pursuit and contemplation leading toward Brahma-jñāna.

ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ

Seeking the Supreme Brahman.

  • ಪರಂ → supreme
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ → searching for, seeking

ಏಷಃ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ ಇತಿ

Thinking, “Surely he will explain all that.”

  • ಏಷಃ → this teacher
  • ಹ ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ → all that (Brahman-related knowledge)
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ → will explain
  • ಇತಿ → thus

ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯಃ

They approached carrying sacrificial fuel in their hands.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಸಮಿತ್ → sacrificial fuel sticks
  • ಪಾಣಯಃ → in their hands

Samit-pāṇi is symbolic: humility readiness for discipleship willingness to serve the teacher

ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಂ ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ

They approached the revered Pippalāda.

  • ಭಗವಂತಂ → venerable, revered one
  • ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಂ → Pippalāda
  • ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ → approached

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ನಾಮತಃ, ಭರದ್ವಾಜಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ । ಶೈಬ್ಯಶ್ಚ ಶಿಬೇರಪತ್ಯಂ ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ, ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮೋ ನಾಮತಃ । ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಃ, ತಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣಿಃ ; ಛಾಂದಸಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ ; ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ ಗರ್ಗಗೋತ್ರೋತ್ಪನ್ನಃ । ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಶ್ಚ ನಾಮತಃ, ಅಶ್ವಲಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಮಾಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ । ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ಭೃಗೋರ್ಗೋತ್ರಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ, ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ ವಿದರ್ಭೇಷು ಭವಃ । ಕಬಂಧೀ ನಾಮತಃ, ಕತ್ಯಸ್ಯಾಪತ್ಯಂ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ; ವಿದ್ಯಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಪಿತಾಮಹೋ ಯಸ್ಯ ಸಃ ; ಯುವಪ್ರತ್ಯಯಃ । ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರತ್ವೇನ ಗತಾಃ, ತದನುಷ್ಠಾನನಿಷ್ಠಾಶ್ಚ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ, ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ಯನ್ನಿತ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞೇಯಮಿತಿ ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯತಿಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ತದನ್ವೇಷಣಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ, ತದಧಿಗಮಾಯ ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತೀತಿ ಆಚಾರ್ಯಮುಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ । ಕಥಮ್ ? ತೇ ಹ ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯಃ ಸಮಿದ್ಭಾರಗೃಹೀತಹಸ್ತಾಃ ಸಂತಃ, ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪೂಜಾವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಮಾಚಾರ್ಯಮ್ ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ ಉಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ ॥ Sukeśa is the personal name; being the son of Bharadvāja, he is called Bhāradvāja. Likewise, Śaibya means a descendant of Śibi, while Satyakāma is his personal name. Sauryāyaṇi means a descendant of Sūrya; "Sauryāyaṇi" is a Vedic form of expression. Gārgya means one born in the lineage of Garga. Kauśalya is the personal name, and Āśvalāyana means a descendant of Aśvala. Bhārgava means one descended from the lineage of Bhṛgu, and Vaidarbhi means one belonging to the region of Vidarbha. Kabandhi is the personal name, and Kātyāyana means a descendant of Katya; the suffix indicates that the ancestor (Katya) is still remembered in the lineage. These indeed were devoted to Brahman, taking the lower Brahman as their supreme goal and being steadfast in its contemplation and worship; hence they are called Brahmaniṣṭhas. At the same time, they were seekers of the Supreme Brahman, wondering, "What is that eternal Reality which ought to be known?" Desiring to attain That, and resolving, "We shall strive in every way to realize It," they engaged in the search for the Supreme Brahman. Thinking, "Surely this teacher will explain all that to us," they approached him. How did they approach? Carrying bundles of sacrificial fuel in their hands, they approached the revered and venerable teacher Pippalāda.

ಸುಕೇಶಾ ಚ ನಾಮತಃ

"Sukeśa" is the personal name.

  • ಸುಕೇಶಾ → Sukeśa
  • ನಾಮತಃ → by name

ಭರದ್ವಾಜಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ

Being the son (descendant) of Bharadvāja, he is called Bhāradvāja.

  • ಭರದ್ವಾಜಸ್ಯ → of Bharadvāja
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring
  • ಭಾರದ್ವಾಜಃ → descendant of Bharadvāja

ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ ಚ ಶಿಬೇಃ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ

Śaibya means a descendant of Śibi.

  • ಶೈಬ್ಯಃ → descendant of Śibi
  • ಶಿಬೇಃ → of Śibi
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring

ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ ನಾಮತಃ

Satyakāma is the personal name.

  • ಸತ್ಯಕಾಮಃ → Satyakāma
  • ನಾಮತಃ → by name

ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ

Sauryāyaṇi means a descendant of Sūrya.

  • ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀ → Sauryāyaṇi
  • ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯ → of Sūrya
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring

ಛಾಂದಸಂ ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ

"Sauryāyaṇi" is the Vedic (metrical) form.

  • ಛಾಂದಸಂ → Vedic usage
  • ಸೌರ್ಯಾಯಣೀತಿ → the form "Sauryāyaṇi"

ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ ಗರ್ಗಗೋತ್ರೋತ್ಪನ್ನಃ

Gārgya is one born in the lineage of Garga.

  • ಗಾರ್ಗ್ಯಃ → Gārgya
  • ಗರ್ಗ → Garga
  • ಗೋತ್ರ → lineage
  • ಉತ್ಪನ್ನಃ → born

ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ ಚ ನಾಮತಃ

Kauśalya is the personal name.

  • ಕೌಸಲ್ಯಃ → Kauśalya
  • ನಾಮತಃ → by name

ಅಶ್ವಲಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ

Āśvalāyana means descendant of Aśvala.

  • ಅಶ್ವಲಸ್ಯ → of Aśvala
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring
  • ಆಶ್ವಲಾಯನಃ → descendant of Aśvala

ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ ಭೃಗೋಃ ಗೋತ್ರಾಪತ್ಯಂ

Bhārgava means one descended from Bhṛgu's lineage.

  • ಭಾರ್ಗವಃ → Bhārgava
  • ಭೃಗೋಃ → of Bhṛgu
  • ಗೋತ್ರಾಪತ್ಯಂ → descendant of the lineage

ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ ವಿದರ್ಭೇಷು ಭವಃ

Vaidarbhi means belonging to Vidarbha.

  • ವೈದರ್ಭಿಃ → Vaidarbhi
  • ವಿದರ್ಭೇಷು → in Vidarbha
  • ಭವಃ → born/residing

ಕಬಂಧೀ ನಾಮತಃ

Kabandhi is the personal name.

  • ಕಬಂಧೀ → Kabandhi
  • ನಾಮತಃ → by name

ಕತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಅಪತ್ಯಂ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ

Kātyāyana means descendant of Katya.

  • ಕತ್ಯಸ್ಯ → of Katya
  • ಅಪತ್ಯಂ → offspring
  • ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ → descendant of Katya

ತೇ ಹ ಏತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ

These indeed were devoted to Brahman.

  • ತೇ → they
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ಏತೇ → these
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ → devoted to Brahman

ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಪರತ್ವೇನ ಗತಾಃ

They had taken the lower Brahman as their immediate object of worship.

  • ಅಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → lower Brahman (saguṇa Brahman)
  • ಪರತ್ವೇನ → as supreme
  • ಗತಾಃ → accepted

This is an important Śaṅkara gloss. Here "ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ" is interpreted as seekers devoted to meditation upon saguṇa Brahman.

ತದನುಷ್ಠಾನನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ ಚ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ

And they were steadfast in its practice.

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಅನುಷ್ಠಾನ → practice/worship
  • ನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → steadfast
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿಷ್ಠಾಃ → devoted to Brahman

ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ

Seeking the Supreme Brahman.

  • ಪರಂ → supreme
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ → Brahman
  • ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ → searching for

Notice the distinction:

  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪರಾಃ → devoted to lower Brahman
  • ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ → seeking knowledge of Nirguṇa Brahman

ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ಯತ್ ನಿತ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞೇಯಂ ಇತಿ

"What is that eternal Reality that ought to be known?"

  • ಕಿಂ ತತ್ → what is that?
  • ಯತ್ → which
  • ನಿತ್ಯಂ → eternal
  • ವಿಜ್ಞೇಯಂ → to be known
  • ಇತಿ → thus

Śaṅkara presents the inner enquiry motivating them.

ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯತಿಷ್ಯಾಮಃ

"We shall strive in every way to attain That."

  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿ → attainment
  • ಅರ್ಥಂ → for the sake of
  • ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ → by every possible effort
  • ಯತಿಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall strive

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ ಇತಿ

"Surely he will explain all this."

  • ಏಷಃ → this teacher
  • ಹ ವೈ → indeed
  • ತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ → all that
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯತಿ → will explain

ಆಚಾರ್ಯಂ ಉಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ

They approached the teacher.

  • ಆಚಾರ್ಯಂ → teacher
  • ಉಪಜಗ್ಮುಃ → approached

ಸಮಿತ್ಪಾಣಯಃ

Carrying fuel sticks in their hands.

  • ಸಮಿತ್ → sacrificial fuel
  • ಪಾಣಯಃ → in their hands

This signifies: humility discipleship readiness for service

ಸಮಿದ್ಭಾರಗೃಹೀತಹಸ್ತಾಃ ಸಂತಃ

Having their hands occupied with bundles of fuel.

  • ಸಮಿದ್ಭಾರ → bundle of fuel sticks
  • ಗೃಹೀತ → held
  • ಹಸ್ತಾಃ → hands
  • ಸಂತಃ → being

ಭಗವಂತಂ ಪೂಜಾವಂತಂ ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಂ ಆಚಾರ್ಯಂ ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ

They approached the revered teacher Pippalāda.

  • ಭಗವಂತಂ → venerable one
  • ಪೂಜಾವಂತಂ → worthy of worship
  • ಪಿಪ್ಪಲಾದಂ → Pippalāda
  • ಆಚಾರ್ಯಂ → teacher
  • ಉಪಸನ್ನಾಃ → approached

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಅಥೋತ್ತರೇಣ ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾತ್ಮಾನಮನ್ವಿಷ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

ಏತದ್ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಮಾಯತನಮೇತದಮೃತಮಭಯಮೇತತ್ಪರಾಯಣಮೇತಸ್ಮಾನ್ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತ ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ನಿರೋಧಃ ।

ತದೇಷ ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ ॥ ೧೦ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Now, by the Northern path — through austerity, celibacy (brahmacarya), faith (śraddhā), and knowledge (vidyā) — having sought out the Self, they win the Sun (Āditya).

This (the Sun) is indeed the abode of all the prāṇas, it is immortal, it is fearless, it is the supreme goal — from it they do not return again. This is the stopping (nirodha, the end of transmigration).

And on this subject there is the following verse (śloka).

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಅಥ — now / next · ಉತ್ತರೇಣ — by the Northern (path) · ತಪಸಾ — through austerity · ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ — through celibacy / brahmacarya · ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ — through faith · ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ — through knowledge · ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ — the Self · ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ — having sought out / having enquired into · ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ — the Sun · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — they win / attain ।

ಏತತ್ — this · ವೈ — indeed · ಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ — of the prāṇas (vital forces) · ಆಯತನಂ — the abode / support · ಏತತ್ — this · ಅಮೃತಂ — immortal / deathless · ಅಭಯಂ — fearless / without fear · ಏತತ್ — this · ಪರಾಯಣಂ — the supreme goal / final refuge · ಏತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — from this · ನ — not · ಪುನಃ — again · ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ — they return · ಇತಿ — thus · ಏಷಃ — this · ನಿರೋಧಃ — the stopping / the end of return ।

ತತ್ — on that · ಏಷಃ — this · ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ — verse / śloka ॥

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಅಥ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಅಯನೇನ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರಂಶಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮತ್ತಾರಮ್ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

ಕೇನ ? ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಜಯೇನ ।

ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ಜಗತಃ ತಸ್ಥುಷಶ್ಚ ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ ಅಹಮಸ್ಮೀತಿ ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ ।

ಏತದ್ವೈ ಆಯತನಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಮಾಯತನಮ್ ಆಶ್ರಯಃ ಏತತ್ ಅಮೃತಮ್ ಅವಿನಾಶಿ ಅಭಯಮ್ ಅತ ಏವ ಭಯವರ್ಜಿತಮ್ ನ ಚಂದ್ರವತ್ಕ್ಷಯವೃದ್ಧಿಭಯವತ್ ; ಏತತ್ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಪರಾ ಗತಿರ್ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಮ್ ಏತಸ್ಮಾನ್ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಯಥೇತರೇ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣ ಇತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏಷಃ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ, ಆದಿತ್ಯಾದ್ಧಿ ನಿರುದ್ಧಾ ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ ।

ನೈತೇ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಮಾದಿತ್ಯಮಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಮಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ ।

ಸ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ ।

ತತ್ ತತ್ರಾಸ್ಮಿನ್ನರ್ಥೇ ಏಷಃ ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ ಮಂತ್ರಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Now by the Northern solstice-path, they win the Sun (Āditya) — that portion of Prajāpati which is Prāṇa, the eater.

How? Through austerity, which is conquest of the senses.

More specifically, through brahmacarya, through faith, and through knowledge directed at the identity with Prajāpati's Self — having sought out the Self, which is Prāṇa, which is the Sun, the support of what moves and what stands still in the universe, and having realised "I am That (aham asmi)" — they win, they reach the Sun.

This (Sun) is indeed the common abode, the support of all prāṇas. This is immortal, imperishable. This is fearless — free from fear precisely because it is unlike the Moon which is subject to waxing, waning, and the fear of decline. This is the supreme goal, the highest destination of those who have knowledge alone and of those who combine action with knowledge. From this they do not return, unlike those others who are mere performers of ritual action. Therefore this (Sun, the Year) is the nirodha — the stopping — for the ignorant; for the ignorant are stopped, held back, by the Sun (Āditya).

These (the ignorant) do not reach the Year, the Sun, the Self, the Prāṇa.

For that Year, whose nature is Time (kālātmā), is the nirodha — the boundary — for the ignorant.

And on this subject there is this śloka — this mantra.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಅಥ — now / next · ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಅಯನೇನ — by the Northern solstice-path · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ — of Prajāpati · ಅಂಶಂ — portion / aspect · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa (the life-force) · ಅತ್ತಾರಂ — the eater / consumer · ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ — the Sun · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — they win / attain ।

ಕೇನ — by what (means)? · ತಪಸಾ — through austerity · ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಜಯೇನ — through conquest of the senses ।

ವಿಶೇಷತಃ — more specifically · ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ — through brahmacarya (celibacy / student discipline) · ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ — through faith · ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ — and through knowledge · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ — directed at / concerned with the identity with Prajāpati's Self · ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ — the Self · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa · ಸೂರ್ಯಂ — the Sun · ಜಗತಃ — of the world / universe · ತಸ್ಥುಷಃ ಚ — and of what stands still · ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ — having sought out / enquired into · ಅಹಮಸ್ಮಿ ಇತಿ — "I am That" · ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ — having known / realised · ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ — the Sun · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — they win · ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ — they reach / attain ।

ಏತತ್ ವೈ — this indeed · ಆಯತನಂ — abode / support · ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾನಾಂ — of all prāṇas · ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಂ — common / universal · ಆಯತನಂ — abode · ಆಶ್ರಯಃ — support / refuge · ಏತತ್ — this · ಅಮೃತಂ — immortal · ಅವಿನಾಶಿ — imperishable · ಅಭಯಂ — fearless · ಅತ ಏವ — precisely therefore · ಭಯವರ್ಜಿತಂ — free from fear · ನ ಚಂದ್ರವತ್ — unlike the Moon · ಕ್ಷಯವೃದ್ಧಿಭಯವತ್ — subject to waning, waxing, and fear · ಏತತ್ — this · ಪರಾಯಣಂ — the supreme goal · ಪರಾ ಗತಿಃ — the highest destination · ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ — of those who have knowledge (alone) · ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಂ — and of those who combine action with knowledge · ಏತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — from this · ನ ಪುನಃ ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ — they do not return again · ಯಥಾ ಇತರೇ — unlike those others · ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಃ — mere performers of ritual action · ಇತಿ — thus · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ — because / therefore · ಏಷಃ — this · ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ — for the ignorant · ನಿರೋಧಃ — the stopping / the boundary · ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ ಹಿ — for from the Sun · ನಿರುದ್ಧಾಃ — stopped / held back · ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ — the ignorant ।

ನ ಏತೇ — these (ignorant ones) do not · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ — the Year · ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ — the Sun · ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ — the Self · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa · ಅಭಿಪ್ರಾಪ್ನುವಂತಿ — reach / attain ।

ಸಃ ಹಿ — for that · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — Year · ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ — whose nature is Time · ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ — for the ignorant · ನಿರೋಧಃ — the stopping / boundary ।

ತತ್ — on that · ತತ್ರ — there / on this subject · ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಅರ್ಥೇ — in this matter · ಏಷಃ — this · ಶ್ಲೋಕಃ — verse · ಮಂತ್ರಃ — mantra ॥

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya for this verse has two sentences that require explicit anvaya treatment, both flagged by Ānandagiri.

Sentence 1 — The means of attaining the Sun

As written:

ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ಜಗತಃ ತಸ್ಥುಷಶ್ಚ ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ ಅಹಮಸ್ಮೀತಿ ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಸಾಧಕಾಃ] ವಿಶೇಷತಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ, ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ, ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮ-ವಿಷಯಯಾ ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ ಚ — ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ [ಯಃ] ಪ್ರಾಣಃ, [ಯಃ] ಸೂರ್ಯಃ, [ಯಃ] ಜಗತಃ ತಸ್ಥುಷಃ ಚ [ಆಧಾರಃ] — ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ, ಅಹಮಸ್ಮಿ ಇತಿ ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ, ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

English: The seekers — specifically through brahmacarya, through faith, and through knowledge directed at identity with Prajāpati's Self — having sought out the Self (which is Prāṇa, which is the Sun, which is the support of the moving and the still in the universe) and having realised "I am That" — win the Sun.

Note: The long participial chain (ಅನ್ವಿಷ್ಯ … ವಿದಿತ್ವಾ) governs the final verb ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ. The relative clause defining ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ as Prāṇa, Sun, and universal support is embedded mid-sentence and must be separated out. The qualifier ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ modifies ವಿದ್ಯಯಾ only, not all three instruments.

Sentence 2 — Nirodha: the Sun as boundary for the ignorant

As written:

ಏತಸ್ಮಾನ್ನ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಯಥೇತರೇ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣ ಇತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏಷಃ ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ, ಆದಿತ್ಯಾದ್ಧಿ ನಿರುದ್ಧಾ ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಂ] ಏತಸ್ಮಾತ್ [ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್] ನ ಪುನಃ ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ — [ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ] ಯಥಾ ಇತರೇ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಃ [ಆವರ್ತಂತೇ] ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ [ಏವಂ] — ಏಷಃ [ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ / ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ] ಅವಿದುಷಾಂ ನಿರೋಧಃ ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ ಹಿ ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ ನಿರುದ್ಧಾಃ [ಭವಂತಿ] ।

English: Those with knowledge do not return from the Sun — unlike those others who are mere ritual performers (who do return). Because this is so — this (Sun / Year) is the nirodha, the stopping-point, for the ignorant; for the ignorant are indeed held back, stopped, at the Sun.

Note: The sentence pivots on ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ … ಏಷಃ ನಿರೋಧಃ, where "nirodha" carries a double meaning: (1) the final stopping of transmigration for the knowers, and (2) the barrier beyond which the ignorant cannot pass. Ānandagiri clarifies that the subject of ನಿರುದ್ಧಾ is ಅವಿದ್ವಾಂಸಃ — the ignorant are stopped at the Sun, not liberated by it.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಅಥೇತಿ ।

ಮಾರ್ಗಾಂತರಾರಂಭಾರ್ಥಃ ಅಥಶಬ್ದಃ ।

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಾ ಇತಿ ।

ತತ್ತಾದಾತ್ಮ್ಯವಿಷಯಯಾ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೂರ್ವಮನ್ವಯಾರ್ಥಮುಕ್ತಂ ಇದಾನೀಂ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಾರ್ಥಮಿತಿ ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಮ್ ।

ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಮಿತಿ ।

ಸಮಷ್ಟಿರೂಪಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಮಿತಿ ।

ಕರ್ಮಾನಧಿಕಾರಿಣಾಂ ಅತ ಏವ ಕೇವಲೋಪಾಸನವತಾಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಮಿತಿ ।

ಸಮುಚ್ಚಯವತಾಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ನನು ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಮಪ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಾವಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿರ್ಭವಿಷ್ಯತೀತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ತೇಷಾಮಾದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿರೇವ ನಾಸ್ತೀತಿ ವಕ್ತುಮಿತ್ಯೇಷ ಇತಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಇತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾದಿತಿ ।

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ತೇಷಾಮಾದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿರನಾಶಂಕ್ಯೇತಿ ಶೇಷಃ ।

ಯದ್ವಾ ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ಇತ್ಯಾರಭ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ನಿರೋಧ ಇತ್ಯಂತಂ ಶ್ರುತಿವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಅಯನಯೋಃ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಪ್ರತಿಪಾದನಪರತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯೇಯಮ್ ।

ತಥಾ ಹಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಮಿಥುನನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪತ್ವಂ ಚ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ ತತ್ಕಥಮಿತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ತತ್ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ತದವಯವಯೋಃ ಅಯನಯೋಃ ತದ್ರೂಪತ್ವಂ ವಕ್ತುಂ ತಯೋಃ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಮಾಹ – ತಸ್ಯೇತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಿಮೇವ ಆಹ – ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಮಿತಿ ।

ಏವಮಪಿ ಕಥಂ ತಯೋಃ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಸ್ಯ ರಯಿತ್ವಂ ವಕ್ತುಂ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ರಯಿರೂಪಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತಕತ್ವಮಾಹ – ತತ್ತತ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಲೋಕಮಿತಿ ।

ಸೋಮರೂಪಂ ಶರೀರಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ತಸ್ಯ ಕರ್ಮಕೃತತ್ವಂ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸಾಧಯತಿ – ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ರಯಿರೂಪಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನದ್ವಾರಾ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಅಯನಸ್ಯ ತದಂತರ್ಭಾವ ಇತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ ತಸ್ಯ ಕರ್ಮಭಿಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯತ್ವಮಾಹ – ಯಸ್ಮಾದಿತಿ ।

ಏವಂ ಚ ತಸ್ಯ ರಯಿತ್ವಂ ಸಿದ್ಧಮಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಏಷ ಇತಿ ।

ಪಿತೃಯಾಣೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತ ಇತಿ ।

ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ತತಶ್ಚ ತದ್ವಿಶೇಷಣಸ್ಯ ಅಯನಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ರಯಿತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇದಾನೀಂ ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಮಾಹ – ಅಥೇತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪಾದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಸ್ಯ ತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಂ ಇತಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಂ ಇತಿ ತತ್ಕಾರ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಯುಕ್ತಮಿತಿ ಭಾವಃ ।

ಅಸ್ಯ ಕರ್ಮಸಾಧ್ಯಚಂದ್ರವೈಲಕ್ಷಣ್ಯಮಾಹ – ಏತದ್ವೈ ಇತಿ ।

ಇತರತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ಸಮಾನಮ್ ।

ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ನರ್ಥ ಇತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ವರೂಪ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ೧೦ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by noting that the word "atha" (now/next) signals the beginning of a new path — the Northern solstice-path — in contrast to the Southern path just described.

On the phrase "ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಯಾ" (knowledge directed at the Self of Prajāpati): Ānandagiri clarifies this means knowledge directed at identity with that (Prajāpati) — i.e., the realisation of non-difference (tādātmya).

On the phrase "they win the Sun" — Ānandagiri notes that the first occurrence of this phrase (in verse 9's context) was for the purpose of establishing the syntactic connection (anvaya); now in the Bhāṣya it appears again for the purpose of full explanation (vyākhyāna). These two uses should be distinguished.

On "sāmānya" (common/universal): Ānandagiri explains this means the Sun is the collective / aggregate form (samaṣṭirūpa) — i.e., the sum total of all prāṇas, not just one individual prāṇa.

On "vidyāvatām" (those who have knowledge): Ānandagiri explains this refers to those who are not qualified for ritual action — and precisely therefore are those who possess only upāsanā (meditation/contemplation) without the combination of ritual and knowledge.

On "karmiṇāṃ ca jñānavatām" (of those who combine action with knowledge): Ānandagiri explains this means those who have the combination (samuccaya) — i.e., those who unite both ritual action and knowledge.

Ānandagiri then raises and resolves an objection: one might ask — would not even the mere ritual performers (kevalakarmins) attain non-return once they reach the Sun? To forestall this, Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's sentence beginning "iti yasmāt" establishes that those people do not even reach the Sun at all. Therefore, the question of their non-return from the Sun does not even arise. The supplementary meaning is: "therefore, their (the kevalakarmins') attaining the Sun is not to be imagined."

Alternatively, Ānandagiri offers a second interpretation: the entire Śruti passage from "tasyāyane" (his two paths) through "eṣa nirodhaḥ" (this is the stopping) should be understood as aimed at establishing that the two ayanas are of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa respectively.

For this — the Bhāṣya must state that the Year is produced by the Rayi-Prāṇa pair and is itself of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa. The question "how so?" then arises.

To establish the Rayi-Prāṇa nature of the two ayanas — first the well-known fact about them is stated with "tasya" (his two paths). The well-known fact itself is then stated with "yābhyām" (by which two). Then the question of how even so the two ayanas can be of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa is raised with "katham?" (how?).

To establish that the Southern solstice is of the nature of Rayi — Śaṅkara states that for the ritual performers, the Moon (which is of the nature of Rayi) is produced (via the Southern path) — with "tat tatra." The word "lokam" means a body of the lunar nature (somarūpaṃ śarīram). That this body is produced by action is established through the fact of rebirth — with "kṛtarūpatvāt."

To establish that the Southern solstice is included within (antarabhāva) the Rayi-natured Moon (since that Moon is attained via the Southern path), Śaṅkara states that the Moon is attainable through action — with "yasmāt." And thus the Rayi-nature of the Southern solstice is established — with "eṣa" (this). The phrase "pitṛyāṇopalakaṣita" means "that which is attained through the Pitṛyāṇa" — and therefore the solstice that is its qualifier is also of the nature of Rayi.

Now, the Prāṇa-nature of the Northern solstice is stated with "atha" (now/next). Since the Northern solstice leads to the Prāṇa-natured Sun, it too is of the nature of Prāṇa. Thus the Year's being of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair is established, and it is reasonable that the Year should be a product (kārya) of that pair.

The difference between the Sun (attained by the Northern path) and the Moon (attained by action / the Southern path) is then stated with "etadvai" (this indeed). Everything else (the remaining analysis) is the same (as what was already covered).

Finally, on "asmin arthe" (in this matter): Ānandagiri explains this means "in the matter of the nature of the Saṃvatsara (Year)" — i.e., the śloka to follow is a Vedic verse that corroborates the entire analysis of the Year as Rayi-Prāṇa.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಅಥ ಇತಿ — with the word "atha (now)" ।

ಮಾರ್ಗಾಂತರ-ಆರಂಭ-ಅರ್ಥಃ — for the purpose of beginning a different / new path · ಅಥಶಬ್ದಃ — the word "atha" ।

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮವಿಷಯಾ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "directed at the Self of Prajāpati" ।

ತತ್ತಾದಾತ್ಮ್ಯ-ವಿಷಯಯಾ — directed at identity with that (Prajāpati) / aimed at non-difference with that · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "they win the Sun" · ಪೂರ್ವಂ — earlier / previously · ಅನ್ವಯಾರ್ಥಂ — for the purpose of syntactic connection (anvaya) · ಉಕ್ತಂ — was stated · ಇದಾನೀಂ — now · ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಾರ್ಥಂ — for the purpose of explanation · ಇತಿ — thus · ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಂ — should be understood / noted ।

ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯಂ ಇತಿ — on the word "common / universal" ।

ಸಮಷ್ಟಿರೂಪಂ — the collective / aggregate form · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ವಿದ್ಯಾವತಾಂ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "those who have knowledge" ।

ಕರ್ಮ-ಅನಧಿಕಾರಿಣಾಂ — of those not qualified for ritual action · ಅತ ಏವ — precisely therefore · ಕೇವಲ-ಉಪಾಸನವತಾಂ — of those who have only upāsanā (contemplation / meditation) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚ ಜ್ಞಾನವತಾಂ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "and of those who combine action with knowledge" ।

ಸಮುಚ್ಚಯವತಾಂ — of those who have the combination (of action and knowledge) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ನನು — now / but (objection marker) · ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಅಪಿ — even for the mere ritual performers · ಆದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೌ — upon attaining the Sun · ಅಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿಃ — non-return · ಭವಿಷ್ಯತಿ — will occur · ಇತಿ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this doubt · ತೇಷಾಂ — of those (kevalakarmins) · ಆದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿಃ ಏವ ನಾಸ್ತಿ — there is simply no attaining of the Sun · ಇತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to say this · ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ಇತಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the sentence beginning "iti eṣa" · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Ānandagiri) explains · ಇತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "iti yasmāt" ।

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — therefore · ತೇಷಾಂ — of those (kevalakarmins) · ಆದಿತ್ಯಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿಃ — the attaining of the Sun · ಅನಾಶಂಕ್ಯಾ — is not to be imagined / doubted · ಇತಿ ಶೇಷಃ — this is the supplementary (implied) meaning ।

ಯದ್ವಾ — or alternatively · ತಸ್ಯ ಅಯನೇ ಇತಿ ಆರಭ್ಯ — beginning from "his two paths" · ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ನಿರೋಧಃ ಇತ್ಯಂತಂ — up to and including "this is the nirodha (stopping)" · ಶ್ರುತಿ-ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the Śruti (Upaniṣad) sentence · ಅಯನಯೋಃ — of the two solstices · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದನ-ಪರತಯಾ — with the intent of establishing the Rayi-nature and Prāṇa-nature · ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯೇಯಂ — should be interpreted ।

ತಥಾ ಹಿ — for this is so ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇ — in the matter of its being produced by the Rayi-Prāṇa pair · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪತ್ವಂ ಚ — and its being of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa · ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ — needs to be stated · ತತ್ ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ — thus raises the question "how so?" · ತತ್ ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the words "how so?" ।

ತದ್-ಅವಯವಯೋಃ — of those two parts / components · ಅಯನಯೋಃ — of the two solstices · ತದ್ರೂಪತ್ವಂ — being of that nature (Rayi/Prāṇa) · ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to state · ತಯೋಃ — of those two · ಪ್ರಥಮಂ — first · ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಂ — the well-known (fact) · ಆಹ — states · ತಸ್ಯ ಇತಿ — with the word "tasya (his)" ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಿಂ ಏವ ಆಹ — states only the well-known fact · ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "yābhyām (by which two)" ।

ಏವಂ ಅಪಿ — even so · ಕಥಂ — how · ತಯೋಃ — of those two · ತದಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಂ — being of the nature of that (Rayi/Prāṇa) · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus raises · ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "katham (how?)" ।

ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಸ್ಯ — of the Southern solstice · ರಯಿತ್ವಂ — the Rayi-nature · ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to state · ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ — for those who perform ritual action · ರಯಿರೂಪ-ಚಂದ್ರ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತಕತ್ವಂ — the quality of producing the Rayi-natured Moon · ಆಹ — states · ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the words "tat tatra" ।

ಲೋಕಂ ಇತಿ — on the word "loka (world / realm)" ।

ಸೋಮರೂಪಂ ಶರೀರಂ — a body of the lunar / soma nature · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ತಸ್ಯ — of that (lunar body/world) · ಕರ್ಮಕೃತತ್ವಂ — the quality of being produced by action · ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತ್ಯಾ — through (the fact of) rebirth · ಸಾಧಯತಿ — establishes / proves · ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of having the character of the accomplished" ।

ರಯಿರೂಪಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ — of the Rayi-natured Moon · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the Southern solstice · ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being attainable · ತಸ್ಯ ಅಯನಸ್ಯ — of that solstice · ತದಂತರ್ಭಾವಃ — inclusion within that (Rayi-nature) · ಇತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to say this · ತಸ್ಯ — of that (Moon) · ಕರ್ಮಭಿಃ — through actions · ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯತ್ವಂ — attainability · ಆಹ — states · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the word "yasmāt (because)" ।

ಏವಂ ಚ — and thus · ತಸ್ಯ — of that (Southern solstice) · ರಯಿತ್ವಂ — the Rayi-nature · ಸಿದ್ಧಂ — established · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus states · ಏಷ ಇತಿ — with the word "eṣa (this)" ।

ಪಿತೃಯಾಣ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "indicated / characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa" ।

ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ — that which is attained through it (the Pitṛyāṇa) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ತತಃ ಚ — and therefore · ತದ್-ವಿಶೇಷಣಸ್ಯ — of the qualifier (Pitṛyāṇa) · ಅಯನಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — of the solstice as well · ರಯಿತ್ವಂ — the Rayi-nature · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಇದಾನೀಂ — now · ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಸ್ಯ — of the Northern solstice · ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಂ — the Prāṇa-nature · ಆಹ — states · ಅಥ ಇತಿ — with the word "atha (now)" ।

ಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪ-ಆದಿತ್ಯ-ಪ್ರಾಪಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because it leads to / produces the Prāṇa-natured Sun · ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಸ್ಯ — of the Northern solstice · ತಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — that too · ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಂ — is of the nature of Prāṇa · ಇತಿ — thus · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಂ — being of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair · ಇತಿ — thus · ತತ್ಕಾರ್ಯತ್ವಂ — its being a product of that pair · ಯುಕ್ತಂ — is reasonable / justified · ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ — this is the import ।

ಅಸ್ಯ — of this (Sun) · ಕರ್ಮಸಾಧ್ಯ-ಚಂದ್ರ-ವೈಲಕ್ಷಣ್ಯಂ — the distinction from the action-produced Moon · ಆಹ — states · ಏತದ್ವೈ ಇತಿ — with the words "etadvai (this indeed)" ।

ಇತರತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸಮಾನಂ — everything else (in the analysis) is the same (as already covered) ।

ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಅರ್ಥೇ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "in this matter" ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಸ್ವರೂಪ ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — the meaning is "in the matter of the nature of the Saṃvatsara (Year)" ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) States the Northern path — through austerity, brahmacarya, faith, and knowledge — by which the knower wins the Sun and does not return ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Unpacks the means (austerity as sense-conquest; knowledge as realisation of identity with Prajāpati's Self); distinguishes the Sun as immortal, fearless, and the supreme goal from the Moon; explains nirodha as the Sun's dual function — liberation for knowers, a barrier for the ignorant ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Clarifies atha as marking the new path; tādātmya as the content of vidyā; samaṣṭirūpa as the meaning of sāmānya; resolves the objection about kevalakarmins and non-return; offers two alternative interpretations of the entire Śruti passage; establishes the Prāṇa-nature of the Northern solstice in parallel with the Rayi-nature of the Southern solstice already shown in verse 9

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The Northern path (Uttarāyaṇa / Devayāna) is for those who combine austerity, brahmacarya, faith, and knowledge — specifically knowledge of identity with Prajāpati's Self (aham asmi — "I am That").
  2. The Sun (Āditya) is the Prāṇa-aspect of Prajāpati — immortal, fearless, the common ground (samaṣṭi) of all prāṇas — in contrast to the Moon which is finite, waxing and waning, and subject to decay.
  3. Nirodha (stopping) operates at two levels: for the knower it is the final end of transmigration; for the ignorant the Sun functions as a barrier — they are held back at the Sun and do not even reach it, let alone transcend it.
  4. Ānandagiri's key contribution here is the systematic parallel: just as verse 9 established the Rayi-nature of the Southern solstice (through the Moon), verse 10 establishes the Prāṇa-nature of the Northern solstice (through the Sun) — completing the proof that the Year as a whole is of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair.
  5. The word "atha" is not merely transitional — Ānandagiri shows it structurally marks the shift from the Rayi-analysis to the Prāṇa-analysis, mirroring the structure of Prajāpati's dyadic nature.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಪಂಚಪಾದಂ ಪಿತರಂ ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಂ ದಿವ ಆಹುಃ ಪರೇ ಅರ್ಧೇ ಪುರೀಷಿಣಮ್ ।

ಅಥೇಮೇ ಅನ್ಯ ಉ ಪರೇ ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ ಷಡರ ಆಹುರರ್ಪಿತಮಿತಿ ॥ ೧೧ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Some knowers of Time call him (the Year / Prajāpati) five-footed, the Father, twelve-formed, full of water (pūrīṣin) — placed in the higher half, beyond the sky.

And then these others, equally learned, call him the all-discerning one — placed (as the entire world) in the wheel of seven horses, having six spokes.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಪಂಚಪಾದಂ — five-footed (having five seasons as feet) · ಪಿತರಂ — the Father (progenitor of all) · ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಂ — twelve-formed (having twelve months as forms/limbs) · ದಿವಃ — from / beyond the sky · ಪರೇ — in the higher · ಅರ್ಧೇ — half / region · ಪುರೀಷಿಣಂ — full of water / nourishment · ಆಹುಃ — they call / say ।

ಅಥ — and now / moreover · ಇಮೇ — these · ಅನ್ಯೇ — others · ಉ — also / but (particle) · ಪರೇ — other (equally learned) knowers · ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ — all-discerning / omniscient · ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ — in the wheel of seven (horses / spokes) · ಷಡರೇ — having six spokes (six seasons) · ಆಹುಃ — they say / describe · ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ — placed / fixed (as spokes in a hub) · ಇತಿ — thus ॥

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಪಂಚಪಾದಂ ಪಂಚ ಋತವಃ ಪಾದಾ ಇವಾಸ್ಯ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ಮನ ಆದಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯ, ತೈರ್ಹ್ಯಸೌ ಪಾದೈರಿವ ಋತುಭಿರಾವರ್ತತೇ ।

ಹೇಮಂತಶಿಶಿರಾವೇಕೀಕೃತ್ಯ ಇಯಂ ಕಲ್ಪನಾ ।

ಪಿತರಂ ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಜನಯಿತೃತ್ವಾತ್ಪಿತೃತ್ವಂ ತಸ್ಯ ; ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಂ ದ್ವಾದಶ ಮಾಸಾ ಆಕೃತಯೋಽವಯವಾ ಆಕರಣಂ ವಾ ಅವಯವಿಕರಣಮಸ್ಯ ದ್ವಾದಶಮಾಸೈಃ ತಂ ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಮ್ ।

ದಿವಃ ದ್ಯುಲೋಕಾತ್ ಪರೇ ಊರ್ಧ್ವೇ ಅರ್ಧೇ ಸ್ಥಾನೇ ತೃತೀಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ದಿವೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ; ಪುರೀಷಿಣಂ ಪುರೀಷವಂತಮ್ ಉದಕವಂತಮ್ ಆಹುಃ ಕಾಲವಿದಃ ।

ಅಥ ತಮೇವಾನ್ಯೇ ಇಮೇ ಉ ಪರೇ ಕಾಲವಿದಃ ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ ನಿಪುಣಂ ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಂ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ ಸಪ್ತಹಯರೂಪೇ ಚಕ್ರೇ ಸಂತತಗತಿಮತಿ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮನಿ ಷಡರೇ ಷಡೃತುಮತಿ ಆಹುಃ ಸರ್ವಮಿದಂ ಜಗತ್ಕಥಯಂತಿ — ಅರ್ಪಿತಮ್ ಅರಾ ಇವ ರಥನಾಭೌ ನಿವಿಷ್ಟಮಿತಿ ।

ಯದಿ ಪಂಚಪಾದೋ ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿರ್ಯದಿ ವಾ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರಃ ಷಡರಃ ಸರ್ವಥಾಪಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಶ್ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಲಕ್ಷಣೋ ಜಗತಃ ಕಾರಣಮ್ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Five-footed: the five seasons are like the five feet of the Year-natured Sun (Āditya); for by them — by the seasons, as if by feet — he moves / revolves. This reckoning is made by treating Hemanta (early winter) and Śiśira (late winter) as one.

The Father: his fatherhood comes from being the generator of all. Twelve-formed: the twelve months are his forms / limbs — or alternatively, the twelve months are the instruments by which he is constituted as a whole. Thus he is twelve-formed.

Beyond the sky: he is in the higher, upward region — in the third heaven (beyond the sky-world). Full of water (pūrīṣiṇ): full of nourishment, full of water. Thus the knowers of Time describe him.

And now these other equally learned knowers of Time describe that same one as all-discerning, omniscient — placed in the wheel of seven horses (seven-spoked), which has continuous motion and is of the nature of Time — in the six-spoked (six-seasoned) one. They say all this world is placed in him — fixed like spokes in the hub of a chariot-wheel.

Whether five-footed and twelve-formed, or seven-wheeled and six-spoked — in every way the Year, whose nature is Time, is Prajāpati characterised by Moon and Sun, and is the cause of the world.

docs.text:

ಹೇಮಂತಶಿಶಿರೌ — Hemanta (early winter) and Śiśira (late winter) · ಏಕೀಕೃತ್ಯ — having combined / treated as one · ಇಯಂ ಕಲ್ಪನಾ — this reckoning / this convention ।

ಪಿತರಂ — the Father · ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ — of all · ಜನಯಿತೃತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being the generator / progenitor · ಪಿತೃತ್ವಂ — fatherhood · ತಸ್ಯ — his · ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಂ — twelve-formed · ದ್ವಾದಶ ಮಾಸಾಃ — the twelve months · ಆಕೃತಯಃ — forms / shapes · ಅವಯವಾಃ — limbs / parts · ಆಕರಣಂ ವಾ — or alternatively the instrument of constitution · ಅವಯವಿಕರಣಂ — being constituted through its limbs · ಅಸ್ಯ — of him · ದ್ವಾದಶಮಾಸೈಃ — by the twelve months · ತಂ — him · ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿಂ — twelve-formed ।

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
This verse has one sentence requiring explicit anvaya treatment, flagged by Ānandagiri, and one compound requiring grammatical disambiguation.

Sentence 1 — The second school of knowers (the "saptacakra" view)

As written:

ಅಥ ತಮೇವ ಅನ್ಯೇ ಇಮೇ ಉ ಪರೇ ಕಾಲವಿದಃ ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ ನಿಪುಣಂ ಸರ್ವಜ್ಞಂ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ ಸಪ್ತಹಯರೂಪೇ ಚಕ್ರೇ ಸಂತತಗತಿಮತಿ ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮನಿ ಷಡರೇ ಷಡೃತುಮತಿ ಆಹುಃ ಸರ್ವಮಿದಂ ಜಗತ್ಕಥಯಂತಿ — ಅರ್ಪಿತಮ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಅಥ [ಪರೇ ಕಾಲವಿದಃ] ಇಮೇ ಅನ್ಯೇ ಉ ಪರೇ [ಏವ] — [ತೇ] ತಂ ಏವ [ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ] ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ [ಇತಿ] ಆಹುಃ ।

[ಕಿಂ ಚ ?] ಸರ್ವಂ ಇದಂ ಜಗತ್ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ ಷಡರೇ [ಕಾಲಾತ್ಮನಿ] ಅರಾ ಇವ ರಥನಾಭೌ ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ [ಇತಿ] ಕಥಯಂತಿ ।

English: And now these other equally learned knowers of Time — they call that very same (Year) all-discerning. And moreover they say that all this world is fixed in the seven-wheeled, six-spoked (Year / Time), like spokes in the hub of a wheel.

Note: The particle "u" (ಉ) is glossed by Ānandagiri as equivalent to "tu" — marking a contrast or addition between the two schools of knowers. The two verbs ಆಹುಃ and ಕಥಯಂತಿ are near-synonyms here — Ānandagiri treats them as a hendiadys expressing the one act of description. The locatives ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರೇ and ಷಡರೇ are both predicates of ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ, not separate finite clauses.

Compound disambiguation — ದ್ವಾದಶಾಕೃತಿ

Śaṅkara offers two grammatical analyses of this compound:

Analysis 1 (samānādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi): The twelve months are his forms / limbs (ākṛtayaḥ = avayavāḥ) — he who has twelve months as his forms.

Analysis 2 (vyādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi): The twelve months are the instruments of his constitution (ākaraṇam = avayavī-karaṇam) — he who is constituted by / through twelve months as his limbs. In both analyses the referent and the final meaning are the same: the Year whose body is made of twelve months.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಇಯಂ ಕಲ್ಪನಾ ಇತಿ ।

ಪಂಚಧಾ ಕರ್ಮಸಾಧ್ಯಚಂದ್ರವೈಲಕ್ಷಣ್ಯಕಲ್ಪನಾ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಜನಯಿತೃತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ಮಕಕಾಲಸ್ಯ ಸರ್ವಜನಕತ್ವಾದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಸಮಾನಾಧಿಕರಣಬಹುವ್ರೀಹಿತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾಯ ವ್ಯಾಧಿಕರಣಬಹುವ್ರೀಹಿರ್ವೇತ್ಯಾಹ – ಆಕರಣಂ ವೇತಿ ।

ಅವಯವಿಕರಣಮಿತಿ ।

ಅವಯವಿತ್ವೇನ ಕರಣಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಪಕ್ಷದ್ವಯೇಽಪ್ಯೇಕ ಏವಾರ್ಥಃ ।

ದ್ಯುಲೋಕಾದಿತಿ ।

ಆಕಾಶರೂಪಾದಂತರಿಕ್ಷಲೋಕಾದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅನ್ಯಥಾ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಲೋಕಾತ್ಪರಸ್ಯ ಚತುರ್ಥತ್ವೇನ ತೃತೀಯಸ್ಯಾಮಿತ್ಯನನ್ವಯಾಪತ್ತೇಃ ।

ಉದಕವಂತಮಿತಿ ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಾಜ್ಜಾಯತೇ ವೃಷ್ಟಿರಿತಿ ಸ್ಮೃತೇರಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅನ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪೂರ್ವಾರ್ಧಗತೇನ ಆಹುರಿತ್ಯನೇನ ಸಂಬಂಧಃ ।

ಉ ಇತಿ ತುಶಬ್ದಸಮಾನಾರ್ಥಃ ನಿಪಾತಃ ।

ಪರೇ ತು ತಮೇವ ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಮಾಹುಃ ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಕಿಮಾಹುಃ ಇತ್ಯತ ಆಹ – ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರ ಇತಿ ।

ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣೇ ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕೇ ಸರ್ವಮಿದಂ ಜಗತ್ ಅರ್ಪಿತಮಿತ್ಯಾಹುಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಮತದ್ವಯೇಽಪಿ ಕೀದೃಶಃ ಅರ್ಥಭೇದಃ ಇತ್ಯತ ಆಹ – ಯದೀತಿ ।

ಪೂರ್ವಮತೇ ಋತೂನಾಂ ಪಾದತ್ವಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ ಮಾಸಾನಾಂ ಅವಯವತ್ವಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲ ಏವ ಉಕ್ತಃ ।

ದ್ವಿತೀಯೇ ತು ಹೇಮಂತಶಿಶಿರೌ ಪೃಥಕ್ಕೃತ್ಯ ಷಣ್ಣಾಂ ಋತೂನಾಂ ಅರತ್ವಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಪರಿವರ್ತನಗುಣಯೋಗೇನ ಚಕ್ರತ್ವಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ ಕಾಲಪ್ರಾಧಾನ್ಯೇನ ಸರ್ವಾಶ್ರಯತ್ವೇನ ಚ ಸ ಏವ ಉಕ್ತಃ ।

ಪಕ್ಷದ್ವಯೇಽಪಿ ಗುಣಭೇದೇನ ಕಲ್ಪನಾಭೇದೇನ ಚ ಭೇದಃ ನ ಧರ್ಮಿಭೇದಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ೧೧ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
On the phrase "this reckoning" (iyaṃ kalpanā): Ānandagiri explains this means the five-fold reckoning — the convention that distinguishes the Sun (Year) from the action-produced Moon by casting the seasons as its five feet.

On "because of being the generator" (janayitṛtvāt): Ānandagiri clarifies that the meaning is — because the Year-natured Time is the progenitor of all (sarvajanakatva).

On the compound "dvādaśākṛti" — Śaṅkara first analyses it as a samānādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi (appositional compound), then offers a vyādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi (non-appositional compound) as an alternative — with the words "ākaraṇaṃ vā" (or alternatively, the instrument of constitution). On the second analysis, "ākaraṇam" means "avayavī-karaṇam" — being constituted through its limbs. In both analyses, the meaning is the same.

On "dyulokāt" (from the sky-world): Ānandagiri explains this means from the sky-world that is of the nature of the ākāśa (space) — i.e., the antarikṣa (mid-region). Otherwise, if it meant from the svarga (heaven), then "beyond it" would make the Sun the fourth (world), which would contradict the statement "in the third heaven" — hence an anvaya-fault would result.

On "udakavantam" (full of water): Ānandagiri explains this rests on the Smṛti statement — "from the Sun rain is born" — hence the Sun is the source of water and is called water-full.

On the syntactic connection of "anye" (others): the word "anye" (in the second half) connects with the verb "āhuḥ" from the first half of the verse. The particle "u" is glossed as a nipāta equivalent in meaning to "tu" (but / moreover). The syntactic connection (anvaya) is: "the others (pāre), however, call that same one all-discerning (vicakṣaṇam)."

To the question "what do they call it?" — Ānandagiri answers: with the words "saptacakra." The meaning is: in that all-discerning one of the nature of the seven-wheeled etc., all this world is said to be fixed (arpitam).

On the question of what exactly differs between the two views — Ānandagiri answers with "yadi" (whether). In the first view (pūrvamata), the Year as Time is described through the Sun-nature — by the convention of the seasons as feet and the months as limbs. In the second view, Hemanta and Śiśira are separated out, the six seasons are treated as spokes (aras), the Year is treated as a wheel by virtue of its quality of revolution (parivartana), and that same Year is described with Time as primary and with the quality of being the support of all (sarvāśrayatva). In both views the difference is only in the quality (guṇa) and in the convention (kalpanā) — there is no difference in the subject (dharmin) itself.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಇಯಂ ಕಲ್ಪನಾ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "this reckoning / convention" ।

ಪಂಚಧಾ — five-fold · ಕರ್ಮಸಾಧ್ಯ-ಚಂದ್ರ-ವೈಲಕ್ಷಣ್ಯ-ಕಲ್ಪನಾ — the convention of distinguishing (the Sun) from the action-produced Moon by five (feet / seasons) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಜನಯಿತೃತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — on the phrase "because of being the generator" ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ಮಕ-ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ — of the Year-natured Time · ಸರ್ವಜನಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being the progenitor of all · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಸಮಾನಾಧಿಕರಣ-ಬಹುವ್ರೀಹಿ-ತಯಾ — as a samānādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi (appositional compound) · ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾಯ — having explained / analysed · ವ್ಯಾಧಿಕರಣ-ಬಹುವ್ರೀಹಿಃ ವಾ — or alternatively a vyādhikaraṇa bahuvrīhi (non-appositional compound) · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus states · ಆಕರಣಂ ವಾ ಇತಿ — with the words "or the instrument of constitution" ।

ಅವಯವಿಕರಣಂ ಇತಿ — on the word "avayavī-karaṇam" ।

ಅವಯವಿತ್ವೇನ ಕರಣಂ — being constituted through its parts / by functioning as a limb-whole · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಪಕ್ಷದ್ವಯೇ ಅಪಿ — in both analyses / both alternatives · ಏಕಃ ಏವ ಅರ್ಥಃ — the meaning is one and the same ।

ದ್ಯುಲೋಕಾತ್ ಇತಿ — on the word "dyulokāt (from the sky-world)" ।

ಆಕಾಶರೂಪಾತ್ — from that which is of the nature of ākāśa (space) · ಅಂತರಿಕ್ಷಲೋಕಾತ್ — from the mid-region (antarikṣa) · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಅನ್ಯಥಾ — otherwise · ಸ್ವರ್ಗಲೋಕಾತ್ ಪರಸ್ಯ — of what is beyond the svarga (heaven) · ಚತುರ್ಥತ್ವೇನ — as the fourth (world) · ತೃತೀಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ಇತಿ — the statement "in the third (heaven)" · ಅನನ್ವಯ-ಆಪತ್ತೇಃ — because of the resulting anvaya-fault (syntactic inconsistency) ।

ಉದಕವಂತಂ ಇತಿ — on the word "udakavantam (full of water)" ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ ಜಾಯತೇ ವೃಷ್ಟಿಃ — from the Sun rain is born · ಇತಿ ಸ್ಮೃತೇಃ — because of this Smṛti statement · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಅನ್ಯ ಇತಿ ಅಸ್ಯ — of the word "anye (others)" · ಪೂರ್ವಾರ್ಧಗತೇನ — occurring in the first half (of the verse) · ಆಹುಃ ಇತಿ ಅನೇನ — with the verb "āhuḥ (they say)" · ಸಂಬಂಧಃ — is the syntactic connection ।

ಉ ಇತಿ — the particle "u" · ತುಶಬ್ದ-ಸಮಾನಾರ್ಥಃ — equivalent in meaning to "tu (but / moreover)" · ನಿಪಾತಃ — is an indeclinable particle ।

ಪರೇ ತು — the others however · ತಂ ಏವ — that very same (one) · ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣಂ — as all-discerning · ಆಹುಃ — call / say · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಕಿಂ ಆಹುಃ — what do they say? · ಇತ್ಯತಃ ಆಹ — to this (Ānandagiri) answers · ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the word "saptacakra (seven-wheeled)" ।

ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ — in that · ವಿಚಕ್ಷಣೇ — all-discerning one · ಸಪ್ತಚಕ್ರ-ಆದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕೇ — of the nature of the seven-wheeled etc. · ಸರ್ವಂ ಇದಂ ಜಗತ್ — all this world · ಅರ್ಪಿತಂ — is placed / fixed · ಇತಿ ಆಹುಃ — they say · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಮತದ್ವಯೇ ಅಪಿ — even in both views / schools · ಕೀದೃಶಃ — what kind of · ಅರ್ಥಭೇದಃ — difference in meaning · ಇತ್ಯತಃ ಆಹ — to this (Ānandagiri) answers · ಯದಿ ಇತಿ — with the word "yadi (whether)" ।

ಪೂರ್ವಮತೇ — in the first view · ಋತೂನಾಂ — of the seasons · ಪಾದತ್ವ-ಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ — through the convention of treating them as feet · ಮಾಸಾನಾಂ — of the months · ಅವಯವತ್ವ-ಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ — through the convention of treating them as limbs · ಆದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾ — through the Sun-nature · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — the Year · ಕಾಲಃ ಏವ — Time itself · ಉಕ್ತಃ — is described ।

ದ್ವಿತೀಯೇ ತು — in the second view however · ಹೇಮಂತಶಿಶಿರೌ — Hemanta and Śiśira (the two winter seasons) · ಪೃಥಕ್ಕೃತ್ಯ — having separated out · ಷಣ್ಣಾಂ ಋತೂನಾಂ — of the six seasons · ಅರತ್ವ-ಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ — through the convention of treating them as spokes · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ಪರಿವರ್ತನ-ಗುಣ-ಯೋಗೇನ — through the quality of revolution / rotation · ಚಕ್ರತ್ವ-ಕಲ್ಪನಯಾ — through the convention of treating it as a wheel · ಕಾಲ-ಪ್ರಾಧಾನ್ಯೇನ — with Time as primary · ಸರ್ವಾಶ್ರಯತ್ವೇನ ಚ — and with the quality of being the support of all · ಸಃ ಏವ — that very same (Year) · ಉಕ್ತಃ — is described ।

ಪಕ್ಷದ್ವಯೇ ಅಪಿ — in both views too · ಗುಣಭೇದೇನ — by difference in attribute / quality · ಕಲ್ಪನಾಭೇದೇನ ಚ — and by difference in convention · ಭೇದಃ — the difference (between them) · ನ ಧರ್ಮಿಭೇದಃ — is not a difference in the subject (dharmin) itself · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Verse (śloka / mantra) cited by Śaṅkara as Vedic authority for the Year as Prajāpati; presents two schools of Time-knowers — one describing the Year as five-footed and twelve-formed, the other as seven-wheeled and six-spoked ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Glosses each epithet of the verse; resolves the apparent contradiction between the two schools by showing both describe the same Year-as-Prajāpati; closes with the summary statement that in any case the Year is the cause of the world ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Disambiguates the grammar of dvādaśākṛti (two bahuvrīhi analyses); resolves the locative "dyulokāt" as antarikṣa not svarga (to avoid an anvaya-fault); glosses "u" as equivalent to "tu"; shows the two schools differ only in convention and quality, not in their subject

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The verse is a śloka cited as Vedic authority (mantra) to support the Bhāṣya's analysis — specifically to corroborate that the Saṃvatsara (Year) is Prajāpati and the cause of the world.
  2. Two schools of Time-knowers describe the Year using different conventions — five-fold (pañcapāda / dvādaśākṛti) and six-fold (saptacakra / ṣaḍara) — but both identify the same entity.
  3. The difference between the two conventions is in guṇa (attribute) and kalpanā (convention of description) only — not in the dharmin (the subject being described). This is Ānandagiri's key clarification.
  4. Hemanta and Śiśira are the pivotal difference: the first school merges them into one season (giving five seasons / five feet); the second school separates them (giving six seasons / six spokes).
  5. The closing Bhāṣya statement ties the verse back to the argument of the entire first question: the Year — whether five-footed or seven-wheeled — is characterised by Moon and Sun (Rayi and Prāṇa) and is the cause of the world.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text: ಮಾಸೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಶುಕ್ಲ ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತೀತರ ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ ॥ ೧೨ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Month (Māsa) is indeed Prajāpati. Of it, the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇapakṣa) is Rayi (the material principle) and the bright fortnight (śuklapakṣa) is Prāṇa (the life-force). Therefore these seers perform their sacrificial rites in the bright (fortnight); the others perform in the other (the dark fortnight).
