docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನಿದಂ ಪ್ರೋತಂ ವಿಶ್ವಂ ಸ ಏವ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾಖ್ಯಃ ಸ್ವಾವಯವೇ ಮಾಸೇ ಕೃತ್ಸ್ನಃ ಪರಿಸಮಾಪ್ಯತೇ ।

ಮಾಸೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಲಕ್ಷಣ ಏವ ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ।

ತಸ್ಯ ಮಾಸಾತ್ಮನಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರೇಕೋ ಭಾಗಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ ಅಪರೋ ಭಾಗಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಆದಿತ್ಯೋಽತ್ತಾಗ್ನಿಃ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇಽಪೀಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ತೈರ್ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ;

ಇತರೇ ತು ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತೀತ್ಯದರ್ಶನಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಕೃಷ್ಣಾತ್ಮಾನಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ ।

ಇತರೇ ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
That very Prajāpati, named the Saṃvatsara (Year), in whom all this world is strung — he is completely contained within his own limb, the Month (Māsa).

The Month is indeed Prajāpati — with exactly the characteristics as described (the Year), and of the dyadic nature (mithunātmaka — of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa).

Of that Prajāpati whose nature is the Month, one portion is the dark fortnight — which is Rayi, food, the Moon; the other portion is the bright — the bright fortnight — which is Prāṇa, the Sun, the eater, the fire.

Because these seers see all as Prāṇa — as the one who is the Self of the bright fortnight — therefore, these seers who are perceivers of Prāṇa, even when performing their sacrificial rites (iṣṭa / yāga) in the dark fortnight, perform them in the bright fortnight alone.

For by them, the dark fortnight is not seen as anything apart from Prāṇa.

The others, however, not seeing Prāṇa — they see only what is of the nature of darkness (non-perceiving, kṛṣṇa).

The others perform in the dark fortnight alone — even when performing in the bright.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
Two sentences in this Bhāṣya require explicit anvaya treatment.

Sentence 1 — Seers perform in the bright even when in the dark

As written:

ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಛುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇಽಪಿ ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಪ್ರಾಣದರ್ಶಿನಃ [ಸಂತಃ] — ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ-ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ಅಪಿ ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಯಾಗಂ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ [ಅಪಿ] ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

English: These seers, being perceivers of Prāṇa — because they see Prāṇa (whose Self is the bright fortnight) as everything — therefore, even while performing the sacrifice in the dark fortnight, they perform in the bright fortnight alone.

Note: The yasmat…tasmāt (because…therefore) frame spans the entire sentence. The participial ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ (while performing) and the finite verb ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ (they perform) are both needed — one states the physical occasion (dark fortnight), the other states the ontological reality (bright fortnight). Ānandagiri flags this as the core anvaya difficulty.

Sentence 2 — Others perform in the dark even when in the bright

As written:

ಇತರೇ ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಇತರೇ [ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಃ] — ಶುಕ್ಲೇ [ಪಕ್ಷೇ] ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — ಇತರಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ।

English: The others — not seeing Prāṇa — even while performing in the bright fortnight, perform in the dark fortnight alone.

Note: This sentence is the exact parallel and inversion of Sentence 1 — same structure (participial + finite verb), opposite result. Ānandagiri's Ṭīkā makes the symmetry explicit: just as knowledge transforms dark into bright for the seers, ignorance transforms bright into dark for the others.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಕಾರಣತ್ವೇ ಶ್ಲೋಕೋಕ್ತಂ ಜಗದಾಶ್ರಯತ್ವಂ ಹೇತುಮಾಹ – ಯಸ್ಮಿನ್ನಿತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಮಾಸಾಹೋರಾತ್ರರೂಪವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಔಷಧ್ಯಾದಿಜನಕತ್ವಾಭಾವಾತ್ ತಸ್ಯ ಮಾಸಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಮಾಹ – ಸ ಏವೇತಿ ।

ಯಥೋಕ್ತೇತಿ ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರರೂಪಃ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಶುಕ್ಲಕೃಷ್ಣಯೋಃ ಉಭಯೋಃ ಅಪಿ ದರ್ಶಪೂರ್ಣಮಾಸಾದಿಕರ್ಮಾನುಷ್ಠಾನದರ್ಶನಾತ್ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಅನುಪಪನ್ನಮ್ ಇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಶುಕ್ಲಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ತುತಿಪರತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಯಸ್ಮಾದಿತಿ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಸರ್ವಮೇವ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಮೇವ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ ಯಸ್ಮಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಃ ತೈಃ ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಾದಿಸರ್ವಜಗತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣದ್ವಾರಾ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷತ್ವೇ ಸತಿ ಕೃಷ್ಣೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಾತ್ಮಕೇ ಶುಕ್ಲ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಇತಿ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ಯ ಸ್ತುತಿಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಏತತ್ ಸ್ತುತ್ಯರ್ಥಮೇವ ಜ್ಞಾನರಹಿತಾನ್ ನಿಂದತಿ – ಇತರೇ ತ್ವಿತಿ ।

ಯೇ ತು ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತ್ಯಜ್ಞತ್ವಾತ್ ತೇಷಾಂ ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವೇನ ಅಜ್ಞಾಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಸನ್ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷತ್ವಮಾಪದ್ಯತೇ ಅತಃ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತೋಽಪಿ ಅದರ್ಶನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಕಾಶರಹಿತೇ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಏವ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ ಇತಿ ತೇ ನಿಂದ್ಯಂತೇ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಉಕ್ತಮರ್ಥಂ ಶ್ರುತ್ಯಾ ಆರೂಢಂ ಕರೋತಿ – ಇತರ ಇತಿ ॥ ೧೨ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by saying that Śaṅkara, in order to state the reason for the world-support (jagadāśrayatva) mentioned in the śloka as proof of causality (kāraṇatva), begins with "yasmin" (in whom).

Then, to show that the Year too — without the Month, day, and night — has no capacity to produce herbs etc., and therefore the Year is of the nature of the Month etc., Śaṅkara says "sa eva" (that very one). On "yathoktam" (as described): Ānandagiri explains this means "of the form of the Year, of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair."

Ānandagiri then raises an objection: since we see the performance of darśa- pūrṇamāsa (fortnightly sacrificial rites) and other rites in both the bright and dark fortnights, the Śruti statement "therefore these seers perform in the bright" would be contradicted — it would be inconsistent (anupapanna). To resolve this, Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's passage beginning "yasmāt" is aimed at praising the knowledge that the bright fortnight is the Self of Prāṇa — not at making a purely factual claim about when rites are performed.

The anvaya is: because (yasmāt) they see Prāṇa as everything, as the Self of all, and because (yasmāt) the dark fortnight is not seen by them as anything apart from Prāṇa — therefore (tasmāt) they perform in the bright alone.

Since Prāṇa is of the nature of the bright fortnight, and since all the world including the dark fortnight is of the nature of Prāṇa — through Prāṇa, the dark fortnight too becomes bright. Therefore those performing in the dark are actually performing in the bright (light-natured) alone. This is the praise (stuti) of the knowledge that the bright fortnight is Prāṇa.

For the very purpose of this praise, Śaṅkara censures those who lack this knowledge — with the words "itare tu" (the others however). Those who do not see Prāṇa as the Self of all — because they do not know the bright fortnight as Prāṇa, their bright fortnight becomes of the nature of ignorance and takes on the quality of the dark fortnight. Therefore even while performing in the bright, they perform in the dark (lightless) alone — and thus they are censured.

Finally, Ānandagiri says Śaṅkara then establishes the stated meaning through the Śruti itself — with "itara" (the other / dark fortnight).

docs.text:

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the Year · ಮಾಸಾಹೋರಾತ್ರರೂಪ-ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ — without (apart from) the Month and day-and-night form · ಔಷಧ್ಯಾದಿ-ಜನಕತ್ವ-ಅಭಾವಾತ್ — because of the absence of the capacity to produce herbs etc. · ತಸ್ಯ — of it (the Year) · ಮಾಸಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಂ — being of the nature of the Month etc. · ಆಹ — states · ಸ ಏವ ಇತಿ — with the words "sa eva (that very one)" ।

ಯಥೋಕ್ತ ಇತಿ — on the word "yathoktam (as described)" ।

ಸಂವತ್ಸರರೂಪಃ — of the form of the Year · ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಃ — of the nature of the Rayi-Prāṇa pair · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಶುಕ್ಲಕೃಷ್ಣಯೋಃ ಉಭಯೋಃ ಅಪಿ — in both the bright and dark (fortnights) · ದರ್ಶಪೂರ್ಣಮಾಸಾದಿ-ಕರ್ಮ-ಅನುಷ್ಠಾನ-ದರ್ಶನಾತ್ — because of observing the performance of darśa-pūrṇamāsa and other rites · ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the statement "therefore these seers" · ಅನುಪಪನ್ನಂ — inconsistent / contradicted · ಇತಿ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this objection · ಶುಕ್ಲಸ್ಯ — of the bright (fortnight) · ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವ-ಜ್ಞಾನ-ಸ್ತುತಿ-ಪರತಯಾ — with the intent of praising the knowledge that (the bright) is the Self of Prāṇa · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the word "yasmāt (because)" ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ — because · ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa · ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ — as everything · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಏವ — as the Self of all · ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — they see · ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಚ — and because · ಪ್ರಾಣ-ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕೇಣ — apart from Prāṇa · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಃ — the dark fortnight · ತೈಃ — by them · ನ ದೃಶ್ಯತೇ — is not seen · ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ — therefore · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ — of Prāṇa · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷ-ಆತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of the bright fortnight · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಾದಿ-ಸರ್ವಜಗತಃ — of all the world including the dark fortnight · ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of Prāṇa · ಪ್ರಾಣದ್ವಾರಾ — through Prāṇa · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the dark fortnight · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷತ್ವೇ ಸತಿ — when it has the nature of the bright fortnight · ಕೃಷ್ಣೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — even while performing in the dark · ಪ್ರಕಾಶಾತ್ಮಕೇ — in what is of the nature of light · ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಏವ — in the bright alone · ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ — they perform · ಇತಿ — thus · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷೇ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಜ್ಞಾನಸ್ಯ — of the knowledge that the bright fortnight is Prāṇa · ಸ್ತುತಿಃ — praise · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಏತತ್ — this (praise) · ಸ್ತುತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಏವ — for the very purpose of this praise · ಜ್ಞಾನರಹಿತಾನ್ — those devoid of knowledge · ನಿಂದತಿ — censures · ಇತರೇ ತು ಇತಿ — with the words "itare tu (the others however)" ।

ಯೇ ತು — those who however · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ — Prāṇa as the Self of all · ನ ಪಶ್ಯಂತಿ — do not see · ಅಜ್ಞತ್ವಾತ್ — because of ignorance · ತೇಷಾಂ — for them · ಶುಕ್ಲಪಕ್ಷಃ — the bright fortnight · ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವೇನ ಅಜ್ಞಾಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ — because it is not known as Prāṇa · ಅಜ್ಞಾನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಸನ್ — being of the nature of ignorance · ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷತ್ವಂ ಆಪದ್ಯತೇ — takes on the nature of the dark fortnight · ಅತಃ — therefore · ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಕುರ್ವಂತಃ ಅಪಿ — even while performing in the bright · ಅದರ್ಶನಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of non-seeing / darkness · ಪ್ರಕಾಶರಹಿತೇ — in what is devoid of light · ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಏವ — in the dark alone · ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ — they perform · ಇತಿ — thus · ತೇ ನಿಂದ್ಯಂತೇ — they are censured · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಉಕ್ತಂ ಅರ್ಥಂ — the stated meaning · ಶ್ರುತ್ಯಾ — through the Śruti · ಆರೂಢಂ ಕರೋತಿ — establishes / confirms with authority · ಇತರ ಇತಿ — with the word "itara (the other / dark fortnight)" ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Applies the Rayi-Prāṇa analysis to the Month — dark fortnight is Rayi, bright is Prāṇa; seers perform in the bright, the others in the dark ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Shows the Month as Prajāpati containing the Year; unpacks dark/bright as Moon/Sun, food/fire; explains that seers who see Prāṇa as all perform in the bright even when physically in the dark — and vice versa for the ignorant ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Resolves the apparent contradiction (anupapanna) that rites are observed in both fortnights; establishes the passage as a stuti (praise) of Prāṇa-knowledge and a nindā (censure) of ignorance; provides the full anvaya for the yasmāt…tasmāt sentence

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The Month is Prajāpati — it contains the Year completely within itself as its own limb (avayava). The Year is non-different from the Month in the same way cause and effect are non-different.
  2. Dark fortnight = Rayi = Moon = food; Bright fortnight = Prāṇa = Sun = fire. The Rayi-Prāṇa dyad operates at every level — Year, Month, fortnight.
  3. The key teaching is epistemological, not ritual: those who see Prāṇa as the Self of all transform even the dark into the bright by their knowledge. Those who do not see Prāṇa transform even the bright into the dark by their ignorance.
  4. Ānandagiri's key contribution is identifying the passage as stuti-nindā (praise and censure) — a standard Vedic rhetorical form — rather than a factual description of when rites are performed. This resolves the apparent contradiction that rites are in fact performed in both fortnights.
  5. The anvaya of yasmāt…tasmāt is the logical spine: knowledge of Prāṇa's identity with the bright fortnight means the dark fortnight is never seen as other than Prāṇa — hence performance anywhere is performance in the bright.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text: ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಹರೇವ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ರಾತ್ರಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ವಾ ಏತೇ ಪ್ರಸ್ಕಂದಂತಿ ಯೇ ದಿವಾ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದ್ಯದ್ರಾತ್ರೌ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ॥ ೧೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Day-and-Night (ahorātra) is indeed Prajāpati. Of it, the day (ahas) alone is Prāṇa and the night (rātri) alone is Rayi. Those who unite with a woman by day indeed waste / lose their Prāṇa. That which is uniting with a woman by night is brahmacarya (celibacy / proper conduct) alone.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಸೋಽಪಿ ಮಾಸಾತ್ಮಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸ್ವಾವಯವೇ ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೇ ಪರಿಸಮಾಪ್ಯತೇ ।

ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ।

ತಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಅಹರೇವ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ರಾತ್ರಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವದೇವ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಮ್ ಅಹರಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ವೈ ಏತೇ ಪ್ರಸ್ಕಂದಂತಿ ನಿರ್ಗಮಯಂತಿ ಶೋಷಯಂತಿ ವಾ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮನೋ ವಿಚ್ಛಿದ್ಯಾಪನಯಂತಿ ।

ಕೇ ? ಯೇ ದಿವಾ ಅಹನಿ ರತ್ಯಾ ರತಿಕಾರಣಭೂತಯಾ ಸಹ ಸ್ತ್ರಿಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ಮೈಥುನಮಾಚರಂತಿ ಮೂಢಾಃ ।

ಯತ ಏವಂ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತನ್ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ।

ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ರತ್ಯಾ ಋತೌ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದಿತಿ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಯಮಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕೋ ವಿಧಿಃ ।

ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ತೂಚ್ಯತೇ ಸೋಽಹೋರಾತ್ರಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿರ್ವ್ರೀಹಿಯವಾದ್ಯನ್ನಾತ್ಮನಾ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
That Prajāpati whose nature is the Month is also completely contained within his own limb, the Day-and-Night (ahorātra).

The Day-and-Night is indeed Prajāpati — as has been stated before (with the same characteristics).

Of it too, the day alone is Prāṇa — the eater, the fire — and the night alone is Rayi — exactly as before.

Those who are foolish — they indeed lose / waste / drain away the Prāṇa whose nature is the day; they cause it to flow out, to dry up, or they cut it away and remove it from themselves.

Who are they? Those fools who by day unite with a woman — whose purpose is enjoyment — and engage in intercourse.

Since this is so, therefore this must not be done — this prohibition is incidental (prāsaṅgika — arising from the context, not the primary topic).

That which is uniting with a woman by night in the proper season (ṛtu) is brahmacarya alone — because it is praiseworthy; therefore the injunction that approaching one's wife by night in the proper season is to be done — this too is an incidental injunction (prāsaṅgika vidhi).

The main topic, however, is now stated: that Prajāpati who is of the nature of the Day-and-Night is established as food — in the form of rice, barley, and the like.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
One sentence in this Bhāṣya requires explicit anvaya treatment.

Sentence — The incidental prohibition and the incidental injunction

As written:

ಯತ ಏವಂ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತನ್ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ।

ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ ರತ್ಯಾ ಋತೌ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಮೇವ ತದಿತಿ ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಯಮಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕೋ ವಿಧಿಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ದಿವಾ ಮೈಥುನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಕ್ಷಯಕರಮ್] ಇತಿ ಯತಃ ಏವಂ [ಉಕ್ತಂ] — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ತತ್ ನ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ [ಇತ್ಯಾಯಂ] ಪ್ರತಿಷೇಧಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ [ಭವತಿ] ।

[ಅಪರಃ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ] — ಯತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ ಋತೌ ರತ್ಯಾ ಸಂಯುಜ್ಯಂತೇ [ತತ್] ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಂ ಏವ [ಭವತಿ] ।

[ತಸ್ಯ] ಪ್ರಶಸ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ರಾತ್ರೌ [ಋತೌ] ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಕರ್ತವ್ಯಂ — ಇತಿ ಅಯಂ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕಃ ವಿಧಿಃ [ಭವತಿ] ।

English: Because intercourse by day causes loss of Prāṇa — therefore this must not be done: this prohibition is incidental (to the main topic). And conversely — that which is uniting with a woman by night in the proper season is brahmacarya alone; because of its being praiseworthy, the injunction that approaching one's wife by night in the proper season is to be done — this too is an incidental injunction.

Note: Śaṅkara uses the technical term ಪ್ರಾಸಂಗಿಕ (prāsaṅgika — incidental / arising from context) twice — once for the prohibition (pratiṣedha) and once for the positive injunction (vidhi). This signals that neither daytime abstinence nor nighttime union is the primary subject of the verse — the primary subject (ಪ್ರಕೃತ) is Prajāpati as food. Ānandagiri confirms this explicitly in the Ṭīkā.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ರಯಿಃ ಪೂರ್ವವತ್ ಇತಿ ।

ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅಹ್ನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣತ್ವ-ಉಕ್ತಿ-ಪ್ರಸಂಗಾತ್ ಅಹ್ನಿ ಮೈಥುನಂ ನಿಷೇಧತಿ – ಪ್ರಾಣಮಿತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಕೃತಮಿತಿ ।

ಕುತೋ ಹ ವಾ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಪೂರ್ವೋಕ್ತಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏತತ್ ಉಪಯೋಗಿತಯಾ ಉಕ್ತಂ ನ ತು ಸಾಕ್ಷಾತ್ ಪ್ರಕೃತಂ ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ ॥ ೧೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
On "rāyiḥ pūrvavat" (Rayi as before): Ānandagiri explains this means Rayi is food and the Moon — i.e., the same identification as established in the earlier analysis of the Year and Month.

On the prohibition of daytime intercourse: Ānandagiri explains that by occasion of (ＵKti-prasaṅga — the incidental context of) stating the day's Prāṇa-nature, Śaṅkara prohibits intercourse by day — with the words "prāṇam" (they lose Prāṇa). This is a prāsaṅgika (incidental) prohibition arising from the context, not the primary teaching.

On "prakṛtam" (the main topic): Ānandagiri clarifies that the primary subject (prakṛta) is what was originally asked — "from where indeed are these creatures born?" — i.e., the question put to the sage at the beginning of the first Praśna. The import is: everything stated above — the Year, Month, fortnight, Day-and-Night — was all stated as being useful (upayogita) for answering that question, but none of it was the direct primary topic (sākṣāt prakṛta). The primary topic now returns: Prajāpati established as food in the form of rice, barley, and the like — from which creatures are born.

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The fractal descent is complete — Year → Month → Fortnight → Day-and-Night. At every level, Rayi and Prāṇa are the two aspects of Prajāpati.
  2. Day = Prāṇa = fire = eater; Night = Rayi = Moon = food. The daytime is the consuming, active principle; the night is the nourishing, material principle.
  3. The prohibition and injunction are prāsaṅgika — incidental, not primary. Śaṅkara is careful to distinguish what is directly relevant to the main topic from what arises as a contextual aside.
  4. The primary topic (prakṛtam) now returns — the original question of the Praśna: from what are creatures born? Prajāpati as food (rice, barley etc.) is the answer. Everything from the Year analysis was upayogita — useful context, not the direct answer.
  5. Ānandagiri's key contribution is pinpointing "prakṛtam" as the structural signal that Śaṅkara is now returning to the original question after the long Rayi-Prāṇa analysis — tying the entire philosophical excursus back to its starting point.

docs.text:
ಏವಂ ಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ — ತತ್ ಅನ್ನಂ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ತತಃ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ ರೇತಃ ನೃಬೀಜಂ ತತ್ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾರಣಂ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಯೋಷಿತಿ ಸಿಕ್ತಾತ್ ಇಮಾಃ ಮನುಷ್ಯಾದಿಲಕ್ಷಣಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಯತ್ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ಕುತೋ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತ ಇತಿ ।

ತದೇವಂ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಮಿಥುನಾದಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರಾಂತೇನ ಅನ್ನರೇತೋದ್ವಾರೇಣ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತ ಇತಿ ನಿರ್ಣೀತಮ್ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Having transformed thus in sequence — that food is indeed Prajāpati.

How? From that (food), indeed comes seed — the male seed, the cause of progeny — from that, when deposited in a woman, these creatures characterised as human beings and the like are born. This is what was asked: "from where indeed are these creatures born?"

Thus it has been determined: these creatures are born through the sequence beginning with the Moon-and-Sun pair, ending with the day-and-night, by the gateway of food and seed.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The opening sentence of this Bhāṣya requires anvaya treatment — the participial ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ (having transformed) is the key to connecting the entire preceding analysis to the final statement.

Sentence — The culminating identification: food is Prajāpati

As written:

ಏವಂ ಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ — ತತ್ ಅನ್ನಂ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ] ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನ-ರೂಪಾತ್ [ಆರಭ್ಯ] ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಮಾಸ-ಪಕ್ಷ-ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಏವಂ ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ — ತತ್ [ಅಂತಿಮಂ ರೂಪಂ] ಅನ್ನಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

[ಅತಃ] ಅನ್ನಂ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ [ಇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ] ।

English: Prajāpati — having transformed through the sequence beginning from the Rayi-Prāṇa pair, through Year, Month, Fortnight, and Day-and-Night — that final form is food. Therefore food is indeed Prajāpati.

Note: The word ಏವಂ ಕ್ರಮೇಣ (thus in sequence) is the syntactic bridge that connects the entire preceding analysis of verses 9–13 to this final statement. The participial ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ (having transformed/evolved) is crucial — it confirms that Prajāpati has not become something other than himself but has evolved (pariṇāma) into food through the chain of transformations. Ānandagiri makes this explicit in his anvaya gloss.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಏವಂ ಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಇತಿ ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ ವ್ರೀಹ್ಯಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತಃ ಸನ್ ಅನ್ನಂ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಜಾತಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ ।

ಅನ್ನರೂಪತ್ವೇಽಪಿ ತಸ್ಯ ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಜನಕತ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ತತಃ ಇತಿ ।

ಭಕ್ಷಿತಾತ್ ಅನ್ನಾತ್ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ರೇತಃ ಇತಿ ।

ಶೋಣಿತಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ತುಲ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ ॥ ೧೪ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
On "evaṃ krameṇa" (thus in sequence): Ānandagiri provides the full anvaya. Having transformed through the sequence of Rayi, Prāṇa, Year, and so on — and being established in the form of rice and other grains — Prajāpati has become food-natured. The syntactic connection (anvaya) is: "Prajāpati, having become food-natured (annātmaka), is food."

On "katham?" (how?): Ānandagiri explains the question being raised: even though Prajāpati has the form of food, how does he become the generator of creatures? This is the question Śaṅkara now answers.

On "tataḥ" (from that): Ānandagiri clarifies this means "from the food that has been eaten" — i.e., it is consumed food that transforms into seed, not food in an abstract sense.

On "retaḥ" (seed): Ānandagiri states that the word "retas" (male seed) is also an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative term) for śoṇita (the female generative substance / blood) — because both are equal in their role as causes of progeny.

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಆದಿ-ಕ್ರಮೇಣ — through the sequence of Rayi, Prāṇa, Year, and so on · ಪರಿಣಮ್ಯ — having transformed / evolved · ವ್ರೀಹ್ಯಾದ್ಯಾತ್ಮನಾ — in the form of rice and other grains · ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥಿತಃ ಸನ್ — being established / situated · ಅನ್ನಂ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — food is indeed Prajāpati · ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಜಾತಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — Prajāpati having become food-natured · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. This verse is the answer to the opening question of the entire first Praśna: "from where are these creatures born?" The answer, reached through six verses of analysis, is: from food, which is Prajāpati.
  2. The sequence is complete — Rayi-Prāṇa → Year → Month → Fortnight → Day-and-Night → Food → Seed → Creatures. Prajāpati transforms (pariṇāma) through each level without becoming other than himself.
  3. "evaṃ krameṇa pariṇamya" is the structural hinge of the entire first Praśna — it looks back at verses 9–13 and confirms they were all stages in one continuous transformation.
  4. Ānandagiri's upalakaṣaṇa note on "retaḥ" is important for completeness — both male seed and female generative substance are equally causes of progeny, and the Śruti uses one to indicate both.
  5. The Rayi-Prāṇa dyad is maintained to the end — food is Rayi (material, nourishing), and it is through the Prāṇa-aspect (digestion, transformation, vital activity) that food becomes seed and seed becomes creatures.

ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ತತ್ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿವ್ರತಂ ಚರಂತಿ ತೇ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯಂತೇ ।

docs.text:

This Brahmaloka belongs to those alone in whom is austerity (tapas) and brahmacarya, and in whom truth (satya) is firmly established.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಏವಂ ಸತಿ ಯೇ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ ।

ಹ ವೈ ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧಸ್ಮರಣಾರ್ಥೌ ನಿಪಾತೌ ।

ತತ್ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ವ್ರತಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿವ್ರತಂ ಋತೌ ಭಾರ್ಯಾಗಮನಂ ಚರಂತಿ ಕುರ್ವಂತಿ, ತೇಷಾಂ ದೃಷ್ಟಂ ಫಲಮಿದಮ್ ।

ಕಿಮ್ ? ತೇ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಪುತ್ರಂ ದುಹಿತರಂ ಚ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯಂತೇ ।

ಅದೃಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಫಲಂ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತದತ್ತಕಾರಿಣಾಂ ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ ಏಷಃ ಯಶ್ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಲಕ್ಷಣಃ ।

ಯೇಷಾಂ ತಪಃ ಸ್ನಾತಕವ್ರತಾದಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಂ ಋತೋರನ್ಯತ್ರ ಮೈಥುನಾಸಮಾಚರಣಂ ಯೇಷು ಚ ಸತ್ಯಂ ಅನೃತವರ್ಜನಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಂ ಅವ್ಯಭಿಚಾರಿತಯಾ ವರ್ತತೇ ನಿತ್ಯಮೇವ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Therefore, in this being so — those householders who observe that vow of Prajāpati. The particles "ha vai" are for the purpose of recalling what is well-known. The vow of Prajāpati — which is the vow of approaching one's wife in the proper season — they observe, they perform. This is the visible (dṛṣṭa) fruit for them.

What is it? They produce a pair — a son and a daughter.

And the invisible (adṛṣṭa) fruit — for those same persons who perform iṣṭa (sacrifice), pūrta (charity), and datta (giving) — is this very Brahmaloka which is cāndramasa (of the Moon), characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa.

This belongs to those in whom austerity (tapas) is the snataka-vrata (the vow of the bath-graduate) and the like; in whom brahmacarya is the non-performance of intercourse outside the proper season; and in whom truth (satya) — the avoidance of falsehood — is firmly established, operating without deviation, always.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
One sentence in this Bhāṣya requires explicit anvaya treatment — the long relative clause describing who attains the Brahmaloka.

Sentence — The conditions for attaining the cāndramasa Brahmaloka

As written:

ಅದೃಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಫಲಂ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತದತ್ತಕಾರಿಣಾಂ ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ ಏಷಃ ಯಶ್ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಲಕ್ಷಣಃ ।

ಯೇಷಾಂ ತಪಃ ಸ್ನಾತಕವ್ರತಾದಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಂ ಋತೋರನ್ಯತ್ರ ಮೈಥುನಾಸಮಾಚರಣಂ ಯೇಷು ಚ ಸತ್ಯಂ ಅನೃತವರ್ಜನಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಂ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾನಾಂ] ಅದೃಷ್ಟಂ ಫಲಂ [ಕಃ ?] — ಏಷಃ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಲಕ್ಷಣಃ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

[ಕೇಷಾಂ ?] ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ — ಯೇ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತದತ್ತ-ಕಾರಿಣಃ [ಸಂತಿ] ಯೇಷಾಂ ತಪಃ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ಯೇಷಾಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ಯೇಷು ಸತ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

English: What is the invisible fruit for householders? It is this very lunar Brahmaloka characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa. And for whom? For those very persons who perform iṣṭa, pūrta, and datta — in whom is austerity, in whom is brahmacarya, and in whom truth is firmly established.

Note: Śaṅkara adds three qualifications — tapas, brahmacarya, satya — beyond the mere performance of the Prajāpati-vow. This is the key point that Ānandagiri flags in the Ṭīkā: the Brahmaloka is not attained by the Prajāpati-vow alone. It requires iṣṭa-pūrta-datta in addition, plus these three inner qualifications. This prevents the wrong conclusion that any householder who observes the proper-season rule automatically attains the lunar Brahmaloka.

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿವ್ರತಾಚರಣಮಾತ್ರೇಣ ನಾದೃಷ್ಟಫಲಂ ಚಂದ್ರಲೋಕಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯತೇ ಮೂರ್ಖಾಣಾಮಪಿ ಪ್ರಸಂಗಾತ್ ಅತ ಆಹ – ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ ಇತಿ ।

ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕ ಇತಿ ।

ಅಪರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಅಂಶತ್ವಾತ್ ರಯಿರೂಪಸ್ಯ ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕತ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಾದಿಕಾರಿಣಾಂ ತಪಆದಿಕಮಪಿ ಚಂದ್ರಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತ್ಯರ್ಥಂ ಅಪೇಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಇತ್ಯತ ಆಹ – ಯೇಷಾಂ ತಪ ಇತಿ ॥ ೧೫ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens with a crucial clarification: the lunar world (Brahmaloka) as an invisible (adṛṣṭa) fruit is not attained merely by observing the Prajāpati-vow (approaching one's wife in the proper season) alone. If it were, even fools who happen to observe the rule would attain it — an absurd consequence (prasaṅga). Therefore Śaṅkara adds "iṣṭāpūrta" — with the words "iṣṭāpūrta."

On "cāndramaso brahmaloka" (the lunar Brahmaloka): Ānandagiri explains that the Moon — which is of the nature of Rayi — being a portion of Aparabrahman (the lower Brahman, Prajāpati), qualifies as a Brahmaloka. It is called Brahmaloka because it is a portion of Prajāpati who is Aparabrahman — not because it is the supreme Brahman.

On "yeṣāṃ tapas" (in whom is austerity): Ānandagiri states that even for those who perform iṣṭa and the like, the austerity and the other qualifications (tapas, brahmacarya, satya) are also required for attaining the lunar world. Therefore Śaṅkara states these separately — with the words "yeṣāṃ tapas."

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) States the visible fruit of the Prajāpati-vow (a son and daughter) and the conditions for the invisible fruit — the Brahmaloka — namely tapas, brahmacarya, and truth ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Defines the Prajāpati-vow precisely as approaching one's wife in the proper season; distinguishes visible (dṛṣṭa) and invisible (adṛṣṭa) fruits; adds iṣṭa-pūrta-datta as conditions for the Brahmaloka; defines tapas, brahmacarya, and satya specifically for a householder ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Prevents the wrong conclusion that the Prajāpati-vow alone yields the Brahmaloka; explains the lunar world's title "Brahmaloka" as arising from the Moon being a portion of Prajāpati who is Aparabrahman; clarifies that tapas etc. are additional requirements even for those who perform iṣṭa

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Two fruits are distinguished — dṛṣṭa (visible, this-worldly: a son and daughter) and adṛṣṭa (invisible, other-worldly: the lunar Brahmaloka). The Prajāpati-vow alone yields only the visible fruit.
  2. The invisible fruit requires more — iṣṭa (sacrifice), pūrta (charity), and datta (giving), plus the inner qualifications of tapas, brahmacarya, and satya. This is the full condition for the cāndramasa Brahmaloka.
  3. The lunar world is called "Brahmaloka" not because it is the supreme Brahman but because the Moon is a portion (aṃśa) of Prajāpati who is Aparabrahman (the lower Brahman). Ānandagiri's clarification here is philosophically important — it prevents confusion between the lunar Brahmaloka and the final liberation.
  4. Tapas for a householder is defined precisely as the snataka-vrata and similar observances — not the extreme austerities of a renunciant. Brahmacarya is defined as not engaging in intercourse outside the proper season. Satya is the unfailing avoidance of falsehood.
  5. Ānandagiri's prasaṅga argument — that fools too would attain the Brahmaloka if the vow alone were sufficient — is a classic reductio ad absurdum used to establish that additional qualifications are necessary.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಯಸ್ತು ಪುನಃ ಆದಿತ್ಯೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತ ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮಭಾವಃ ವಿರಜಃ ಶುದ್ಧಃ ನ ಚಂದ್ರಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕವತ್ ರಜಸ್ವಲಃ ವೃದ್ಧಿಕ್ಷಯಾದಿಯುಕ್ತಃ ಅಸೌ ತೇಷಾಮ್ ।

ಕೇಷಾಂ ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — ಯಥಾ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾನಾಂ ಅನೇಕವಿರುದ್ಧಸಂವ್ಯವಹಾರಪ್ರಯೋಜನವತ್ತ್ವಾತ್ ಜಿಹ್ಮಂ ಕೌಟಿಲ್ಯಂ ವಕ್ರಭಾವಃ ಅವಶ್ಯಂಭಾವಿ ತಥಾ ನ ಯೇಷು ಜಿಹ್ಮಮ್ ।

ಯಥಾ ಚ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾನಾಂ ಕ್ರೀಡಾದಿನಿಮಿತ್ತಂ ಅನೃತಂ ಅವರ್ಜನೀಯಂ ತಥಾ ನ ಯೇಷು ತತ್ ।

ತಥಾ ಮಾಯಾ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾನಾಮಿವ ನ ಯೇಷು ವಿದ್ಯತೇ ।

ಮಾಯಾ ನಾಮ ಬಹಿಃ ಅನ್ಯಥಾ ಆತ್ಮಾನಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶ್ಯ ಅನ್ಯಥಾ ಏವ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಕರೋತಿ, ಸಾ ಮಾಯಾ ಮಿಥ್ಯಾಚಾರರೂಪಾ ।

ಮಾಯಾ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಆದಯಃ ದೋಷಾಃ ಯೇಷು ಏಕಾಕಿಷು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿ-ವಾನಪ್ರಸ್ಥ-ಭಿಕ್ಷುಷು ನಿಮಿತ್ತಾಭಾವಾತ್ ನ ವಿದ್ಯಂತೇ, ತತ್ಸಾಧನಾನುರೂಪ್ಯೇಣ ಏವ ತೇಷಾಂ ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ।

ಇತಿ ಏಷಾ ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಗತಿಃ ।

ಪೂರ್ವೋಕ್ತಃ ತು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಚಂದ್ರಲಕ್ಷಣಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
But that (Brahmaloka) which is indicated by the Sun — the Northern solstice — the state of being the Self of Prāṇa: that is spotless (viraja), pure — unlike the lunar Brahmaloka which is tainted (rajasvalā), subject to waxing and waning and the like. That belongs to those — to whom? It is said:

Just as crookedness (jihma) — deviousness, a bent disposition — is unavoidable for householders because they are engaged in many conflicting worldly transactions — so (this viraja Brahmaloka belongs to) those in whom there is no such crookedness.

And just as falsehood, arising from occasions like play and entertainment, is unavoidable for householders — so (it belongs to) those in whom there is no such falsehood.

And just as deceit (māyā) exists in householders — so (it belongs to) those in whom it does not exist.

Māyā means: outwardly presenting oneself as one thing while inwardly acting in a different way altogether — that māyā which is of the nature of duplicitous conduct.

These faults — māyā and the like — do not exist in those who live alone: brahmacarins, forest-dwellers (vānaprasthas), and mendicants (bhikṣus) — because the occasions / causes (for these faults) are absent. Precisely because their means (sādhana) are in keeping with this (viraja) world — that spotless Brahmaloka belongs to them.

This is the path / destination of those who combine knowledge with action (jñānayuktakarmavants). The Brahmaloka mentioned earlier, however — the lunar one — is for those who perform only ritual action (kevalakarmins).

This Bhāṣya has one complex sentence that requires explicit anvaya — the long relative-clause chain defining the qualifications for the viraja Brahmaloka.

Sentence — Who attains the viraja Brahmaloka

As written:

ಮಾಯಾ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಆದಯಃ ದೋಷಾಃ ಯೇಷು ಏಕಾಕಿಷು ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿ-ವಾನಪ್ರಸ್ಥ-ಭಿಕ್ಷುಷು ನಿಮಿತ್ತಾಭಾವಾತ್ ನ ವಿದ್ಯಂತೇ, ತತ್ಸಾಧನಾನುರೂಪ್ಯೇಣ ಏವ ತೇಷಾಂ ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಯೇಷು ಏಕಾಕಿಷು — ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚಾರಿಷು, ವಾನಪ್ರಸ್ಥೇಷು, ಭಿಕ್ಷುಷು ಚ — ಜಿಹ್ಮ-ಅನೃತ-ಮಾಯಾ-ಆದಯಃ ದೋಷಾಃ ನಿಮಿತ್ತ-ಅಭಾವಾತ್ ನ ವಿದ್ಯಂತೇ — ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ [ಸಾಧನ-ಅನುರೂಪ್ಯೇಣ] ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ [ಭವತಿ] ।

English: In those who live alone — brahmacarins, vānaprasthas, and bhikṣus — the faults of crookedness, falsehood, māyā and the like do not exist, because the occasions / causes for them are absent. Precisely because their means (sādhana) are fitting and in keeping with that (viraja) world — that spotless Brahmaloka belongs to those very persons.

Note: The causal chain here is: absence of occasions → absence of faults → suitability of sādhana → attainment of viraja Brahmaloka. Ānandagiri flags that the word ಭಿಕ್ಷು here does not include the Paramahaṃsa — the highest renunciant who is beyond even the desire for any Brahmaloka — but refers to the lower orders of mendicancy (kuṭīcaka etc.) who still aspire to worlds.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ತೇಷಾಮಸೌ ವಿರಜ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಯಸ್ತ್ವಿತಿ ।

ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣ ಇತಿ ।

ತೇನ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮಭಾವಃ ಅಪರಬ್ರಹ್ಮತಯಾ ಅವಸ್ಥಾನಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅಸೌ ಕೇಷಾಂ ತೇಷಾಂ ಇತಿ ।

ತೇಷಾಮಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಇತ್ಯತ್ರ ತೇಷಾಂ ಇತಿ ಅನೇನ ಕೇಷಾಂ ನಿರ್ದೇಶಃ ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾರ್ಥಃ ।

ನ ಯೇಷು ಜಿಹ್ಮಂ ಇತ್ಯತ್ರ ಜಿಹ್ಮಾದಿಶಬ್ದಂ ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕಪ್ರದರ್ಶನೇನ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಯಥ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ।

ಮಾಯಾಗ್ರಹಣಂ ತಾದೃಶಾನಾಂ ದೋಷಾಣಾಂ ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಇತಿ ವದನ್ ವಾಕ್ಯಾರ್ಥಂ ಸಂಗೃಹ್ಯ ದರ್ಶಯತಿ – ಮಾಯಾ ಇತಿ ಏವಮಿತಿ ।

ಭಿಕ್ಷುಷು ಇತಿ ಪರಮಹಂಸ-ವ್ಯತಿರಿಕ್ತಾನಾಂ ಕುಟೀಚಕಾದೀನಾಂ ಗ್ರಹಣಮ್ ।

ತೇಷಾಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಾದಪಿ ವಿರಕ್ತತ್ವೇನ ತತ್ರ ಅನರ್ಥಿತ್ವಾತ್ ।

ಇತಿಶಬ್ದಾರ್ಥಂ ಆಹ – ಇತ್ಯೇಷ ಇತಿ ॥ ೧೬ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by saying Śaṅkara explains the sentence "teṣām asau viraja" (that spotless Brahmaloka belongs to those) — with the words "yas tu" (but that which).

On "uttarāyaṇa" (Northern solstice): Ānandagiri explains this means "attainable through it (the Northern solstice)." And "prāṇātmabhāva" (the state of being the Self of Prāṇa) means abiding as Aparabrahman (the lower Brahman, Prajāpati).

On "asau keṣāṃ teṣām" (that — of those — to whom): Ānandagiri identifies this as a question being raised — in the sentence "teṣām asau virajaḥ," the word "teṣām" (of those) raises the question: of whom exactly is this a reference?

On "na yeṣu jihnam" (in whom there is no crookedness): Ānandagiri says Śaṅkara explains the words "jihma" etc. by the method of contrast (vyatireka-pradarśana) — beginning with "yathā" (just as). By showing what these faults are like when present in householders, Śaṅkara makes clear what their absence means.

On the use of "māyā": Ānandagiri states that the mention of māyā is an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative term) for all such similar faults — and Śaṅkara gathers the full meaning of the sentence and presents it with the words "māyā iti evam ādi" (māyā and the like).

On "bhikṣuṣu" (mendicants): Ānandagiri clarifies that "bhikṣu" here refers not to the Paramahaṃsa (the highest order of renunciant) but to the lower orders such as the kuṭīcaka and the like. The reason the Paramahaṃsa is excluded is that such persons, being dispassionate (virakta) even towards the Brahmaloka, do not desire it — they are "anarthin" (non-aspirants) for that world.

Finally, on the meaning of the word "iti" (thus) at the end of the Bhāṣya: this is explained with the words "ity eṣā" — meaning "this is (the path of those who combine knowledge with action)."

docs.text:
ತೇಷಾಂ ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the sentence beginning "teṣām asau virajaḥ" · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಯಸ್ತು ಇತಿ — with the words "yas tu (but that which)" ।

ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣ ಇತಿ — on the word "uttarāyaṇa (Northern solstice)" ।

ತೇನ — through it / by that (Northern solstice) · ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಃ — attainable · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಪ್ರಾಣಾತ್ಮಭಾವಃ — the state of being the Self of Prāṇa · ಅಪರ-ಬ್ರಹ್ಮತಯಾ — as Aparabrahman (the lower Brahman) · ಅವಸ್ಥಾನಂ — abiding / residing · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಅಸೌ ಕೇಷಾಂ ತೇಷಾಂ ಇತಿ — "that — of those — to whom" · ತೇಷಾಂ ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಇತ್ಯತ್ರ — in the sentence "teṣām asau virajaḥ" · ತೇಷಾಂ ಇತಿ ಅನೇನ — by this word "teṣām (of those)" · ಕೇಷಾಂ ನಿರ್ದೇಶಃ — a reference to whom? · ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾರ್ಥಃ — this is the sense of the question ।

ನ ಯೇಷು ಜಿಹ್ಮಂ ಇತ್ಯತ್ರ — in the phrase "in whom there is no crookedness" · ಜಿಹ್ಮ-ಆದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಂ — the word "jihma (crookedness)" and the like · ವ್ಯತಿರೇಕ-ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನೇನ — by the method of showing the contrast · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಯಥಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ — beginning with "yathā (just as)" ।

ಮಾಯಾ-ಗ್ರಹಣಂ — the mention / use of the word "māyā" · ತಾದೃಶಾನಾಂ ದೋಷಾಣಾಂ — of such similar faults · ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ — is an indicative term (standing for a wider class) · ಇತಿ ವದನ್ — saying this · ವಾಕ್ಯಾರ್ಥಂ — the meaning of the sentence · ಸಂಗೃಹ್ಯ — gathering together · ದರ್ಶಯತಿ — shows / presents · ಮಾಯಾ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಇತಿ — with the words "māyā and the like" ।

ಭಿಕ್ಷುಷು ಇತಿ — on the word "bhikṣuṣu (mendicants)" · ಪರಮಹಂಸ-ವ್ಯತಿರಿಕ್ತಾನಾಂ — of those other than the Paramahaṃsa · ಕುಟೀಚಕ-ಆದೀನಾಂ — of the kuṭīcaka and the like (lower orders of renunciation) · ಗ್ರಹಣಂ — the inclusion / reference ।

ತೇಷಾಂ — of those (Paramahaṃsas) · ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಾತ್ ಅಪಿ — even towards the Brahmaloka · ವಿರಕ್ತತ್ವೇನ — because of dispassion · ತತ್ρ — there (in the Brahmaloka) · ಅನರ್ಥಿತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being non-aspirants / not desirous of it ।

ಇತಿಶಬ್ದ-ಅರ್ಥಂ — the meaning of the word "iti (thus)" · ಆಹ — states · ಇತ್ಯೇಷಾ ಇತಿ — with the words "ity eṣā (this is)" ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Final verse of the first Praśna — the viraja (spotless) Brahmaloka belongs to those free from crookedness, falsehood, and deceit ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Identifies the viraja Brahmaloka as the Solar / Northern path; contrasts it with the tainted lunar Brahmaloka; defines jihma, anṛta, and māyā with examples from householder life; identifies its attainers as brahmacarins, vānaprasthas, and bhikṣus; closes with the summary distinction between the two paths ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Clarifies "prāṇātmabhāva" as abiding as Aparabrahman; explains the vyatireka method of Śaṅkara's definitions; identifies "māyā" as upalakaṣaṇa for all such faults; critically distinguishes the bhikṣu from the Paramahaṃsa — the latter being beyond even the desire for the Brahmaloka

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Two Brahmalokasare distinguished — the cāndramasa (lunar, tainted, subject to waxing and waning, for kevalakarmins) stated in verse 15, and the viraja (spotless, pure, Solar, for jñānayuktakarmavants) stated in verse 16. This is the closing structural distinction of the entire first Praśna.
  2. The viraja Brahmaloka is identified with the Solar / Northern path — the state of being the Self of Prāṇa, abiding as Aparabrahman. This is higher than the lunar world but still within the realm of Aparabrahman — not the final liberation.
  3. The three faults — jihma (crookedness), anṛta (falsehood), and māyā (dissimulation) — are defined through contrast with householder life. They are unavoidable for householders because of the many conflicting demands of worldly transactions. They are absent in those who live alone because the occasions for them are absent.
  4. The four āśramas are implied — brahmacarins, vānaprasthas, bhikṣus are named; the gṛhastha (householder) is the implied contrast throughout.
  5. Ānandagiri's exclusion of the Paramahaṃsa is the most philosophically subtle point in this Ṭīkā: the highest renunciant is beyond even the desire for the viraja Brahmaloka — they are anarthin (non-aspirants) for any world. This preserves the hierarchy: kevalakarmins → lunar world; jñānayuktakarmavants → viraja Solar world; jñānins / Paramahaṃsas → liberation beyond worlds.

docs.title: ಮಂತ್ರ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ಹ ಸ ಋಷಿರುವಾಚ ಭೂಯ ಏವ ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ಪೃಚ್ಛತ ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ ೨ ॥ To them, the sage said: "Live here for one more year, practicing austerity, brahmacarya, and faith. Then ask questions according to your desire. If we know the answers, we shall explain everything to you."

ತಾನ್ ಹ — to them indeed

  • ತಾನ್ → to them
  • ಹ → indeed

ಸ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ — the sage said

  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯ ಏವ — for some more time; further

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additional
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಪಸಾ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ — through austerity, brahmacarya, and faith

  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya
  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ — you shall stay for a year

  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ → for one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay, dwell

ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ — ask questions according to your desire

  • ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ — if we know

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ — we shall indeed tell you everything

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall tell

ಇತಿ — thus

  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ
docs.text:
ತಾನ್ ಏವಮುಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ — ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ, ತಥಾಪೀಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ ಸಮ್ಯಗ್ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತೋ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ । ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ ಯೋ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಸ್ತಮನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ । ಯದಿ ತದ್ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ । ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥೋ ಯದಿ - ಶಬ್ದೋ ನಾಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾದವಸೀಯತೇ ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವೋ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮ ಇತಿ ॥ To those who had approached him in that manner, the sage indeed said again: "Although you are already practitioners of austerity, nevertheless, remain here for a year with discipline — practicing austerity in the form of control of the senses, especially brahmacarya, and faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the authority of the scriptures and the teacher. Live here with reverence and with wholehearted dedication to serving the teacher. Thereafter, ask questions according to your respective desires. Whatever subject each of you wishes to know, and whatever inquiry arises in each one's mind, ask questions concerning that very subject. If we know the answer to what you ask, we shall explain it to you." The word 'if' (yadi) is used only to indicate the sage's humility and freedom from arrogance; it is not intended to imply ignorance or doubt. This is evident from the fact that all the questions are subsequently answered and resolved. Thus he says: "We shall indeed explain to you everything concerning the matters that you ask."

ತಾನ್ ಏವಮ್ ಉಪಗತಾನ್ ಸಃ ಹ ಕಿಲ ಋಷಿಃ ಉವಾಚ

The sage indeed said to those who had approached him in this manner.

  • ತಾನ್ → those (students)
  • ಏವಮ್ → thus, in this manner
  • ಉಪಗತಾನ್ → those who had approached
  • ಸಃ → he
  • ಹ ಕಿಲ → indeed
  • ಋಷಿಃ → the sage
  • ಉವಾಚ → said

ಭೂಯಃ ಪುನರೇವ

Further, once again.

  • ಭೂಯಃ → further, additionally
  • ಪುನಃ → again
  • ಏವ → indeed

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಯೂಯಂ ಪೂರ್ವಂ ತಪಸ್ವಿನ ಏವ

Although you are already practitioners of austerity,

  • ಯದ್ಯಪಿ → although
  • ಯೂಯಂ → you
  • ಪೂರ್ವಂ → previously, already
  • ತಪಸ್ವಿನಃ → practitioners of austerity
  • ಏವ → indeed

ತಥಾಪಿ ಇಹ ತಪಸಾ ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಸಂಯಮೇನ

Even so, here through tapas, namely control of the senses,

  • ತಥಾಪಿ → nevertheless
  • ಇಹ → here
  • ತಪಸಾ → through austerity
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ-ಸಂಯಮೇನ → through restraint of the senses
  • ಇಂದ್ರಿಯ → senses
  • ಸಂಯಮ → control, restraint
  • ಏನ → by, through

Śaṅkara explicitly glosses tapas here as indriya-saṃyama (sense-control).

ವಿಶೇಷತೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ

Especially through brahmacarya.

  • ವಿಶೇಷತಃ → especially, particularly
  • ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಚರ್ಯೇಣ → through brahmacarya

ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ ಚ ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ

And through faith, that is, a trusting attitude toward the scriptures and teacher.

  • ಶ್ರದ್ಧಯಾ → through faith
  • ಚ → and
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ-ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ → through an attitude of trust in the authority of the scriptures
  • ಆಸ್ತಿಕ್ಯ → faith in the validity of the Veda
  • ಬುದ್ಧಿ → understanding, attitude

ಆದರವಂತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live here for a year with reverence.

  • ಆದರ-ವಂತಃ → possessed of reverence
  • ಆದರ → respect, reverence
  • ವಂತಃ → possessing
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ಕಾಲಂ → for the period of one year
  • ಸಂವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall stay

ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ ಗುರುಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾಪರಾಃ ಸಂತಃ ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ

You shall live devoted to proper service of the teacher.

  • ಸಮ್ಯಕ್ → properly
  • ಗುರು-ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ-ಪರಾಃ → devoted to service of the teacher
  • ಗುರು → teacher
  • ಶುಶ್ರೂಷಾ → service, attendance
  • ಪರಾಃ → dedicated to
  • ಸಂತಃ → being
  • ವತ್ಸ್ಯಥ → you shall live

ತತಃ ಯಥಾಕಾಮಂ

Thereafter, according to your desire,

  • ತತಃ → then, thereafter
  • ಯಥಾ-ಕಾಮಂ → according to your wish

ಯಃ ಯಸ್ಯ ಕಾಮಃ ತಂ ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ

Without going beyond what each one desires to know.

  • ಯಃ → whichever
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಕಾಮಃ → desire
  • ತಂ → that
  • ಅನತಿಕ್ರಮ್ಯ → not transgressing, not exceeding

ಯದ್ವಿಷಯೇ ಯಸ್ಯ ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ

Regarding whatever subject each one has an inquiry,

  • ಯದ್-ವಿಷಯೇ → regarding whichever topic
  • ಯಸ್ಯ → of whom
  • ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ → desire to know, inquiry

ತದ್ವಿಷಯಾನ್ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ ಪೃಚ್ಛತ

Ask questions concerning those subjects.

  • ತದ್-ವಿಷಯಾನ್ → concerning those subjects
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾನ್ → questions
  • ಪೃಚ್ಛತ → ask

ಯದಿ ತತ್ ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ

If we know that which is asked by you,

  • ಯದಿ → if
  • ತತ್ → that
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್-ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked by you
  • ಯುಷ್ಮತ್ → by you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟಂ → asked
  • ವಿಜ್ಞಾಸ್ಯಾಮಃ → we know

ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ

The word "if" is used to indicate absence of arrogance.

  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ-ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನಾರ್ಥಃ → for demonstrating humility
  • ಅನುದ್ಧತತ್ವ → non-arrogance, humility
  • ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನ → showing
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → purpose
  • ಯದಿ-ಶಬ್ದಃ → the word "if"

This is an important observation of Śaṅkara.

ನ ಅಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಶಯಾರ್ಥಃ

It is not intended to suggest ignorance or doubt.

  • ನ → not
  • ಅಜ್ಞಾನ → ignorance
  • ಸಂಶಯ → doubt
  • ಅರ್ಥಃ → meaning, purpose
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ ಅವಸೀಯತೇ

This is understood from the subsequent resolution of the questions.

  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ನಿರ್ಣಯಾತ್ → from the determination of the questions
  • ಪ್ರಶ್ನ → questions
  • ನಿರ್ಣಯ → ascertainment, resolution
  • ಅವಸೀಯತೇ → is understood, is concluded

ಸರ್ವಂ ಹ ವಃ ಪೃಷ್ಟಾರ್ಥಂ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ ಇತಿ

"We shall indeed explain to you everything that you ask."

  • ಸರ್ವಂ → everything
  • ಹ → indeed
  • ವಃ → to you
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ-ಅರ್ಥಂ → the matter asked about
  • ಪೃಷ್ಟ → asked
  • ಅರ್ಥಂ → subject matter
  • ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಃ → we shall explain
  • ಇತಿ → thus

docs.text: Source of Ṭīkā: Ānandāśrama Sanskrit Series No. 8 (Ānandagiri on Śaṅkara Bhāṣya)

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text: ಅಥ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಭಗವನ್ ಕುತೋ ಹ ವಾ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತ ಇತಿ ॥ ೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: Then Kabandhi Kātyāyana approached (Pippalāda) and asked: "Revered Sir, from where indeed are these creatures born?"

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text: ಅಥ — then / next · ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ — Kabandhi Kātyāyana (the student's name and lineage) · ಉಪೇತ್ಯ — having approached / coming near · ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ — asked / enquired · ಭಗವನ್ — O Revered Sir / O Lord · ಕುತಃ — from where · ಹ ವಾ — indeed · ಇಮಾಃ — these · ಪ್ರಜಾಃ — creatures / beings · ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ — are born / come into being · ಇತಿ — thus ॥

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಅಥ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ ಉಪೇತ್ಯ ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ — ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್, ಕುತಃ ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಹ ವೈ ಇಮಾಃ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣ-ಆದ್ಯಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ಇತಿ ।

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ ಯತ್ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ ತದ್ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಮ್ ಇತಿ ತದರ್ಥಃ ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Then — after the period of one year (spent in the discipline prescribed in verse 2) — Kabandhi Kātyāyana approached, came near, and asked: "O Revered Sir, from where indeed are these creatures — Brāhmaṇas and the like — born, come into being?"

The purpose of this question is: what is the fruit and what is the destination of the lower knowledge (aparavidyā) and action (karma) combined together — that is what needs to be stated.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಅಥ — then / after · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾತ್ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ — after the year (of discipline) · ಕಬಂಧೀ ಕಾತ್ಯಾಯನಃ — Kabandhi Kātyāyana · ಉಪೇತ್ಯ — having approached · ಉಪಗಮ್ಯ — having come near · ಪಪ್ರಚ್ಛ — asked · ಪೃಷ್ಟವಾನ್ — enquired · ಹೇ ಭಗವನ್ — O Revered Sir · ಕುತಃ — from where · ಕಸ್ಮಾತ್ — from what (cause) · ಹ ವೈ — indeed · ಇಮಾಃ — these · ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದ್ಯಾಃ — Brāhmaṇas and the like · ಪ್ರಜಾಃ — creatures / beings · ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ — are born · ಉತ್ಪದ್ಯಂತೇ — come into being · ಇತಿ — thus ।

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ — of lower knowledge and action · ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ — combined together · ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ — what the fruit is · ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ — what the destination is · ತತ್ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ — that needs to be stated · ಇತಿ — thus · ತದರ್ಥಃ — the purpose of that · ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ — this question ॥

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya's second sentence — identifying the real purpose of the question — requires explicit anvaya, as it is Śaṅkara's interpretive gloss, not a paraphrase of the Mūla.

Sentence — The real import of Kabandhi's question

As written:

ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಯಾ ಗತಿಃ ತತ್ ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ ಇತಿ ತದರ್ಥಃ ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಅಯಂ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ — "ಕುತಃ ಇಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಯಂತೇ" ಇತಿ — ತದರ್ಥಃ [ಏಕಃ] : ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾ-ಕರ್ಮಣೋಃ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಯೋಃ ಯತ್ ಕಾರ್ಯಂ [ಫಲಂ] ಯಾ ಚ ಗತಿಃ — ತತ್ [ಸರ್ವಂ] ವಕ್ತವ್ಯಂ [ಇತ್ಯಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಃ] ।

English: This question — "from where are these creatures born?" — has this purpose: (the questioner is implying) what is the fruit and what is the destination of lower knowledge and action when combined together — that is what needs to be stated.

Note: Śaṅkara's identification of the question's real purpose (tadarthah) is a crucial hermeneutical move. The surface question appears to be about cosmogony (where do creatures come from?). But Śaṅkara identifies the deeper intent: the question is really about the fruit and destination of aparavidyā-karma- samuccaya — the combined path of lower knowledge and ritual action. This is what the entire first Praśna goes on to answer.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ ಇತಿ ಉಪಕ್ರಾಂತೇ ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪ್ರಕರಣೇ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿ-ಕರ್ತೃಕ-ಪ್ರಜಾಸೃಷ್ಟಿ-ವಿಷಯ-ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪ್ರತ್ಯುಕ್ತ್ಯೋಃ ಅಸಂಗತಿಂ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪ್ರತ್ಯುಕ್ತಿ-ರೂಪಾಯಾಃ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯಂ ಆಹ – ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾ ಇತಿ ।

ತೇಷಾಂ ಅಸೌ ವಿರಜಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ ಇತಿ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತ-ಕಾರ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಸ್ಯ ಅಥ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಇತಿ ತದ್ಗತೇಃ ದೇವಯಾನ-ಮಾರ್ಗಸ್ಯ ಚ ಇಹ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಾಣತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇದಂ ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಣಾಂ ಚ ಇತಿ ಅಪಿ ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಮ್ ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ ಚಂದ್ರಲೋಕಸ್ಯ ತದ್ಗತೇಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಸ್ಯ ಚ "ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ ಏಷ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ" "ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ" ಇತಿ ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಾಣತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ ।

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಇದಂ ಅಪಿ ಪರಬ್ರಹ್ಮ-ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ-ಅವಸರೇ ಅಸಂಗತಂ ಏವ ತಥಾಪಿ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಾತ್ ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಾತ್ ಚ ವಿರಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ಏವ ತತ್ρ ಅಧಿಕಾರಃ ಇತಿ ತತಃ ವೈರಾಗ್ಯ-ಅರ್ಥಂ ಇದಂ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಮುಖತಃ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಃ ಪ್ರತೀಯತೇ ತಥಾಪಿ ತದ್-ಉಕ್ತೌ ಪ್ರಯೋಜನ-ಅಭಾವಾತ್ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ-ಉಕ್ತಿ-ವ್ಯಾಜೇನ ಪರವಿದ್ಯಾ-ಫಲಂ ಏವ ಅತ್ρ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ ।

ಪ್ರಶ್ನ ಇತಿ ಪ್ರತಿವಚನಂ ಚ ಇತಿ ಅಪಿ ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಂ ತಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಏವ ತದ್-ಉಕ್ತೇಃ ಇತಿ ॥ ೩ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by identifying a potential objection: this is a Brahma-prakaraṇa (a context directed at enquiry into Brahman) — introduced with the words "seeking the supreme Brahman" (verse 2). So a question and answer about Prajāpati's creation of creatures would seem incongruous (asaṅgati) here. To resolve this apparent incongruity, Śaṅkara states the real purport (tātparya) of the question-and-answer in the form of the Śruti — with the words "aparavidyā" etc.

Ānandagiri then explains the two things that will be stated in the Praśna in answer to this question:

First: the fruit of the combined (samuccita) path of aparavidyā and karma — namely the viraja Brahmaloka ("that spotless Brahmaloka belongs to those," verse 16) — and the path leading to it, the Devayāna (Northern path), will be stated here (in the course of this Praśna). This is the meaning.

Second: and this is also an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative) for the fruit of ritual action alone (kevalakamma). The lunar world as the fruit of ritual action alone, and the Pitṛyāṇa as the path leading to it — these will also be stated here with the words "this Brahmaloka belongs to those very ones" and "those who desire progeny resort to the Southern path."

Even though this topic (creation of creatures and the paths) is, strictly speaking, incongruous in a context of enquiry into the supreme Brahman — nevertheless, only one who is dispassionate (virakta) towards both the fruit of ritual action alone and the fruit of combined action has the qualification (adhikāra) for that (enquiry into Brahman). Therefore this is stated for the purpose of generating dispassion (vairāgya).

Even though on the surface the creation (of creatures) appears to be what is being described — nevertheless, since there would be no purpose in stating mere cosmogony, it is the fruit of higher knowledge (paravidyā-phala) that is being stated here under the pretext of describing creation. This is the import.

And the words "praśna" (question) and "prativacana" (answer) should also be understood together — for both the question and the answer serve the same purpose of stating that fruit.

docs.text:
ಪರಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಅನ್ವೇಷಮಾಣಾಃ ಇತಿ — the words "seeking the supreme Brahman" · ಉಪಕ್ರಾಂತೇ — having been begun / introduced · ಅಸ್ಮಿನ್ — in this · ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ-ಪ್ರಕರಣೇ — context of Brahman-enquiry · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿ-ಕರ್ತೃಕ — done by Prajāpati · ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ-ವಿಷಯ — concerning the creation of creatures · ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪ್ರತ್ಯುಕ್ತ್ಯೋಃ — of the question and its answer · ಅಸಂಗತಿಂ — incongruity / apparent inconsistency · ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this objection · ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪ್ರತ್ಯುಕ್ತಿ-ರೂಪಾಯಾಃ — which is in the form of question and answer · ಶ್ರುತೇಃ — of the Śruti · ತಾತ್ಪರ್ಯಂ — the real purport / intent · ಆಹ — states · ಅಪರವಿದ್ಯಾ ಇತಿ — with the word "aparavidyā (lower knowledge)" ।

ಇದಂ — this · ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ — is an indicative / also stands for · ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಣಾಂ ಚ — of those who perform ritual action alone · ಇತಿ ಅಪಿ ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಂ — should also be understood ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the fruit of ritual action alone · ಚಂದ್ರಲೋಕಸ್ಯ — of the lunar world · ತದ್ಗತೇಃ — of the path leading to it · ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಸ್ಯ ಚ — and of the Pitṛyāṇa · "ತೇಷಾಂ ಏವ ಏಷ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಲೋಕಃ" — "this Brahmaloka belongs to those very ones" · "ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ" — "those who desire progeny resort to the Southern path" · ಇತಿ — thus · ವಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಾಣತ್ವಾತ್ — because it will be stated · ಇತಿ — thus ।

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ — even though · ಇದಂ ಅಪಿ — this too · ಪರಬ್ರಹ್ಮ-ಜಿಜ್ಞಾಸಾ-ಅವಸರೇ — in the context of enquiry into the supreme Brahman · ಅಸಂಗತಂ ಏವ — is indeed incongruous · ತಥಾಪಿ — even so · ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಾತ್ — from the fruit of ritual action alone · ಸಮುಚ್ಚಿತಕರ್ಮ-ಕಾರ್ಯಾತ್ ಚ — and from the fruit of combined action · ವಿರಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ಏವ — only of one who is dispassionate · ತತ್ρ ಅಧಿಕಾರಃ — the qualification (for Brahman-enquiry) · ಇತಿ — thus · ತತಃ — therefore · ವೈರಾಗ್ಯ-ಅರ್ಥಂ — for the purpose of generating dispassion · ಇದಂ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — this is stated ।

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ — even though · ಮುಖತಃ — on the surface / apparently · ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಃ — creation (of creatures) · ಪ್ರತೀಯತೇ — appears to be what is described · ತಥಾಪಿ — even so · ತದ್-ಉಕ್ತೌ — in stating that (mere cosmogony) · ಪ್ರಯೋಜನ-ಅಭಾವಾತ್ — because of the absence of purpose · ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ-ಉಕ್ತಿ-ವ್ಯಾಜೇನ — under the pretext of describing creation · ಪರವಿದ್ಯಾ-ಫಲಂ ಏವ — the fruit of higher knowledge alone · ಅತ್ρ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — is stated here · ಇತಿ ಭಾವಃ — this is the import ।

ಪ್ರಶ್ನ ಇತಿ — the word "praśna (question)" · ಪ್ರತಿವಚನಂ ಚ ಇತಿ — and "prativacana (answer)" · ಅಪಿ ದ್ರಷ್ಟವ್ಯಂ — should also be understood together · ತಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಏವ — through both of them alone · ತದ್-ಉಕ್ತೇಃ — for the stating of that (fruit) · ಇತಿ — thus ॥

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Kabandhi Kātyāyana poses the first question of the Praśna Upaniṣad — from where are creatures born? ಭಾṣya (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Identifies the time (after one year of discipline); clarifies the scope of "creatures" as Brāhmaṇas and the like; most importantly identifies the real intent of the question as asking about the fruit and destination of aparavidyā-karma-samuccaya ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Resolves the apparent incongruity of a cosmogony question in a Brahman-enquiry context; identifies the two fruits to be described (viraja Brahmaloka for samuccita-karma; lunar world for kevala-karma); states the real purpose is vairāgya (dispassion); confirms that even the creation narrative is a pretext for stating paravidyā-phala

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. The first question of the Praśna Upaniṣad — "from where are creatures born?" — is deceptively simple. Śaṅkara and Ānandagiri together show it carries a much deeper intent.
  2. The real purpose is threefold according to Ānandagiri: (a) to state the fruit and path of the combined knowledge-action path (samuccita — viraja Brahmaloka via Devayāna), (b) to state the fruit and path of ritual action alone (kevala — lunar world via Pitṛyāṇa), and (c) to generate vairāgya (dispassion) towards both, as the qualification for Brahman-enquiry.
  3. Asaṅgati resolved — the apparent incongruity of discussing creation in a Brahman-enquiry context is resolved by Ānandagiri: the creation narrative is a vyāja (pretext). The real content being stated under this pretext is paravidyā-phala — the fruit of higher knowledge.
  4. Vairāgya-artha — dispassion as the purpose — is the key hermeneutical principle Ānandagiri introduces. One who sees both the lunar world and the viraja Brahmaloka as limited fruits will naturally be drawn towards the unlimited — the supreme Brahman. The entire first Praśna serves this purpose.
  5. Both question and answer serve the same purpose — Ānandagiri's closing note that "praśna" and "prativacana" together state the fruit is a structural observation: the entire dialogue (question + answer) is a single Śruti unit aimed at one purpose, not a mere exchange of information.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸ ಹೋವಾಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸ ತಪೋಽತಪ್ಯತ ಸ ತಪಸ್ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ।

ಇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ॥ ೪ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: To him (Katyāyana) the sage replied: Prajāpati, desirous of progeny, performed austerity. Having performed austerity, he produced a pair — Rayi and Prāṇa — (thinking): "These two will produce creatures for me in many ways."

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ತಸ್ಮೈ ಏವಂ ಪೃಷ್ಟವತೇ ಸ ಹ ಉವಾಚ ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯ ಆಹ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಆತ್ಮನಃ ಸಿಸೃಕ್ಷುಃ ವೈ ।

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್ ಜಗತ್ ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ, ಸೃಜ್ಯಮಾನಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ ।

ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತಾರ್ಥವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ, ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ ।

ಅಥ ತು ಸಃ ಏವಂ ತಪಃ ತಪ್ತ್ವಾ ಶ್ರೌತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚ್ಯ, ಸೃಷ್ಟಿಸಾಧನಭೂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತೇ ಮಿಥುನಂ ದ್ವಂದ್ವಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಸೋಮಂ ಅನ್ನಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಅಗ್ನಿಂ ಅತ್ತಾರಮ್ ।

ಇತ್ಯೇತೌ ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮೌ ಅತ್ರ-ಅನ್ನಭೂತೌ ಮೇ ಮಮ ಬಹುಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ ಇತಿ ಏವಂ ಸಂಚಿಂತ್ಯ ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿಕ್ರಮೇಣ ಸೂರ್ಯಾ-ಚಂದ್ರಮಸೌ ಅಕಲ್ಪಯತ್ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
To the one who had asked thus, he (Pippalāda) replied — for the purpose of removing (answering) that (question): Prajāpati was indeed desirous of progeny — desirous of creating creatures from himself.

Prajāpati — being the Self of all, knowing "I shall create the world," performing what was enjoined (jñāna and karma combined), saturated with that very contemplation (of being Prajāpati), arising at the beginning of the kalpa as Hiraṇyagarbha, and being the lord of the creatures — both moving and stationary — that are to be created:

He deliberated upon / performed austerity — the knowledge cultivated through many births, concerned with the meanings revealed by the Śruti — he contemplated, he practised.

Then, having thus performed that austerity — having deliberated upon Vedic knowledge — he produced the pair (mithuna) that is the instrument of creation; he produced the dyad: Rayi — the Soma, the food — and Prāṇa — the Fire, the eater.

Thinking thus — "these two, Agni and Soma, which are the eater and the food, will produce creatures for me in many ways" — he fashioned Sun and Moon in the sequence of the creation of the cosmic egg (aṇḍa).

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya's main sentence describing Prajāpati is the most complex in this verse — a long nominative chain with multiple participials before the finite verb.

Sentence — Prajāpati as Hiraṇyagarbha performing austerity

As written:

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್ ಜಗತ್ ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್ ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಃ ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮಾನಾಂ ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ತಪಃ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಅತಪ್ಯತ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಸಃ] ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — [೧] ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಸನ್, [೨] "ಜಗತ್ ಸ್ರಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ" ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾನವಾನ್, [೩] ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ [ಜ್ಞಾನಕರ್ಮಸಮುಚ್ಚಯಕಾರೀ], [೪] ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತಃ [ಉಪಾಸನಾಕಾಲೀನ-ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿ-ಭಾವನಾ-ಯುಕ್ತಃ], [೫] ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಾತ್ಮನಾ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ, [೬] ಸ್ಥಾವರಜಂಗಮ-ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ — ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಶ್ರೌತ-ಜ್ಞಾನ-ವಿಷಯಂ ತಪಃ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ [ಅಥ] ಅತಪ್ಯತ ।

English: That Prajāpati — [1] being the Self of all, [2] knowing "I shall create the world," [3] performing what was enjoined (combining knowledge and action), [4] saturated with the contemplation of being Prajāpati (during his prior meditation), [5] arisen at the beginning of the kalpa as Hiraṇyagarbha, [6] being the lord of moving and stationary creatures — deliberated upon and performed austerity, which is knowledge cultivated through many births and directed at the meanings revealed by the Śruti.

Note: Six participial/adjectival descriptions accumulate before the two finite verbs (ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ and ಅತಪ್ಯತ). Ānandagiri unpacks each one with a specific technical term — particularly "yathoktakārī" (performing what was enjoined) as jñāna-karma-samuccaya-kārī, and "tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ" as upāsanākālīna-prajāpati- bhāvanā-yuktaḥ.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ತಸ್ಮೈ ಸ ಹೋವಾಚ ಇತಿ ಪ್ರತಿಜ್ಞಾತಂ ವಿಶೇಷತಃ ದರ್ಶಯತಿ – ತದಪಾಕರಣಾಯ ಇತಿ ।

ಆದ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಸನ್ ಇತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಸನ್ ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಯಥೋಕ್ತಕಾರೀ ಇತಿ ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಕರ್ಮಸಮುಚ್ಚಯಕಾರೀ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ತದ್ಭಾವಭಾವಿತ ಇತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿರಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ಇತಿ ಉಪಾಸನಕಾಲೀನ-ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿ-ಭಾವನಾ-ಯುಕ್ತಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಪೂರ್ವಕಲ್ಪೀಯ-ತದ್ಭಾವ-ಭಾವಿತಃ ಏತತ್ಕಲ್ಪಾದೌ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಗರ್ಭಾತ್ಮನಾ ನಿರ್ವೃತ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಸನ್ ಪಶ್ಚಾತ್ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಃ ಸನ್ ತಪಃ ಜನ್ಮಾಂತರಭಾವಿತಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಶ್ರುತಿಪ್ರಕಾಶಿತ-ಅರ್ಥ-ವಿಷಯಂ ಅತಪ್ಯತ ಅನ್ವಾಲೋಚಯತ್ ಚಿಂತಾದಿನಾ ತತ್ಸಂಸ್ಕಾರಂ ಉದ್ಬೋಧ್ಯ ಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ ।

ತತ್ρ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ಆದಿತ್ಯಚಂದ್ರ-ಉತ್ಪಾದನೇನ ತದ್ಭಾವಂ ಆಪದ್ಯ ಪಶ್ಚಾತ್ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ಸಾಧ್ಯ-ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಭಾವಂ ಆಪದ್ಯ ಏವಮೇವ ತದವಯವ-ಅಯನದ್ವಯ-ಮಾಸ-ಪಕ್ಷ-ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಭಾವಂ ಆಪದ್ಯ ತತಃ ತತ್ಸಾಧ್ಯ-ವ್ರೀಹ್ಯಾದ್ಯನ್ನ-ಭಾವಂ ರೇತಃ-ಭಾವಂ ಚ ಆಪದ್ಯ ತೇನ ರೇತಸಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಸೃಜೇಯಂ ಇತ್ಯೇವಂ ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ್ಯ ಪ್ರಥಮಂ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಶಬ್ದಿತ-ಚಂದ್ರ-ಸೂರ್ಯ-ದ್ವಂದ್ವಂ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿತವಾನ್ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ಸ ಏವಂ ಇತಿ ।

ರಯಿಶಬ್ದೇನ ಧನವಾಚಿನಾ ಭೋಜ್ಯಜಾತಂ ಲಕ್ಷಯಿತ್ವಾ ಭೋಜ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಸೋಮಕಿರಣ-ಅಮೃತ-ಯುಕ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ತದ್ದ್ವಾರಾ ಸೋಮಃ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಯತೇ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ರಯಿಂ ಚ ಇತಿ ।

ಏವಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಶಬ್ದೇನ ಅಪಿ ।

"ಅಹಂ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ದೇಹಮಾಶ್ರಿತಃ । ಪ್ರಾಣಾಪಾನಸಮಾಯುಕ್ತಃ ಪಚಾಮ್ಯನ್ನಂ ಚತುರ್ವಿಧಮ್ ॥" [ಭಗವದ್ಗೀತಾ ೧೫।೧೪] ಇತಿ ಸ್ಮೃತೇಃ ಅಗ್ನೇಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಸಂಬಂಧಾತ್ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಭೋಕ್ತಾ ಲಕ್ಷ್ಯತೇ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ಪ್ರಾಣಂ ಚ ಇತಿ ।

ಅಗ್ನೀಷೋಮಯೋಃ ಅಂಡ-ಅಂತರ್ಗತತ್ವೇನ ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ-ಅನಂತರಂ ಉತ್ಪತ್ತಿಃ ಇತ್ಯಾಶಯೇನ ಆಹ – ಅಂಡೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ ಇತಿ ।

"ಉದ್ಯಂತಂ ವಾವ ಆದಿತ್ಯಂ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಅನುಸಮಾರೋಹತಿ" ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತೇಃ ಸೂರ್ಯ-ಅಗ್ನ್ಯೋಃ ಏಕತ್ವಂ ಅಭಿಪ್ರೇತ್ಯ ಅಗ್ನಿಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಪದೇನ ಆಹ – ಸೂರ್ಯ-ಚಂದ್ರಮಸೌ ಇತಿ ॥ ೪ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by noting that what was announced in principle (pratijñāta) in the first verse of the Praśna — Pippalāda will answer the question — is now being shown in detail by Śaṅkara — with the words "tadapākaraṇāya" (for the purpose of removing / answering that question).

On the first occurrence of "san" (being) in the Bhāṣya: Ānandagiri gives the anvaya — it connects to "prajākāmaḥ san" (being desirous of progeny). This clarifies the syntactic flow of Śaṅkara's long sentence.

On "yathoktakārī" (performing what was enjoined): Ānandagiri clarifies this means "performing the combination of knowledge and action" (jñāna-karma-samuccaya-kārī) — i.e., Hiraṇyagarbha is not a mere ritualist nor a mere meditator, but one who combines both.

On "tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ" (saturated with that contemplation): Ānandagiri explains this means "endowed with the meditation on being Prajāpati who is the Self of all — practised during the time of upāsanā (meditation)." Then Ānandagiri provides the full anvaya of this dense passage: Prajāpati — saturated with that Prajāpati- contemplation from the previous kalpa — having arisen at the beginning of this kalpa as Hiraṇyagarbha, and then being desirous of progeny — performed austerity (which is the knowledge cultivated through many births, directed at Śruti-meanings) — by contemplation and reflection, he awakened those saṃskāras (latent impressions) and produced knowledge.

Ānandagiri then provides the complete sequential logic of Prajāpati's plan: first by producing Sun and Moon, then by taking on the nature of the Year (produced through Moon and Sun), then by taking on the natures of the two ayanas, Month, Fortnight, and Day-and-Night (the components of the Year), then by taking on the nature of food (rice etc.) produced through those, and then seed — deciding "I shall create creatures through that seed" — and having resolved this plan, he first produced the Moon-Sun dyad designated as Rayi and Prāṇa. This is stated with the words "sa evam" (he thus).

On "rayiṃ ca" (and Rayi): Ānandagiri explains that the word "rayi" (which means wealth) indicates the class of what is to be enjoyed (bhokhya-jāta); and since what is to be enjoyed is associated with Soma's rays and nectar — through that, Soma (the Moon) is indicated. Similarly with the word "prāṇa."

Citing the Bhagavad Gītā (15.14): "Having become Vaiśvānara, residing in the bodies of living beings, combined with prāṇa and apāna, I digest the fourfold food" — because Fire is connected to Prāṇa through this Smṛti, Fire is indicated as the enjoyer (bhoktā) — with the words "prāṇaṃ ca."

On "aṇḍotpatti" (creation of the cosmic egg): Ānandagiri explains that since Agni and Soma are contained within the cosmic egg, their arising comes after the creation of the egg — this is the intent.

On "sūryacandramasau" (Sun and Moon): Ānandagiri notes that based on the Śruti — "Fire follows the rising Sun" — the identity of Sun and Fire is intended, and therefore Fire is referred to by the word "Sun." This is stated with the words "sūryacandramasau."

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) States that Prajāpati performed austerity and produced the pair — Rayi and Prāṇa — to generate creatures ಭಾṣya (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Identifies Prajāpati with Hiraṇyagarbha; defines tapas as Śruti-directed knowledge cultivated over many births; identifies Rayi = Soma = food and Prāṇa = Fire = eater; describes the sequential plan of creation from Sun-Moon to seed ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Provides the anvaya of the dense Bhāṣya sentence; clarifies yathoktakārī as jñāna-karma-samuccaya; unpacks tadbhāvabhāvita as upāsanā-meditation; gives the full sequential cosmogonic plan; explains rayi and prāṇa as upalakaṣaṇas for Soma and Agni respectively; cites BG 15.14 for Fire-Prāṇa identity; cites Śruti for Sun-Fire identity

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. This verse is the cosmogonic answer to the first Praśna's question — from where are creatures born? Prajāpati creates the Rayi-Prāṇa pair as the first step in a chain that ends with seed and creatures.
  2. Prajāpati = Hiraṇyagarbha — the first-born, the cosmic egg, arising at the beginning of each kalpa. His "austerity" is not physical discipline but the contemplation and reawakening of Śruti-knowledge from previous births.
  3. Yathoktakārī = jñāna-karma-samuccaya — Ānandagiri's gloss confirms that Hiraṇyagarbha is the paradigm of the combined path: both knowledge and action, not one alone.
  4. The sequential cosmogonic plan laid out by Ānandagiri in the Ṭīkā is the clearest single summary of the entire first Praśna's argument: Sun-Moon → Year → ayanas → Month → Fortnight → Day-and-Night → food → seed → creatures.
  5. Rayi and Prāṇa as upalakaṣaṇas — the word "rayi" (wealth) indicates the class of what is enjoyed and thereby points to Soma; the word "prāṇa" through its connection to Fire (BG 15.14) points to Agni. This is Ānandagiri's linguistic precision — the Upaniṣad uses these two terms as indicative labels for the Moon-Sun pair.

docs.text: ಆದಿತ್ಯೋ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣೋ ರಯಿರೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ರಯಿರ್ವಾ ಏತತ್ಸರ್ವಂ ಯನ್ಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚಾಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ತಸ್ಮಾನ್ಮೂರ್ತಿರೇವ ರಯಿಃ ॥ ೫ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Sun (Āditya) is indeed Prāṇa; the Moon (Candra) is indeed Rayi. Rayi is indeed all this — whatever is formed (mūrta) and whatever is formless (amūrta). Therefore the formed (mūrti) alone is Rayi.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ತತ್ರ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಹ ವೈ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ।

ರಯಿಃ ಏವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾಃ ।

ರಯಿಃ ಏವ ಅನ್ನಂ ಸೋಮ ಏವ ।

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಏಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ; ಗುಣಪ್ರಧಾನಕೃತಃ ಭೇದಃ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ರಯಿಃ ವೈ ಅನ್ನಂ ಏವ ಏತತ್ ಸರ್ವಮ್ ।

ಕಿಂ ತತ್ ? ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸ್ಥೂಲಂ ಚ ಅಮೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮಂ ಚ ।

ಮೂರ್ತ-ಅಮೂರ್ತೇ ಅತ್ರ-ಅನ್ನರೂಪೇ ಅಪಿ ರಯಿಃ ಏವ ।

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಭಕ್ತಾತ್ ಅಮೂರ್ತಾತ್ ಯತ್ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತರೂಪಂ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ, ಸಾ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
There, in the matter of the second Praśna — the Sun (Āditya) is indeed Prāṇa, the eater, the fire. The Moon alone is Rayi. Rayi alone is food, and that is the Soma (the Moon) alone.

That this (Prajāpati) is one — being both the eater-fire and the food — is one pair; and the distinction (between eater and food) is made by (one being) primary and (the other being) subordinate in quality (guṇapradhānakṛta).

How (is all this Rayi)? Rayi — food — is indeed all this. What is that? Whatever is formed (gross) and whatever is formless (subtle).

Both the formed and the formless — even in the roles of eater and food — are Rayi alone.

Therefore, distinguished from the formless, whatever is other and of the nature of form — that formed one (mūrti) alone is Rayi (food), because it is being eaten by the formless eater (the formless Prāṇa).

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
Two sentences in this Bhāṣya require explicit anvaya — the central logical statement about guṇapradhāna and the concluding resolution.

Sentence 1 — The one pair and the guṇapradhāna distinction

As written:

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಏಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಮ್ ; ಗುಣಪ್ರಧಾನಕೃತಃ ಭೇದಃ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ [ಅಗ್ನಿ-ಸೋಮ-ರೂಪಂ] ಏಕಂ [ಏವ] — [ಯತ್] ಅತ್ತಾ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚ [ತತ್] ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ [ಏಕ ಏವ] ।

[ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ] ಏಕಂ ತು ಮಿಥುನಂ [ಭವತಿ] ।

[ಅತ್ತಾ-ಅನ್ನಯೋಃ] ಭೇದಃ [ಕೃತಃ —] ಗುಣಪ್ರಧಾನ-ಕೃತಃ [ಕೇವಲಂ] ।

English: That this — of the nature of Fire and Moon — is one: what is both the eater-fire and the food is Prajāpati alone. Prajāpati is one pair. The distinction (between eater and food) is made solely by one being primary (pradhāna) and the other subordinate in quality (guṇa).

Note: The key philosophical point is that the eater (attā) and the food (anna) are not ontologically two — they are one Prajāpati. The distinction is epistemological / functional: one aspect is primary (pradhāna — the eater, Prāṇa, Fire) and the other is subordinate (guṇa — the food, Rayi, Moon). Ānandagiri names this structure explicitly.

Sentence 2 — Why the formed alone is Rayi when both formed and formless are Rayi

As written:

ಮೂರ್ತ-ಅಮೂರ್ತೇ ಅತ್ರ-ಅನ್ನರೂಪೇ ಅಪಿ ರಯಿಃ ಏವ ।

ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಭಕ್ತಾತ್ ಅಮೂರ್ತಾತ್ ಯತ್ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಮೂರ್ತರೂಪಂ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ, ಸಾ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯತಃ] ಮೂರ್ತ-ಅಮೂರ್ತೇ ಉಭೇ ಅಪಿ ಅತ್ರ-ಅನ್ನ-ರೂಪೇ — ರಯಿಃ ಏವ [ಇತಿ ಉಕ್ತಂ] ।

[ಕಿಂ ತು] ಯದಾ ವಿಭಕ್ತ-ದೃಷ್ಟ್ಯಾ — ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ [ಪ್ರಾಧಾನ್ಯೇನ ಅತ್ತಾ] — [ತದಾ] ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ [ಯಾ ಮೂರ್ತ-ರೂಪಂ] ಸಾ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ [ಭವತಿ] — [ಯತಃ] ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಅತ್ತ್ರಾ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನಾ [ಸ್ತಿ] ।

English: In general — both the formed and the formless, even in the roles of eater and food, are Rayi alone. But when they are viewed as distinguished from each other — the formless Prāṇa being primarily the eater — then the formed one (mūrti) alone is Rayi, because it is being eaten by the formless eater.

Note: This resolves the apparent contradiction in the Mūla: "all this — both formed and formless — is Rayi," and yet "the formed alone is Rayi." Śaṅkara explains it as two levels of description — the undivided view (where everything is Rayi) and the distinguished view (where only the formed is Rayi, being eaten by the formless).

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣೌ ಶ್ರುತಿಃ ಸ್ವಯಂ ಏವ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟ ಇತಿ ಆಹ – ತತ್ರ ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಇತಿ ।

ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಏವ ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಆದಿ-ಪ್ರಜಾ-ಪರ್ಯಂತ-ಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಂ ವಕ್ತುಂ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರ-ಸ್ರಷ್ಟ್ರೋಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯ-ಉಪಾದಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮತ್ವಂ ಆಹ – ತದೇತದೇಕಂ ಇತಿ ।

ಕಥಂ ಏಕಸ್ಯ ಅತ್ತಾ ಅನ್ನಂ ಚ ಇತಿ ಭೇದಃ ಇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ತಸ್ಯ ಏವ ಗುಣಭಾವ-ವಿವಕ್ಷಯಾ ಅನ್ನತ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಾಧಾನ್ಯ-ವಿವಕ್ಷಯಾ ಚ ಅತ್ತೃತ್ವಂ ಇತಿ ಭೇದಃ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ಗುಣ ಇತಿ ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮತ್ವಂ ಇತಿ ಶಂಕತೇ — ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ ।

ತತ್ρ ರಯೇಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿತ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ರಯಿಃ ಇತಿ ।

ಅಮೂರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ ವಾಯ್ವಾದೇಃ ಕೇನಚಿತ್ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ರಯಿತ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ನನು ಮೂರ್ತ-ಅಮೂರ್ತಯೋಃ ಅತ್ರ-ಅನ್ನಯೋಃ ಉಭಯೋಃ ಅಪಿ ರಯಿತ್ವೇ ಅನ್ನಂ ಏವ ರಯಿಃ ಇತಿ ಕಥಂ ಉಕ್ತಂ ಇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಮೂರ್ತ-ಅಮೂರ್ತತ್ವ-ವಿಭಾಗಂ ಅಕೃತ್ವಾ ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಗುಣಭಾವ-ಮಾತ್ರ-ವಿವಕ್ಷಯಾ ಸರ್ವಂ ರಯಿಃ ಇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ ।

ಯದಾ ಉಭೇ ವಿಭಜ್ಯ ಗುಣ-ಪ್ರಧಾನ-ಭಾವೇನ ವಿವಕ್ಷ್ಯೇತೇ ತದಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತೇನ ಪ್ರಾಣೇನ ಮೂರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಅದ್ಯಮಾನತ್ವಾತ್ ಮೂರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಏವ ರಯಿತ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಇತಿ ॥ ೫ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by noting that Śaṅkara states the Śruti itself explains Rayi and Prāṇa — with the words "tatra āditya" (there, the Sun).

To establish that Prajāpati alone is the creator from the Year down to creatures, Śaṅkara states the Prajāpati-nature of Rayi and Prāṇa — since the two, who are the creators of the Year, have Prajāpati as their material cause (upādāna). This is done with the words "tad etad ekam" (that this is one).

Ānandagiri then raises and resolves the objection: how can one (Prajāpati) have the distinction of being both eater and food? The answer is: its food-nature is stated with the intent of describing a subordinate aspect (guṇabhāva-vivakṣā), and its eater-nature is stated with the intent of describing the primary aspect (prādhānya-vivakṣā). This is what Śaṅkara means by "guṇa" (subordinate quality).

A further objection is raised: how can Rayi and Prāṇa be of the nature of Prajāpati? — with the word "katham" (how?).

Śaṅkara's answer — that Rayi is Prajāpati because Rayi is the Self of all (sarvātmaka) — is confirmed. The implication is: even the formless — such as air (vāyu) and the like — has the quality of Rayi (food-nature) because it is eaten by something.

Ānandagiri then raises and resolves another objection: if both the formed and the formless (in the roles of eater and food) are Rayi, how was it said that "food alone is Rayi"? The answer: without making the distinction of formed and formless, with the intent of describing everything as having only the subordinate quality (guṇabhāvamātra) of food-nature, all is said to be Rayi.

But when the two are distinguished and described in terms of primary and subordinate — then, because the formed is eaten by the formless Prāṇa, only the formed has the Rayi-nature — with the word "tasmāt" (therefore).

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Identifies Sun as Prāṇa and Moon as Rayi; states all — both formed and formless — is Rayi; then qualifies: the formed alone is Rayi ಭಾṣya (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Shows Sun = Prāṇa = Fire = eater; Moon = Rayi = food = Soma; explains the one Prajāpati as a pair (mithuna) with the distinction made by guṇa-pradhāna; resolves the apparent contradiction between "all is Rayi" and "the formed alone is Rayi" ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Notes the Śruti explains Rayi-Prāṇa itself; explains Prajāpati-upādānatva of Rayi-Prāṇa; resolves the one-but-two objection via guṇabhāva-vivakṣā / prādhānya-vivakṣā; distinguishes two levels of description — undivided (all is Rayi) and divided (formed alone is Rayi)

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Sun = Prāṇa = Fire = eater; Moon = Rayi = food = Soma. This is the foundational identification of the second Praśna, stated here without qualification.
  2. Prajāpati is one pair (ekaṃ mithuna) — the eater and the food are not two separate entities but one Prajāpati viewed from two aspects. The distinction is guṇapradhānakṛta — made by one being primary, the other subordinate.
  3. Two levels of description resolve the apparent contradiction in the Mūla: At the undivided level (guṇabhāvamātra-vivakṣā) — all, both formed and formless, is Rayi. At the divided level (guṇapradhānabhāva-vivakṣā) — only the formed is Rayi, because it is eaten by the formless.
  4. The formless too has Rayi-nature — even air (vāyu) and other formless principles are eaten by something and are therefore Rayi from one perspective. This is Ānandagiri's important clarification on the scope of Rayi.
  5. Prajāpati-upādānatva — Prajāpati is the material cause (upādāna) of Rayi and Prāṇa. Since they are created from Prajāpati and are of the nature of Prajāpati, their being the Prajāpati-natured pair (mithuna) is established.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಅಥಾದಿತ್ಯ ಉದಯನ್ಯತ್ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ತೇನ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ।

ಯದ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ ಯತ್ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ ಯದುದೀಚೀಂ ಯದಧೋ ಯದೂರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಯದಂತರಾ ದಿಶೋ ಯತ್ಸರ್ವಂ, ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ ತೇನ, ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ॥ ೬ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Now, when the Sun (Āditya) rises and enters the Eastern direction — by that, he gathers the prāṇas of the East into his rays.

Whatever he illumines — the South, the West, the North, below, above, the intermediate directions, and everything — by that, he gathers all the prāṇas into his rays.
