docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ತಥಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಯತ್ ಚ ಅದ್ಯಂ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ ಉದಯನ್ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಗೋಚರಮಾಗಚ್ಛನ್ ಯತ್ ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ ಅನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾವಭಾಸರೂಪೇಷು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ ಕರೋತಿ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ತಥೈವ ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ ಯತ್ ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ ಯತ್ ಉದೀಚೀಮ್ ಅಧಃ ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ ಯತ್ ಚ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ ಕೋಣದಿಶಃ ಅವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ ಯತ್ ಚ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ, ತೇನ ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್ಸ್ಥಾನ್ ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Similarly, Prāṇa — even though formless (amūrta) — is the eater, and is everything that exists, and also everything that is eaten.

How? When the Sun (Āditya) rises — ascending, coming within the range of the eye of living beings — whatever Eastern direction he enters and pervades with his own light: by that — by the pervasion of his own Self — he gathers the prāṇas of the East (those who are within all things, those who have become food) into his rays, which are of the nature of the illumination of his own Self, which are pervaded (by him). He places them within himself, making them his own Self — this is the meaning.

Similarly, whatever he enters of the South, West, North, below, above — and the intermediate directions (the corner directions, the sub-directions) — and whatever else, all of it, he illumines: by that — by the pervasion of his own light — he gathers all the prāṇas of all directions into his rays.

docs.text:
ತಥಾ — similarly · ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಅಪಿ — even though formless · ಪ್ರಾಣಃ — Prāṇa · ಅತ್ತಾ — the eater · ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ — everything indeed · ಯತ್ ಚ ಅದ್ಯಂ — and also whatever is eaten ।

ಕಥಮ್ — how? · ಅಥ — now / then · ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ — the Sun · ಉದಯನ್ — rising · ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛನ್ — ascending · ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ — of living beings · ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಗೋಚರಂ — within the range of the eye · ಆಗಚ್ಛನ್ — coming / arriving · ಯತ್ — whatever · ಪ್ರಾಚೀಂ ದಿಶಂ — the Eastern direction · ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ — with his own light · ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ — enters · ವ್ಯಾಪ್ನೋತಿ — pervades · ತೇನ — by that · ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮ-ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ — by the pervasion of his own Self · ಸರ್ವಾಂತಃಸ್ಥಾನ್ — those situated within all things · ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ — the prāṇas / living beings · ಪ್ರಾಚ್ಯಾನ್ — of the East · ಅನ್ನಭೂತಾನ್ — those who have become food · ರಶ್ಮಿಷು — in his rays · ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮ-ಅವಭಾಸ-ರೂಪೇಷು — which are of the nature of the illumination of his own Self · ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಮತ್ಸು — which are pervaded · ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being pervaded · ಪ್ರಾಣಿನಃ — the living beings · ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ — gathers / places · ಸಂನಿವೇಶಯತಿ — causes to be placed · ಆತ್ಮಭೂತಾನ್ ಕರೋತಿ — makes them his own Self · ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ತಥೈವ — similarly · ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ — whatever he enters · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಂ — the South · ಯತ್ ಪ್ರತೀಚೀಂ — whatever the West · ಯತ್ ಉದೀಚೀಂ — whatever the North · ಅಧಃ — below · ಊರ್ಧ್ವಂ — above · ಯತ್ ಪ್ರವಿಶತಿ — whatever he enters · ಯತ್ ಚ ಅಂತರಾ ದಿಶಃ — and whatever the intermediate directions · ಕೋಣದಿಶಃ — the corner directions · ಅವಾಂತರದಿಶಃ — the sub-directions · ಯತ್ ಚ ಅನ್ಯತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ — and whatever else, everything · ಪ್ರಕಾಶಯತಿ — he illumines · ತೇನ — by that · ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶ-ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತ್ಯಾ — by the pervasion of his own light · ಸರ್ವಾನ್ — all · ಸರ್ವದಿಕ್ಸ್ಥಾನ್ — situated in all directions · ಪ್ರಾಣಾನ್ — the prāṇas · ರಶ್ಮಿಷು — in his rays · ಸಂನಿಧತ್ತೇ — gathers ॥

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya opens with a compressed statement and then provides a detailed explanation. The opening sentence requires explicit anvaya.

Sentence — The opening identification of formless Prāṇa as eater and everything

As written:

ತಥಾ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಯತ್ ಚ ಅದ್ಯಂ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಯಥಾ ರಯಿಃ ಸರ್ವಂ ಮೂರ್ತಮ್ ಅದ್ಯಂ ಚ ಉಕ್ತಃ —] ತಥಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಪಿ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಸನ್ — [ಏಕತಃ] ಅತ್ತಾ [ಚ], [ಅನ್ಯತಃ] ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ [ಭವತಿ] — ಯತ್ ಚ ಅದ್ಯಂ [ತತ್ ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣ ಏವ] ।

English: Just as Rayi (the material principle) was said to be everything formed and also what is eaten — similarly Prāṇa too, even though formless, is on one side the eater, and is on the other side everything — and even what is eaten is also Prāṇa.

Note: This sentence resolves the apparent tension in the second Praśna: Prāṇa was said to be the eater (attā), but also said to be everything (sarva). Ānandagiri flags this as the core point of the Bhāṣya — both the eater and the eaten are Prāṇa, because Prāṇa is the Self of all (sarvātmaka). The word "adyam" (what is eaten) is key — Ānandagiri confirms it covers both the gross food and the formless Prāṇa-as-food.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ರಯಿಶಬ್ದಿತಸ್ಯ ಅನ್ನಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿತ್ವಾರ್ಥಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಂ ಉಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ ತದರ್ಥಂ ಏವ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಂ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ಅಥ ಆದಿತ್ಯ ಇತಿ ವಾಕ್ಯೇನ ಇತ್ಯಾಹ – ತಥಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ।

ಯತ್ ಚ ಅದ್ಯಂ ತದಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಪಿ ಸರ್ವಂ ಏವ ಇತಿ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಃ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಸ್ವಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಇತಿ ।

ಸ್ವಕೀಯ-ಪ್ರಕಾಶೇನ ಸ್ವ-ಪ್ರಭಯಾ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಅಂತರ್ಭೂತಾನ್ ಇತಿ ।

ಯದ್ಯಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ ಅತ್ತೃತ್ವಂ ಉಕ್ತಂ ತಥಾಪಿ ರಯಿರ್ವಾ ಏತತ್ ಸರ್ವಂ ಇತ್ಯತ್ರ ಅಮೂರ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ ಗುಣಭಾವ-ವಿವಕ್ಷಯಾ ಅನ್ನತ್ವಂ ಉಕ್ತಂ ಇತಿ ತಥೋಕ್ತಂ ।

ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮ-ಅಭಾವಭಾಸ-ರೂಪೇಷು ಇತಿ ।

ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮ-ಪ್ರಭಾ-ರೂಪೇಷು ರಶ್ಮಿಷು ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ ।

ಸಂಬದ್ಧತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ೬ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by explaining the structural purpose of this verse in the second Praśna: having stated the all-Self-nature (sarvātmatva) of food (called Rayi) for the purpose of establishing its Prajāpati-nature, now the all-Self-nature of Prāṇa is also stated for the same purpose — by the sentence beginning "atha āditya" (now the Sun). This is what Śaṅkara is doing — with the words "tathā" and so on.

On the phrase "yat cādyam" (and what is eaten): Ānandagiri states the implication — even what is eaten is Prāṇa; therefore the eater-Prāṇa is also everything; thus Prāṇa is of the nature of all (sarvātmaka).

On "svaprakāśena" (with his own light): Ānandagiri clarifies this means "with his own radiance, with his own luminosity" — the light that is intrinsic to the Sun, not borrowed from elsewhere.

On "antarbhūtān" (those who are within, absorbed into): Ānandagiri resolves a potential difficulty. Although the quality of being the eater (attṛtva) was stated for Prāṇa, in the statement "rāyirvā etat sarvam" (all this is Rayi) the food-nature (annatva) was stated even for the formless Prāṇa — with the intent of describing it as having a subordinate quality (guṇabhāva-vivakṣayā). Therefore it was described that way (as food/Rayi).

On "svātmāvabhāsarūpeṣu" (rays which are of the nature of the illumination of his own Self): Ānandagiri clarifies this means "in the rays which are of the nature of his own Self's radiance" — the rays are not separate from the Sun but are the very luminosity of the Sun's Self.

On "vyāptatvāt" (because of being pervaded): Ānandagiri glosses this as "sambaddhatvāt" — because of being connected to / associated with (the Sun through his rays).

docs.title: Summary of Mūla, Bhāṣya, and Ṭīkā
docs.text: Text Author Function ಮೂಲ (Mūla) Upaniṣad (Atharva-veda tradition) Describes the Sun entering and illumining all directions and gathering all prāṇas into his rays — a cosmological image of Prāṇa's universal pervasion ಭಾṣya (Bhāṣya) Śaṅkarācārya (8th c. CE) Explains the verse as establishing the sarvātmatva (all-Self-nature) of Prāṇa; shows that even the formless Prāṇa is both the eater and everything that is eaten; interprets rays as the Sun's own Self-luminosity pervading all living beings ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Identifies the structural purpose — parallel to the Rayi's sarvātmatva, now Prāṇa's sarvātmatva is established; explains the subordinate food-nature of Prāṇa (guṇabhāva); clarifies svaprakāśa as intrinsic radiance and vyāptatvāt as sambaddhatva

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Structural parallel: The second Praśna establishes sarvātmatva for both Rayi and Prāṇa. Verse 6 does for Prāṇa what an earlier verse did for Rayi — shows it as the Self of all. Ānandagiri makes this explicit.
  2. Prāṇa is both eater and eaten — the eater (attā) and what is eaten (adyam) are both Prāṇa, because Prāṇa is sarvātmaka (the Self of all). This is the philosophical resolution of the apparent paradox stated at the start of the Bhāṣya.
  3. The rays are the Sun's own Self-luminosity — not external instruments but the very radiance of his Self. When the Sun pervades a direction through his rays, he is making that direction his own Self. ātmasātkurvan (making his own Self) from verse 7 is already anticipated here.
  4. Guṇabhāva-vivakṣā — Ānandagiri introduces this technical term to explain why Prāṇa (the formless) could be described as food (the formed) in an earlier verse. It was stated with the intent of describing a subordinate aspect — not Prāṇa's primary nature but a secondary characterisation for the purpose of the argument.
  5. Vyāptatvāt = sambaddhatvāt — Ānandagiri's gloss simplifies the compound: the prāṇas of living beings are gathered into the rays because they are connected to / pervaded by those rays. The Sun's daily rising is the concrete, observable form of this metaphysical pervasion.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಸ ಏಷ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರೋ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽಗ್ನಿರುದಯತೇ ।

ತದೇತದೃಚಾಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ॥ ೭ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
This very one — the Vaiśvānara, of universal form, Prāṇa, Fire — rises.

And this same matter has been stated (confirmed) by a Ṛc (Vedic verse) as well.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಸಃ ಏಷಃ — this very one / that same one · ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ — the Vaiśvānara (the fire common to all living beings) · ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ — of universal form · ಪ್ರಾಣಃ — Prāṇa (the life-force) · ಅಗ್ನಿಃ — Fire · ಉದಯತೇ — rises ।

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ — that this (matter) · ಋಚಾ — by a Ṛc (Vedic verse) · ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ — has been stated / confirmed ॥

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಸ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಸ ಏವ ಅತ್ತಾ ಉದಯತೇ ಉದ್ಗಚ್ಛತಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ ।

ತದೇತತ್ ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು ಋಚಾ ಮಂತ್ರೇಣ ಅಪಿ ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
This very one — the eater, Prāṇa — is the Vaiśvānara, the Self of all; and of universal form because he is the Self of the universe. And this same one — Prāṇa, Fire, and the eater — rises, ascends, every day, making all directions his own Self.

And this matter that has been stated (the greatness of the Sun / Āditya) has also been confirmed by a Ṛc — by a mantra.

docs.text:

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ — that this · ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು — the matter that has been stated · ಋಚಾ — by a Ṛc · ಮಂತ್ರೇಣ ಅಪಿ — also by a mantra · ಅಭ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ — has been confirmed / further stated ॥

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The key sentence in this Bhāṣya accumulates five predicative identifications of the same subject — requiring explicit anvaya to show they all refer to one entity.

Sentence — The fivefold identification of the rising Prāṇa

As written:

ಸ ಏಷಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅಗ್ನಿಃ ಚ ಸ ಏವ ಅತ್ತಾ ಉದಯತೇ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಸಃ ಏಷಃ [ಏಕ ಏವ ಸ್ವಯಂ] — ಅತ್ತಾ [ಚ], ಪ್ರಾಣಃ [ಚ], ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ [ಚ], ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಾ [ಚ], ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ [ಚ — ವಿಶ್ವಾತ್ಮತ್ವಾತ್], ಅಗ್ನಿಃ [ಚ] — ಸಃ ಏವ ಅತ್ತಾ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಹಂ ಸರ್ವಾ ದಿಶಃ ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ ಉದಯತೇ ।

English: That very one — who is simultaneously the eater, Prāṇa, Vaiśvānara, the Self of all, of universal form (because he is the Self of the universe), and Fire — that very eater rises every day, making all directions his own Self.

Note: Śaṅkara uses "sa evaita" twice — first to introduce the cluster of identifications and then to resume the subject before the finite verb ಉದಯತೇ. The participial ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ (making his own Self) is the key phrase — Ānandagiri's gloss on "pratyakṣatvam" (perceptibility / directness) confirms this rising is the observable, daily manifestation of the one Prāṇa-Fire-Sun.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಕ್ಷತ್ವಮಾಹ – ಸ ಏಷ ಇತಿ ।

ವೈಶ್ವಾನರ ಇತಿ ।

ನರಾ ಜೀವಾ ವಿಶ್ವೇ ಚ ತೇ ನರಾಃ ಚ ವಿಶ್ವಾನರಾಃ ಸ ಏವ ವೈಶ್ವಾನರಃ ಸರ್ವಜೀವಾತ್ಮಕ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಪಂಚಾತ್ಮಕ ಇತಿ ಭೇದಃ ।

ಉಕ್ತಂ ವಸ್ತು ಇತಿ ।

ಆದಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಉಕ್ತಂ ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯಂ ಇತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ॥ ೭ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by noting that Śaṅkara states the perceptibility (pratyakṣatva) of that Prāṇa — with the words "sa eṣa" (this very one). The point is that what has been described philosophically throughout the second Praśna is now directly identified with the observable daily rising of the Sun.

On "vaiśvānara": Ānandagiri gives the etymological derivation. The nāras (living beings / jīvas) are all — they are the viśve nārāḥ (all the living beings); that which belongs to or pervades all the living beings is vaiśvānara. Therefore vaiśvānara means "of the nature of all living beings / the Self of all jīvas."

Ānandagiri then distinguishes vaiśvānara from viśvarūpa: vaiśvānara means the Self of all living beings (sarvajīvātmaka — the jīva aspect), whereas viśvarūpa means the Self of the entire manifest world / all phenomena (sarvaprapañcātmaka — the prapañca / universe aspect). These are two distinct aspects of the same Prāṇa-Sun.

On "uktaṃ vastu" (the matter that has been stated): Ānandagiri clarifies this means the greatness of the Sun (Āditya) that has been described in the preceding verses of the second Praśna — and this greatness is now being further confirmed by a Ṛc (Vedic verse, which follows in verse 8).

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Verse 7 is the pivot between the philosophical analysis of the second Praśna and the Vedic śloka that will confirm it in verse 8. Verse 7 draws the analysis to a perceptible, observable conclusion — the daily rising of the Sun.
  2. The five identifications — attā (eater), prāṇa (life-force), vaiśvānara (Self of all jīvas), viśvarūpa (Self of all phenomena), agni (fire) — are all names of the same one Prāṇa-Sun. Śaṅkara's Bhāṣya gathers them all into a single subject.
  3. ಆತ್ಮಸಾತ್ಕುರ್ವನ್ (ātmasātkurvan) — "making all directions his own Self" — is philosophically the most significant phrase. The Sun's rising is not merely physical motion but the Self asserting its identity with all directions, all space.
  4. Ānandagiri's vaiśvānara / viśvarūpa distinction is precise and important: vaiśvānara = Self of all jīvas (the individual living beings); viśvarūpa = Self of the entire prapañca (the manifest universe as a whole). Both are aspects of the same Prāṇa-Sun — the jīva-aspect and the prapañca-aspect.
  5. The ṛc cited in verse 8 is now announced here — "tadetan ṛcābhyuktam" links verse 7 structurally to verse 8, making the two verses a unit: prose identification followed by Vedic verse confirmation.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿರೇಕಂ ತಪಂತಮ್ ।

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಮುದಯತ್ಯೇಷ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥ ೮ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
All-formed, the golden one, the one who knows all that is born, the supreme refuge, the one light, shining —

With a thousand rays, existing in a hundredfold way — this Sun rises as the Prāṇa of all creatures.

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಸರ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ರಶ್ಮಿವಂತಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಜಾತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾನಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಾಶ್ರಯಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಸರ್ವಪ್ರಾಣಿನಾಂ ಚಕ್ಷುರ್ಭೂತಂ ಏಕಂ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ ತಪಂತಂ ತಾಪಕ್ರಿಯಾಂ ಕುರ್ವಾಣಂ ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ ।

ಕಃ ಅಸೌ ಯಂ ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ ?

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಅನೇಕರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ಅನೇಕಧಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಉದಯತಿ ಏಷಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Those who have known the Sun as their own Self — having known him as: all-formed (of universal form), the golden one (possessed of rays), the omniscient one (jātavedas — who knows all that is born), the supreme refuge (support of all prāṇas), the one light (which has become the eye of all living beings), without a second, and shining (performing the act of heating) — those are the knowers of Brahman.

Who is that one whom they have known?

He who has a thousand rays, who exists in a hundredfold way — in the diversity of all living beings — he is the Prāṇa of all creatures: this Sun rises.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya for this verse requires explicit anvaya treatment because the Mūla is a verse (śloka) in which a series of accusative compounds (in the second case — dvitīyā) cannot be directly connected syntactically to the nominative sentence that follows. Ānandagiri identifies this as the structural problem that necessitates the Bhāṣya's approach.

The grammatical problem — accusatives without a verb

As written in the Mūla:

ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಹರಿಣಂ ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ ಪರಾಯಣಂ ಜ್ಯೋತಿರೇಕಂ ತಪಂತಮ್ [accusatives] ।

ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಉದಯತಿ ಏಷ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ [nominatives + verb] ।

The problem: The words in the first half — viśvarūpam, hariṇam, jātavedasam, parāyaṇam, jyotiḥ ekam, tapantam — are all accusative. But there is no verb in the first half that governs them. The second half states "this Sun rises as the Prāṇa of creatures" — nominatives with a verb. The two halves cannot be directly connected as a single sentence (samānādhikaraṇa anvaya would fail).

Śaṅkara's solution — adhyāhāra (supplying an implied element): Śaṅkara supplies the implied verb and object: "those who have known (vijñātavantaḥ) the Sun as their own Self (svātmānam)" — thereby making the accusatives the object of the supplied verb, and the knowers of Brahman (brahmvidaḥ) the subject.

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

[ಯೇ] ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಸೂರ್ಯಂ [—] ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ, ಹರಿಣಂ, ಜಾತವೇದಸಂ, ಪರಾಯಣಂ, ಜ್ಯೋತಿಃ ಏಕಂ ಅದ್ವಿತೀಯಂ, ತಪಂತಂ [—] ವಿಜ್ಞಾತವಂತಃ, ತೇ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿದಃ ।

ಕಃ ಅಸೌ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ? [ಯಃ] ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಶತಧಾ ಪ್ರಾಣಿಭೇದೇನ ವರ್ತಮಾನಃ — ಏಷಃ ಪ್ರಜಾನಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಸೂರ್ಯಃ ಉದಯತಿ ।

English: Those who have known the Sun as their own Self — (the Sun who is) all-formed, the golden one, the omniscient, the supreme refuge, the one undivided light, the shining one — those are the knowers of Brahman. And who is that Sun? He who has a thousand rays, who exists in a hundredfold way in the diversity of living beings — this Sun, the Prāṇa of all creatures, rises.

Note: The technical term used by Ānandagiri is adhyāhāra — the supply of an implied element not present in the text, which is necessary to make the sentence syntactically complete. The second occurrence of "sūryam" and the supplied "vijñātavantaḥ brahmvidaḥ" are both adhyāhāra. Ānandagiri describes the problem precisely: the dvitīyā-anta (accusative) compounds cannot have samānādhikaraṇa (appositional) connection with the prathamā-anta (nominative) words — hence the vākyabheda (sentence-splitting) and adhyāhāra are the only solution.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text: ವಿಶ್ವರೂಪಂ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಾಂತಾನಾಂ ಸಹಸ್ರರಶ್ಮಿಃ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಪ್ರಥಮಾಂತಾನಾಂ ಸಾಮಾನಾಧಿಕರಣ್ಯೇನ ಅನ್ವಯ-ಅಯೋಗಾತ್ ಅಧ್ಯಾಹಾರಂ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ವಾಕ್ಯಭೇದೇನ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಸ್ವಾತ್ಮಾನಂ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿನಾ ॥ ೮ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: Ānandagiri's Ṭīkā for this verse is a single compact grammatical observation. He identifies the structural problem of the verse precisely: the accusative compounds beginning with "viśvarūpam" (viśvarūpam, hariṇam, jātavedasam, parāyaṇam, jyotiḥ ekam, tapantam) cannot be connected in a samānādhikaraṇa (appositional) relationship with the nominative words beginning with "sahasraraśmiḥ" (sahasraraśmiḥ, śatadhā vartamānaḥ, prāṇaḥ, eṣa sūryaḥ) — because accusatives and nominatives cannot be in apposition. Therefore, Śaṅkara makes an adhyāhāra (supplies an implied element) and explains by splitting the verse into two sentences (vākyabheda) — beginning with "svātmānam" (as their own Self).

CE) Resolves the grammatical problem by adhyāhāra — supplying "vijñātavantaḥ brahmvidaḥ" and "svātmānam" to connect the accusatives; identifies the knowers of Brahman as those who know the Sun as their own Self; glosses each epithet ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā) Ānandagiri (13th c. CE) Identifies the grammatical problem precisely — accusative-nominative apposition is impossible (samānādhikaraṇya anvayāyogāt) — and confirms Śaṅkara's solution of adhyāhāra plus vākyabheda

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. This verse is a śloka — a formal verse in the Upaniṣad serving as scriptural authority for the identification of the Sun as Prāṇa, which is the central teaching of the second Praśna.
  2. The Sun's seven epithets form a cumulative portrait of the Prāṇa-as-Sun: all-formed (universal), golden (luminous), omniscient (jātavedas), supreme refuge, the one undivided light, shining — culminating in the identification of this one with the Prāṇa of all creatures.
  3. "Svātmānam sūryam vijñātavantaḥ" — knowing the Sun as one's own Self — is the liberating knowledge. This echoes the "aham asmi" (I am That) of the first Praśna's Northern path.
  4. The grammatical teaching — adhyāhāra and vākyabheda — is as important as the philosophical teaching here. The method of resolving verses where grammatical connection is impossible is a standard tool of Vedāntic commentary, and Ānandagiri names it precisely.
  5. The verse closes the second Praśna on the same note that the first Praśna closed — the Sun as Prāṇa, the supreme light, the knower's goal.

docs.title: ಮೂಲ (Mūla)
docs.text:
ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ತದಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತೇ ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಲೋಕಮಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ।

ತ ಏವ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇತ ಋಷಯಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿರ್ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text: The Year (Saṃvatsara) is indeed Prajāpati (the Lord of creatures). His two paths are the Southern and the Northern. Those who worship iṣṭa (sacrificial rites) and pūrta (charitable works) as the (sufficient) accomplishment — they win only the lunar world. They indeed return again (to this world). Therefore those seers who desire progeny resort to the Southern path. This very Pitṛyāṇa is Rayi (the material/nourishing principle).

ತತ್ — that · ಯೇ — those who · ಹ ವೈ — truly / indeed · ತತ್ — that (qualifying the action) · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ — sacrificial rites and charitable works · ಕೃತಂ — accomplished / done · ಇತಿ — thus (thinking) · ಉಪಾಸತೇ — they worship · ತೇ — they · ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಂ ಏವ — only the lunar · ಲೋಕಂ — world / realm · ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ — win / attain ।

docs.title: ಭಾಷ್ಯ (Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿರನ್ನಮಮೂರ್ತಿಶ್ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣೋಽತ್ತಾದಿತ್ಯಸ್ತದೇತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತಿ, ಉಚ್ಯತೇ — ತದೇವ ಕಾಲಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರೋ ವೈ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ, ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರಸಮುದಾಯೋ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದ್ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣೈತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವೇತ್ಯುಚ್ಯತೇ ।

ತತ್ಕಥಮ್ ? ತಸ್ಯ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇಃ ಅಯನೇ ಮಾರ್ಗೌ ದ್ವೌ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ಚೋತ್ತರಂ ಚ ।

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹ್ಯಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನೋತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧತ್ ।

ಕಥಮ್ ? ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಚ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಾದಿಷು ಯೇ ಹ ವೈ ಋಷಯಃ ತದುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ।

ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಣೋ ದ್ವಿತೀಯಸ್ತಚ್ಛಬ್ದಃ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಪೂರ್ತಂ ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ನಾಕೃತಂ ನಿತ್ಯಮ್, ತೇ ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಮೇವ ಚಂದ್ರಮಸಿ ಭವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತೇರ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕಸ್ಯಾಂಶಂ ರಯಿಮನ್ನಭೂತಂ ಲೋಕಮ್ ಅಭಿಜಯಂತೇ ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಂದ್ರಮಸಸ್ಯ ।

ತೇ ಏವ ಚ ಕೃತಕ್ಷಯಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಂತೇ ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಂ ಹೀನತರಂ ವಾ ವಿಶಂತೀತಿ ಹ್ಯುಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಯಸ್ಮಾದೇವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಮನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನಾಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸ್ವಕೃತಮೇವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

ಏಷ ಹ ವೈ ರಯಿಃ ಅನ್ನಮ್, ಯಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣಃ ಪಿತೃಯಾಣೋಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಶ್ಚಂದ್ರಃ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
[Opening question — pūrvapakṣa:] The Moon is what has form (mūrti); food is matter; the formless (amūrti) is Prāṇa; and the Sun is the eater — how can this one pair generate all progeny?

[Answer:] It is said thus: That very Kāla (Time) is the Saṃvatsara, and the Saṃvatsara is indeed Prajāpati — because everything is produced out of it. For the Year is nothing but the aggregate of tithis (lunar days), days, and nights, produced by Moon and Sun together. Since the Year is non-different from the dyad of Rayi and Prāṇa, it is said to be of the very nature of that pair (mithunātmaka).

How so? Prajāpati the Year has two paths — the Southern and the Northern. These are the well-known solstices (ayanas), each characterised by six months, by which the Sun (Savitṛ) travels southward and northward, distributing worlds respectively to those who perform only ritual action (kevalakarmins) and to those who combine knowledge with action (jñānasaṃyuktakarmavants).

How exactly? Among Brāhmaṇas and others — those seers who worship the iṣṭāpūrta as accomplished. The second occurrence of the word "tat" here serves as an adjective qualifying the action. Iṣṭa is sacrificial rite; pūrta is charitable work (and so on); they worship only what has been done (kṛtam) — not what is eternal and unconditioned (nitya). They win only the cāndramasa (lunar) world — the Rayi portion, the food-natured, material aspect of Prajāpati's dyadic nature, which exists in the Moon — because the lunar world has the character of the accomplished (kṛtarūpa).

They indeed return again when their accumulated merit is exhausted — entering this world or a still lower one, as has been stated. Because those seers — householders and perceivers of heaven — desire progeny and produce Prajāpati in his food-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable rites, they resort to the Southern path signified by the Southern solstice, which is nothing but the result of their own deeds. This Pitṛyāṇa is verily Rayi — food/matter. The Moon, characterised by the Pitṛyāṇa path, is that Rayi.

docs.title: Anvaya (Prose Order of the Bhāṣya)
docs.text:
The Bhāṣya contains four sentences whose word-order is sufficiently compressed or inverted that the syntactic structure needs to be laid out explicitly. These are the four that Ānandagiri himself flags with "ಇತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ."

Sentence 1 — The pūrvapakṣa (opening question)

As written:

ಯಃ ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಅನ್ನಂ ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಅತ್ತಾ ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ — ತತ್ ಏತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ — ಕಥಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಯಃ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಅಸೌ [ಸಃ] ಮೂರ್ತಿಃ [ರಯಿಃ] ; ಅನ್ನಂ [ಅಪಿ ರಯಿಃ ಏವ] ।

ಯಃ ಚ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ [ಸಃ] ಅಮೂರ್ತಿಃ ; ಆದಿತ್ಯಃ [ಅಪಿ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ ಏವ,] ಅತ್ತಾ [ಚ] ।

ತತ್ ಏತತ್ [ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣರೂಪಂ] ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಅಸ್ತಿ] ।

[ಏತತ್ ಮಿಥುನಂ] ಕಥಂ [ಸರ್ವಾಃ] ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಿ [ಇತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಃ] ?

English: That Moon is the formed one (Rayi); food too is Rayi. That Prāṇa is the formless one; the Sun too is Prāṇa, and is the eater. That one pair — of the nature of Rayi and Prāṇa — is all, is everything. [Question:] How will this pair generate all progeny?

Sentence 2 — The Year produces through tithis and ahorātras

As written:

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ ಹಿ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ।

ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಏತನ್ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ [ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಹಿ [ಕಃ ?] ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥಿ-ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ [ಏವ] ।

[ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣ-ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ [ಅನನ್ಯಃ] — ತದ್-ಅನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — [ಅತಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ] ಮಿಥುನಾತ್ಮಕ ಏವ ಇತಿ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ।

English: For what is the Year? It is the aggregate of the tithis produced by the Moon and the ahorātras (days-and-nights) produced by the Sun. Since the Year is non-different from the Rayi-Prāṇa pair — because of that non-difference — the Year is said to be of the very nature of that pair.

Note: The compound ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ತಿಥ್ಯಹೋರಾತ್ರ-ಸಮುದಾಯಃ hides the internal division that Ānandagiri makes explicit: tithis are produced by the Moon, ahorātras by the Sun — not both by both.

Sentence 3 — The Sun's two movements and the worlds allotted (the most complex sentence)

As written:

ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇ ಹಿ ಅಯನೇ ಷಣ್ಮಾಸ-ಲಕ್ಷಣೇ, ಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಚ ಯಾತಿ ಸವಿತಾ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಚ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order — two separate syntactic streams):

[Stream 1 — Southern path:] ಸವಿತಾ [ಚಂದ್ರಃ ಅಪಿ — ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಾತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

[Stream 2 — Northern path:] [ಸ ಏವ ಸವಿತಾ] ಉತ್ತರೇಣ [ಅಯನೇನ] ಯಾತಿ ಜ್ಞಾನಸಂಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ ।

English: Stream 1: The Sun (and the Moon too, by upalakaṣaṇa) travels by the Southern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who perform only ritual action.

Stream 2: That same Sun travels by the Northern solstice-path while distributing worlds to those who combine knowledge with action.

Note: The original text runs both streams together in one participial construction (ವಿದಧತ್ governing both objects). Ānandagiri's anvaya splits them explicitly and also adds that ಸವಿತಾ is an upalakaṣaṇa — it denotes the Moon as well, since the Moon too moves along these paths generating tithis.

Sentence 4 — The final statement on householder-seers and the Southern path

As written:

ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಏವಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ, ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ಚಂದ್ರಂ ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

Anvaya (resolved prose order):

ಏತೇ ಋಷಯಃ — ಪ್ರಜಾಕಾಮಾಃ, ಪ್ರಜಾರ್ಥಿನಃ, ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ರಷ್ಟಾರಃ, ಗೃಹಸ್ಥಾಃ — ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತ-ಕರ್ಮಣಾ [ಮಾಧ್ಯಮೇನ] ಅನ್ನಾತ್ಮಕಂ [ಚ] ಚಂದ್ರರೂಪಂ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಂ ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ [ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್] — ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ [ತೇ] ಸ್ವಕೃತಂ ಏವ [ಯತ್] ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನ-ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಿತಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಂ [ಚಂದ್ರಂ] ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ ।

English: Because these seers — desirous of progeny, seekers of offspring, perceivers of heaven, householders — bring about Prajāpati in his food-natured Moon-form as their fruit through sacrificial and charitable action, therefore they resort to nothing but their own deed, which is the Southern path — the Moon indicated by the Southern solstice.

Note: The accumulation of four appositive epithets for ಋಷಯಃ and the placement of ಯಸ್ಮಾತ್…ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ across the sentence boundary makes this the densest construction in the Bhāṣya on this verse. The anvaya clarifies that ಫಲತ್ವೇನ ಅಭಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತಯಂತಿ and ಪ್ರತಿಪದ್ಯಂತೇ are the two main verbs, and that ಚಂದ್ರಂ is to be supplied in the concluding clause from context.

docs.title: ಟೀಕಾ (Ṭīkā)
docs.text:
ಸ ಮಿಥುನಮುತ್ಪಾದಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಪಕ್ರಾಂತಂ ಮಿಥುನಮುಪಸಂಹರತಿ – ಯಶ್ಚಾಸಾವಿತಿ ।

ಯಶ್ಚಾಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ ಯಶ್ಚಾಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಸ್ತದೇಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಮಿತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಏತೌ ಮೇ ಬಹುಧಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಃ ಕರಿಷ್ಯತ ಇತ್ಯುಕ್ತಂ ತತ್ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಕಾರೇಣೇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಪ್ರಜಾಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಉಚ್ಯತ ಇತಿ ।

ತದೇವ ಮಿಥುನಮೇವ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ ಕಾಲಃ ।

ಸ ಚ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕಮಿಥುನನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ತದುಪಪಾದಯತಿ – ಚಂದ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾಸ್ತಿಥಯ ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾನ್ಯಹೋತ್ರಾಣೀತಿ ವಿಭಾಗಃ ।

ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇಽಪಿ ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ ಕಥಂ ತದಾತ್ಮಕತೇತ್ಯಾಶಂಕ್ಯ ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣಯೋರಭೇದಾದಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ನ ಕೇವಲಂ ತಿಥ್ಯಾದಿದ್ವಾರಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಕಿಂ ತ್ವಯನದ್ವಯದ್ವಾರಾಽಪೀತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಯನೇ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯಂ ತತ್ಪ್ರಶ್ನಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ತತ್ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಕುತೋ ಹೇತ್ವಂತರಾದಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಯಾತಿ ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿದಧದುತ್ತರೇಣ ಯಾತೀತ್ಯನ್ವಯಃ ।

ಸವಿತೇತ್ಯುಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ।

ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠಾದಿರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷಾದಿರುತ್ತರಾಯಣಮಿತಿ ಶ್ರುತಿಷು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ ತತಶ್ಚ ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ವಿಧಾತುಂ ತಯೋರ್ದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಗಮನಾತ್ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಾಯನದ್ವಯಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಸ್ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ತಯೋರಯನಯೋರಿತಿ ತದ್ದ್ವಾರಾ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಮಿತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಯೋಃ ಕಥಂ ಲೋಕವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ – ಕಥಮಿತಿ ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯದಕ್ಷಿಣೋತ್ತರಾಯಣದ್ವಾರಾ ಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇಃ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲೋಕಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾಚ್ಚ ತಯೋಸ್ತದ್ವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಮಿತಿ ತದ್ಯೇ ಹ ವಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿವಾಕ್ಯೇನ ಪರಿಹರತಿ – ತತ್ತತ್ರೇತಿ ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚೇತಿ ।

ಅಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ ತಪಃ ಸತ್ಯಂ ವೇದಾನಾಂ ಚಾನುಪಾಲನಮ್ ।

ಆತಿಥ್ಯಂ ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಶ್ಚ ಇಷ್ಟಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ವಾಪೀಕೂಪತಡಾಗಾದಿ ದೇವತಾಯತನಾನಿ ಚ ।

ಅನ್ನಪ್ರದಾನಮಾರಾಮಃ ಪೂರ್ತಮಿತ್ಯಭಿಧೀಯತೇ ॥

ಇತಿ ತಯೋರ್ಭೇದಃ ।

ಕೃತಮಿತ್ಯುಪಾಸತ ಇತಿ ಕೃತಶಬ್ದೋಪರಿತನಮಿತಿಶಬ್ದಮಿಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತಿ ಪೂರ್ತಶಬ್ದೋಪರ್ಯಾಕೃಷ್ಯಾಽಽದಿಶಬ್ದಪರ್ಯಾಯತಯಾ ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ – ಇತ್ಯಾದೀತಿ ।

ದತ್ತಮಾದಿಶಬ್ದಾರ್ಥಃ ।

ಕೃತಮೇವೋಪಾಸತೇ ಕಾರ್ಯಮೇವಾನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತೀತ್ಯರ್ಥಃ ।

ಇದಂ ಚ ವಿಶೇಷಣಂ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಹೇತುತಯೋಕ್ತಮ್ ।

ಕೃತರೂಪೇಷ್ಟ್ಯಾದಿಜನ್ಯತ್ವಾಚ್ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯಾಪಿ ಕೃತತ್ವೇನಾನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿರಿತ್ಯಾಹ – ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾದಿತಿ ।

ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ ಮಂತ್ರವಾಕ್ಯಂ ಪ್ರಮಾಣಯತಿ – ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಮಿತಿ ॥ ೯ ॥

docs.title: Overall Translation
docs.text:
Ānandagiri opens by locating this Bhāṣya passage within its context: Prajāpati was said to produce a pair (mithuna), and Śaṅkara now brings that pair to conclusion with the words "yaścāsau" (that which is the Moon). The syntax (anvaya) is: "That Moon which has form, and that Prāṇa which is formless — these two together are one pair that is everything (sarvātmaka)." It was said that "these two will produce many progeny for me" — and now the question "how?" arises.

Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's answer shows how Rayi and Prāṇa, through the medium of the Saṃvatsara (Year) and related structures, become creators of progeny. That very pair (mithuna) is the Saṃvatsara — Time itself — and that Saṃvatsara is Prajāpati, because the Saṃvatsara is produced out of (nirvartyate) the pair that is of the nature of Prajāpati. Ānandagiri then unpacks the sub-point (tannirvartyatvāt): tithis (lunar days) are produced by the Moon; days and nights (ahorātras) are produced by the Sun — this is the division. Yet even though Time is produced by them, how can Time be identical to them? Ānandagiri answers by citing the principle of non-difference between cause and effect (kāryakāraṇayoḥ abhedāt) — hence "non-difference from that" (tadananyatvāt).

Ānandagiri then clarifies that it is not only through tithis etc. that the Year is produced by Moon and Sun, but also through the two ayanas (solstices) — and this is the purpose of the sub-question "tat katham?" (how so?). The real question is: from what other reason does the Year come to be produced by Moon and Sun? The correct syntactic connection (anvaya) of Śaṅkara's sentence is: the Sun travels by the Southern path while distributing worlds for those who perform only ritual action; it travels by the Northern path while distributing worlds for those who combine knowledge with action. And the word "Savitṛ" (Sun) here is an upalakaṣaṇa (indicative term) — it also implies the Moon. The Southern solstice begins with Jyeṣṭha (month), and the Northern with Mārgaśīrṣa — this is the accepted Vedic teaching. Since the two solstices are established because of the Sun (and Moon) moving along those Southern and Northern paths for the purpose of distributing worlds to the performers of action, the two ayanas are produced by them, and through the ayanas the Year too is produced by them.

To the further question "how are Moon and Sun distributors of worlds?", Ānandagiri explains: because the worlds are attained through the Southern and Northern ayanas produced by Moon and Sun, and because the worlds thus attained are themselves of the nature of Moon and Sun — therefore those two are the distributors of worlds. This is resolved by Śaṅkara's statement beginning "tad ye ha vā…" — which Ānandagiri glosses as "tat tatra."

On the definition of iṣṭa and pūrta, Ānandagiri quotes the traditional two-verse definition:

Iṣṭa is: Agnihotra, austerity (tapas), truth (satya), observance of the Vedas, hospitality (ātithya), and Vaiśvadeva rite.

Pūrta is: the digging of step-wells, wells, and tanks; construction of temples; gift of food; and planting of gardens.

On the word "kṛtam" (accomplished) — Ānandagiri explains that Śaṅkara's "iti" after "kṛtam" draws in and covers "iṣṭāpūrte" as well as "pūrta," and the word "ādi" (etc.) stands for "datta" (what is given/donated). The meaning is: they worship and carry out only what is accomplished/conditioned — only kārya (the produced, finite). This qualifier (viśeṣaṇa) is stated as the reason for their return. Finally, Ānandagiri explains "kṛtarūpatvāt": because the lunar world itself is born from conditioned acts like iṣṭi etc., it too has the character of the kṛta (the accomplished, the finite) and is therefore impermanent — hence rebirth. The Vedic statement "imaṃ lokam" is cited as the scriptural proof (māna) for this return.

docs.title: Word-to-Word
docs.text:
ಸ — he (Prajāpati) · ಮಿಥುನಂ — the pair / dyad · ಉತ್ಪಾದಯತಿ — produces / generates · ಇತಿ — thus · ಉಪಕ್ರಾಂತಂ — what was introduced / begun earlier · ಮಿಥುನಂ — the pair · ಉಪಸಂಹರತಿ — brings to conclusion / summarises · ಯಶ್ಚಾಸಾವಿತಿ — with the words "that which is the Moon" ।

ಯಃ ಚ ಅಸೌ ಚಂದ್ರಮಾ — and that which is the Moon · ಯಃ ಚ ಅಮೂರ್ತಃ ಪ್ರಾಣಃ — and that which is the formless Prāṇa · ತತ್ ಏಕಂ ಮಿಥುನಂ — that one pair / dyad · ಸರ್ವಂ — all · ಸರ್ವಾತ್ಮಕಂ — all-comprising / totality · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಏತೌ — these two · ಮೇ — for me · ಬಹುಧಾ — in many ways · ಪ್ರಜಾಃ — progeny · ಕರಿಷ್ಯತಃ — will produce · ಇತಿ ಉಕ್ತಂ — thus it was said · ತತ್ — that · ಕೇನ ಪ್ರಕಾರೇಣ — by what means / in what way · ಇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ — thus (Śaṅkara) raises the question · ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "how" ।

ರಯಿಪ್ರಾಣಯೋಃ — of Rayi and Prāṇa · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಾದಿ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the medium of the Year etc. · ಪ್ರಜಾಸ್ರಷ್ಟೃತ್ವಂ — the quality of being creators of progeny · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ಉಚ್ಯತೇ ಇತಿ — with the word "it is said" ।

ತತ್ ಏವ ಮಿಥುನಂ ಏವ — that very pair itself · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಃ — is the Year · ಕಾಲಃ — Time ।

ಸ ಚ — and that · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತಿಃ — is Prajāpati · ಪ್ರಜಾಪತ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ-ಮಿಥುನ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because it is produced from the pair that is of the nature of Prajāpati · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of being produced from it" ।

ತತ್ — this · ಉಪಪಾದಯತಿ — (Śaṅkara) establishes / proves · ಚಂದ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the word "Moon" ।

ಚಂದ್ರನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾಃ — produced by the Moon · ತಿಥಯಃ — the tithis (lunar days) · ಆದಿತ್ಯನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯಾನಿ — produced by the Sun · ಅಹೋರಾತ್ರಾಣಿ — the days-and-nights · ಇತಿ ವಿಭಾಗಃ — thus is the division / distinction ।

ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವೇ ಅಪಿ — even though produced by them · ಕಾಲಸ್ಯ — of Time · ಕಥಂ — how · ತದಾತ್ಮಕತಾ — identity with them / being of their nature · ಇತಿ ಆಶಂಕ್ಯ — anticipating this doubt · ಕಾರ್ಯಕಾರಣಯೋಃ ಅಭೇದಾತ್ — because of the non-difference of cause and effect · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ತದನನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of non-difference from that" ।

ನ ಕೇವಲಂ — not only · ತಿಥ್ಯಾದಿ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the medium of tithis etc. · ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by Moon etc. · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ — of the Year · ಕಿಂ ತು — but also · ಅಯನದ್ವಯ-ದ್ವಾರಾ ಅಪಿ — through the medium of the two solstices as well · ಇತಿ ವಕ್ತುಂ — in order to say this · ತಸ್ಯ ಅಯನೇ ಇತಿ ಆದಿ ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the sentence beginning "his two paths" · ತತ್-ಪ್ರಶ್ನ-ಪೂರ್ವಕಂ — preceded by that question · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ತತ್ ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the words "how so?" ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by Moon and Sun · ಕುತಃ — from what · ಹೇತ್ವಂತರಾತ್ — from another / additional reason · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಕೇವಲಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ — of those who perform only ritual action · ಲೋಕಾನ್ — worlds · ವಿದಧತ್ — while distributing · ದಕ್ಷಿಣೇನ ಯಾತಿ — travels by the Southern (path) ।

ಜ್ಞಾನಯುಕ್ತಕರ್ಮವತಾಂ — of those who combine knowledge with action · ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿದಧತ್ — while distributing worlds · ಉತ್ತರೇಣ ಯಾತಿ — travels by the Northern · ಇತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಃ — thus is the syntactic connection ।

ಸವಿತಾ ಇತಿ — the word "Savitṛ (Sun)" · ಉಪಲಕ್ಷಣಂ — is an indicative term (standing for a wider class) · ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — for the Moon as well ।

ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠ-ಆದಿಃ — beginning with Jyeṣṭha (month) · ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನಂ — the Southern solstice · ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷ-ಆದಿಃ — beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa (month) · ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣಂ — the Northern solstice · ಇತಿ ಶ್ರುತಿಷು ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ — as established in the Vedic texts · ತತಃ ಚ — and therefore · ಕರ್ಮಿಣಾಂ ಲೋಕಾನ್ ವಿಧಾತುಂ — in order to distribute worlds to the performers of action · ತಯೋಃ — of those two (Moon and Sun) · ದಕ್ಷಿಣ-ಉತ್ತರಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಮಾರ್ಗಾಭ್ಯಾಂ — by the Southern and Northern paths · ಗಮನಾತ್ — because of the movement / travel · ತನ್ನಿಮಿತ್ತತ್ವಾತ್ — because they are the cause of it · ಅಯನದ್ವಯ-ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧೇಃ — because the two solstices are well established · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by them · ತಯೋಃ ಅಯನಯೋಃ — of those two solstices · ಇತಿ — thus · ತದ್-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through them (the solstices) · ಸಂವತ್ಸರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — of the Year as well · ತನ್ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯತ್ವಂ — being produced by them · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯಯೋಃ — of Moon and Sun · ಕಥಂ — how · ಲೋಕವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಂ — the quality of being distributors of worlds · ಇತಿ ಪೃಚ್ಛತಿ — thus (Ānandagiri) asks · ಕಥಂ ಇತಿ — with the word "how?" ।

ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ನಿರ್ವರ್ತ್ಯ-ದಕ್ಷಿಣ-ಉತ್ತರ-ಅಯನ-ದ್ವಾರಾ — through the Southern and Northern solstices produced by Moon and Sun · ಲೋಕಪ್ರಾಪ್ತೇಃ — because of the attainment of worlds · ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಲೋಕಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — and because the world to be attained also · ಚಂದ್ರಾದಿತ್ಯ-ಆತ್ಮಕತ್ವಾತ್ — because of being of the nature of Moon and Sun · ತಯೋಃ — of those two · ತದ್-ವಿಧಾಯಕತ್ವಂ — their quality of being distributors of those worlds · ಇತಿ — thus · ತದ್-ಯೇ ಹ ವಾ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ-ವಾಕ್ಯೇನ — by the sentence beginning "tad ye ha vā" · ಪರಿಹರತಿ — (Śaṅkara) resolves / answers · ತತ್ ತತ್ರ ಇತಿ — with the words "tat tatra" ।

ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಚ ಇತಿ — and with the words "iṣṭa and" ।

ಅಗ್ನಿಹೋತ್ರಂ — the Agnihotra rite (daily fire offering) · ತಪಃ — austerity · ಸತ್ಯಂ — truth · ವೇದಾನಾಂ ಅನುಪಾಲನಂ — observance of the Vedas · ಆತಿಥ್ಯಂ — hospitality · ವೈಶ್ವದೇವಃ — the Vaiśvadeva rite (offering to all gods) · ಚ — and · ಇಷ್ಟಂ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಧೀಯತೇ — is called Iṣṭa ॥

ವಾಪೀ-ಕೂಪ-ತಡಾಗ-ಆದಿ — step-wells, wells, tanks, etc. · ದೇವತಾಯತನಾನಿ — temples / shrines · ಅನ್ನಪ್ರದಾನಂ — gift of food · ಆರಾಮಃ — garden / park · ಚ — and · ಪೂರ್ತಂ ಇತಿ ಅಭಿಧೀಯತೇ — is called Pūrta ॥

ಇತಿ ತಯೋಃ ಭೇದಃ — thus is the distinction between the two ।

ಕೃತಂ ಇತಿ ಉಪಾಸತೇ ಇತಿ — the phrase "they worship (it as) accomplished" · ಕೃತ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಉಪರಿತನ-ಇತಿ-ಶಬ್ದಂ — the word "iti" placed after the word "kṛta" · ಇಷ್ಟಾಪೂರ್ತೇ ಇತಿ — the compound "iṣṭāpūrte" · ಪೂರ್ತ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಉಪರಿ — over the word "pūrta" · ಆಕೃಷ್ಯ — drawing / pulling (the iti) · ಆದಿ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಪರ್ಯಾಯತಯಾ — as a synonym for the word "ādi" (etc.) · ವ್ಯಾಚಷ್ಟೇ — (Śaṅkara) explains · ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಇತಿ — with the word "and so on" ।

ದತ್ತಂ — what is given / donated · ಆದಿ-ಶಬ್ದ-ಅರ್ಥಃ — is the meaning of the word "ādi" ।

ಕೃತಂ ಏವ ಉಪಾಸತೇ — they worship only what is accomplished / conditioned · ಕಾರ್ಯಂ ಏವ ಅನುತಿಷ್ಠಂತಿ — they carry out only what is produced / finite · ಇತಿ ಅರ್ಥಃ — this is the meaning ।

ಇದಂ ಚ ವಿಶೇಷಣಂ — and this qualifier / adjective · ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ — for the return / rebirth · ಹೇತುತಯಾ — as the reason · ಉಕ್ತಂ — is stated ।

ಕೃತರೂಪ-ಇಷ್ಟ್ಯಾದಿ-ಜನ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because (the Moon) is born from conditioned acts like iṣṭi etc. · ಚಂದ್ರಸ್ಯ ಅಪಿ — even of the Moon · ಕೃತತ್ವೇನ — because of having the nature of the accomplished / conditioned · ಅನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಾತ್ — because of impermanence · ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿಃ — there is return / rebirth · ಇತಿ ಆಹ — thus (Śaṅkara) states · ಕೃತರೂಪತ್ವಾತ್ ಇತಿ — with the words "because of having the character of the accomplished" ।

ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತೌ — for (establishing) the return / rebirth · ಮಂತ್ರ-ವಾಕ್ಯಂ — the Vedic statement / scriptural sentence · ಪ್ರಮಾಣಯತಿ — (Śaṅkara) cites as proof / establishes with scriptural authority · ಇಮಂ ಲೋಕಂ ಇತಿ — with the words "this world" ॥

docs.title: Core Philosophical Thread
docs.text:
1. Rayi and Prāṇa (Moon/matter and Sun/life-force) are the primordial pair.
  2. The Year (Saṃvatsara) is non-different from this pair — it is produced by them through tithis, ahorātras, and the two ayanas, and cause-effect non-difference makes it identical with them.
  3. The two paths after death follow from this structure: the Southern (Pitṛyāṇa) leads to the lunar world — a finite, conditioned realm of Rayi — and return; the Northern (Devayāna) leads beyond.
  4. Iṣṭa-pūrta worshippers, treating conditioned deeds as the final end, attain only the conditioned lunar world and cycle back.
  5. Ānandagiri's contribution is to sharpen the logical spine: the identity of Time with the Rayi-Prāṇa pair rests on the Vedāntic principle of kāryakāraṇa-abheda (non-difference of effect from cause), and "Savitṛ" in the Bhāṣya functions as an upalakaṣaṇa that includes the Moon as well.
